title: Director of Special Assets Group
description:
IN0534 Fishers, OH0523 Independence Bus Office, OH0713 NW Bancshares HQ, PA0258 Bellevue, PA0736 Administration Center

Job Description

The Director of Special Assets Group is responsible to oversee the day-to-be tasks and performance of the commercial Special Assets Group (SAG). The position will monitor the SAG workout officers and their daily duties of working out any and all commercial loans, including SBA, small business, CRE, C&I, Corporate Finance, Middle Market, Equipment Finance, Sports Finance, Franchise Lending. The Director will oversee any and all audit and compliance tasks for SAG. The Director will oversee quarterly reporting of all SAG Criticized and Classified Loans. The Director will oversee all-appraisals ordered by SAG. The Director will also oversee any special projects set by the Executive Director of Loss Mitigation.

Essential Functions
• Ensure total document and data integrity
• Maximize technology tools available
• Support Northwest’s credit culture that stresses Asset Quality before Profitability and Growth
• Establish excellent work relationships with lenders with the common interest in mitigating credit losses
• Promote Northwest’s Mission, Vision, and Values statements
• Remain compliant with all rules and regulations related to loan workouts and collections
• Establish meaningful performance metrics to track improvement in effectiveness and efficiency
• Assist the Credit Administration Department in all matters relating to maintain the credit quality of the loan portfolio, and loan officers in the identification of problem credits
• Advise on loan and credit risk policy by making recommendations as appropriate
• Administer and review exist credits assigned to Loss Mitigation to ensure compliance with loan approval documentation
• Actively participate on the Criticized Asset Committee
• Mitigate losses in the Special Asset loan portfolio
• Recommend restructuring of problem loans with the objective of improving collateral position, mitigating credit losses and minimizing collection expenses
• Work closely with loan recovery staff to recover previously charged-off loans.
• Recommend and/or execute the sale of troubled loans in lieu of further collection if cost-effective.
• Employ legal expertise when appropriate to mitigate losses and potential lender liability claims.
• Identify and consider all potential workout strategies before making the decision/recommendation to charge-off
• Oversee SBA Collections and stay up-to-date with latest SBA policies and procedures.
• Manage the annual reviews and goals of SAG
• Will work closely with the Director of Special Assets Credit to make sure strategy and risk rating is proper
• Will work on RCSA with the compliance department
• Will meet at minimum once a week with Executive Director of Loss Mitigation
• Make sure SAG is up to date on any Bank Training

Additional Essential Functions
• Ensure compliance with Northwest’s policies and procedures, and Federal/State regulations
• Navigate Microsoft Office Software, computer applications, and software specific to the department in order to maximize technology tools and gain efficiency
• Work as part of a team
• Work with on-site equipment

What You Bring to the Team
• Complete special projects as necessary

Safety and Health for Supervisors with Direct Reports
• Provide leadership and positive direction for maintaining the safety and loss prevention program
• Actively participate in and support employee participation in the safety and loss prevention program by ensuring that employees know how to properly report a safety issue, making sure that all accidents are promptly reported to Human Resources and documented, and ensuring that prompt action is taken whenever workplace hazards are identified
• Help implement emergency procedures

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education
Bachelor's Degree in business/finance or related subject

Work Experience
8 - 12 years experience in special assets, repossessed assets, bankruptcy, collections, commercial lending, litigation or loan workouts.

General Supervisory/Manager Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
• Ability to identify existing and potential problems, obtain and evaluate relevant information, identify possible causes of the problems, and suggest an alternative course of action including innovative or creative approaches
• Ability to allocate and effectively use information, personnel, time, and other resources necessary for implementation of Northwest’s strategic plans
• Ability to make decisions, render judgments, and take action on tasks within the scope of given authority in a timely fashion
• Ability to develop, evaluate, and implement alternative courses of action, based on correct assumptions concerning resources and guidelines, and support decisions or recommendations with data or reasoning
• Ability to present and express ideas and information effectively and concisely in an oral and/or written mode in a manner appropriate for the audience
• Ability to listen and comprehend what others are saying and facilitate the open exchange of ideas and information
• Ability to motivate and provide direction in the activities of others, appropriately assigning work and authority, in the accomplishment of goals; providing advice and assistance as required

L'opportunité

Le/La Coordinateur(trice) Logistique Site est responsable de la réception, de la manutention, du stockage, de la préservation et du suivi de maintenance des équipements, matériels et marchandises sur les sites HVDC.

Le/La Coordinateur(trice) Logistique Site est rattaché(e) fonctionnellement au HVDC Head of C&C Site Support et opère sous la responsabilité opérationnelle du Site Manager en charge du chantier.

Votre impact

Coordination des livraisons de matériel

  • Coordonner avec les équipes Supply Chain Management (SCM), les fournisseurs et les sous-traitants la planification et le suivi des livraisons de matériel, notamment les plannings, quantités, dimensions et exigences de stockage.
  • Assurer le suivi des approvisionnements et des livraisons des équipements fournis par les sous-traitants afin de garantir une visibilité régulière sur les dates de livraison prévues.
  • Évaluer les risques et retards de livraison avec les parties prenantes du projet et analyser leurs impacts potentiels sur les activités du site et le planning du projet.

Réception du matériel et logistique de site

  • Coordonner la réception, le déchargement et la manutention des matériels en toute sécurité en veillant à la disponibilité des équipements, ressources et mesures HSE nécessaires.
  • Contrôler les livraisons, vérifier la documentation d’expédition, identifier les écarts ou dommages éventuels et initier les processus de déclaration et de réclamation appropriés.
  • Maintenir des registres précis des matériels réceptionnés, mettre à jour les systèmes logistiques et communiquer l’arrivée des équipements ainsi que les actions associées aux parties prenantes concernées.

Gestion des réclamations qualité

  • Initier et gérer les réclamations qualité relatives aux matériels manquants, endommagés ou non conformes à l’aide des outils de reporting applicables.
  • Assurer le suivi de la résolution des réclamations et des délais de remplacement tout en maintenant une visibilité sur les sujets en cours.
  • Collaborer avec les équipes site, SCM et logistique afin d’évaluer les impacts, mettre en œuvre les actions correctives et clôturer les réclamations une fois résolues.

Gestion du stockage et de la préservation

  • Élaborer et maintenir les plans de préservation des matériels afin de garantir le stockage et la conservation des équipements conformément aux exigences des fabricants et du projet.
  • Assurer la traçabilité des stocks et la gestion des emplacements de stockage afin de faciliter l’identification et la mise à disposition des matériels.
  • Coordonner les transferts et remises de matériel avec les partenaires et sous-traitants en garantissant le respect des exigences de stockage, de préservation et de documentation.

Coordination des activités de maintenance

  • Coordonner les opérations de maintenance des équipements du site lorsque les intervalles de maintenance planifiés sont atteints pendant les phases d’exécution et de mise en service.
  • Suivre les heures de fonctionnement des équipements et s’assurer de la disponibilité des plans de maintenance, des ressources, des consommables et du personnel nécessaires.
  • Tenir à jour et transmettre les enregistrements de maintenance à l’équipe Projet pour la documentation finale du projet et du client.

Gestion des pièces de rechange

  • Assurer la remise des pièces de rechange destinées au client dans les délais définis et conformément à la stratégie de transfert du projet.
  • Garantir la séparation et le contrôle des pièces de rechange client et des pièces de rechange de mise en service tout au long du cycle de vie du projet.
  • Coordonner avec les équipes projet et mise en service l’autorisation et la documentation du transfert des pièces de rechange au client.

Gestion des matériels inutilisés et des déchets

  • Identifier les matériels inutilisés, réutilisables ou destinés à la mise au rebut en collaboration avec les parties prenantes du site et du projet.
  • Contribuer au transfert, au redéploiement, à la vente ou à la mise aux enchères des matériels excédentaires conformément aux procédures de l’entreprise et aux exigences SCM.
  • Coordonner l’élimination conforme des déchets et matériels hors d’usage via des prestataires agréés, dans le respect des réglementations locales et des standards HSE.

Votre profil

  • Expérience en logistique de chantier, supply chain, gestion d’entrepôt ou projets de construction, avec la capacité à gérer les flux de matériels dans un environnement projet dynamique.
  • Bonne maîtrise de la coordination logistique, de la gestion des stocks ainsi que des pratiques de stockage et de préservation des équipements, garantissant la traçabilité et l’efficacité opérationnelle.
  • Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les équipes projet, les sous-traitants, les fournisseurs, les transporteurs et les clients, associée à de solides compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes.
  • Bonne connaissance des exigences HSE, des standards qualité et des processus logistiques, avec un engagement fort en matière de conformité et de sécurité au travail.
  • Esprit proactif, organisé et orienté solutions, avec la capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités, anticiper les risques et assurer une documentation ainsi qu’un reporting rigoureux.
  • Très bonne pratique des langues française et anglaise

En savoir plus sur nous

Nous pensons que le travail de qualité s’épanouit dans un environnement où les collaborateurs se sentent réellement soutenus et justement valorisés. Nos avantages sont conçus pour créer une véritable valeur pour chacun, en favorisant l’engagement, la performance et le développement. En plaçant le bien-être au cœur de nos priorités, nous construisons un environnement de travail où la réussite individuelle et organisationnelle progresse conjointement.

L’offre finale sera déterminée en fonction des compétences, des qualifications, des expériences du candidat, et en cohérence avec les grilles salariales internes.

  • Bonus, Participation, Titres-restaurant ou accès à un restaurant d’entreprise, Assurance santé, Avantages sociaux, Horaires de travail flexibles, Modèle de travail hybride, Plateforme dédiée au bien-être, CSE: Avantages liés à la vie familiale et plateforme internet offrant des avantages sur certains achats, Parking, Partenariats entreprise: Crèche d'entreprise (sous conditions d'attribution)

English version

The role is fully based on a construction site based in Corsica.

The Opportunity

The Site Logistics Coordinator is responsible for the receipt, handling, storage, preservation and maintenance of goods and materials on HVDC sites.

The Site Logistics Coordinator reports functionally to the HVDC Head of C&C Site Support and is operationally under the direction of the Site Manager responsible for the construction site.

How You'll Make an Impact

1. Material Delivery Coordination

  • Coordinate with Supply Chain Management (SCM), suppliers, and subcontractors to plan and monitor material deliveries, including schedules, quantities, dimensions, and storage requirements.
  • Track procurement and delivery status of subcontractor-supplied equipment, ensuring regular updates and visibility of expected delivery dates.
  • Assess delivery risks and delays with project stakeholders and evaluate potential impacts on site activities and project schedules.

2. Material Receipt and Site Logistics

  • Coordinate the safe receipt, unloading, and handling of materials by ensuring the availability of required equipment, resources, and HSE controls.
  • Inspect deliveries, verify packing documentation, identify discrepancies or damages, and initiate the appropriate reporting and claim processes.
  • Maintain accurate records of received materials, update logistics systems, and communicate material arrivals and related actions to relevant stakeholders.

3. Quality Reporting and Claims Management

  • Initiate and manage quality claims for missing, damaged, or non-conforming materials using the applicable reporting systems.
  • Monitor claim resolution and replacement delivery schedules while maintaining visibility of outstanding issues.
  • Collaborate with site, SCM, and logistics teams to assess impacts, implement mitigation measures, and close claims upon successful resolution.

4. Storage and Preservation Management

  • Develop and maintain material preservation plans, ensuring equipment is stored and preserved according to manufacturer and project requirements.
  • Maintain clear inventory tracking and storage location records to support efficient material identification and retrieval.
  • Coordinate material handovers with partners and subcontractors, ensuring compliance with storage, preservation, and documentation requirements.

5. Maintenance Coordination

  • Coordinate maintenance activities for site equipment reaching scheduled maintenance intervals during project execution and commissioning.
  • Monitor equipment operating hours and ensure maintenance plans, resources, consumables, and personnel are available when required.
  • Maintain and hand over maintenance records to Project Management for final project and customer documentation.

6. Spare Parts Management

  • Manage the timely handover of customer spare parts in line with project requirements and approved handover strategies.
  • Ensure clear segregation and control of customer spare parts and commissioning spare parts throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Coordinate with project and commissioning teams to authorize and document the transfer of spare parts to customers.

7. Management of Unused and Scrap Materials

  • Identify unused, reusable, and scrap materials in collaboration with site and project stakeholders.
  • Support the transfer, redeployment, sale, or auction of surplus materials in accordance with company procedures and SCM requirements.
  • Coordinate the compliant disposal of scrap materials through approved waste management providers, ensuring adherence to local regulations and HSE standards.

Your Background

  • Experience in site logistics, supply chain, warehouse operations, or construction projects, with the ability to manage material flows in a dynamic project environment.
  • Strong knowledge of logistics coordination, inventory management, material storage, and preservation practices, ensuring traceability and operational efficiency.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with project teams, subcontractors, suppliers, transport providers, and customers, supported by strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Good understanding of HSE requirements, quality standards, and logistics processes, with a commitment to compliance and safe working practices.
  • Proactive, organized, and solution-oriented mindset, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, anticipate risks, and maintain accurate documentation and reporting.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in French and English.

More about us

We believe great work thrives in an environment where people feel genuinely supported and fairly rewarded. Our benefits are designed to create real value for every individual—fueling engagement, performance, and growth. By prioritizing well-being, we build a workplace where personal and organizational success grow together.

title: 2027 X-Ray Imaging and Physical Analysis Research Associate
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories’ technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems.

The Microelectronics Technology Department (MTD) is part of PSL with specialized laboratories used to test, accelerate, and analyze, failures in electronics used for space system. MTD is comprised of two sections: one that performs radiation effects testing and discrete microelectronics testing, while the other section performs failure analysis on microelectronics using tools that can identify anomalies from the macroscopic down to the atomic scale. We are hiring an X-Ray Imaging and Physical Analysis Research Associate (Research Associate ll - Hardware/Device Testing). You will be responsible for performing of X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT) data acquisition and image analysis, and also sample preparation and mounting technique development for XCT, and other advanced physical analysis imaging techniques, to enhance perceptivity of failures and anomalies in different microelectronic materials and devices for space applications.

Highlights of our lab's capabilities can be seen here: Microelectronics Lab Virtual Tour

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in El Segundo, CA.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Collect and interpret 2D X-ray radiography images and 3D x-ray computed tomography data of aerospace parts including microelectronics, 3D-printed materials, machined parts, including flight hardware
  • Support the analysis of materials, devices, test structures and prototypes using tools including optical microscopes and XCT
  • Sample preparation with mechanical polisher, laser engraving tool, and sample fixturing with FDM 3D printers, machine shops
  • Maintain equipment capability by procuring replacement parts, performing basic maintenance and calibration, and coordinating service visits from equipment vendors, data archival. Compiling information.

What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring

  • Strong written and oral communication skills
  • Must work well in a team environment
  • Possess organizational, time management and project management skills
  • Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational need
  • Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations

What You Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college/university program in electrical engineering, physics, chemistry, computer science, material science, earth science, biomedical engineering, mechanical engineering or related fields (pursuing or conferred within last 12 months)
  • 0-1 year of industry experience
  • Knowledge x-ray absorption and propagation.
  • Experience working with Python or similar programming language
  • Strong interpersonal skills, ability to effectively convey technical information to non-technical personnel via oral and written forms
  • Willing to travel occasionally to work location or customer site/domestically/internationally approx. 10% if required.
  • This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Master’s degree from an accredited college/university program in related fields (pursuing or conferred within last 12 months)
  • Experience using LLMs to code in Python for instrument communication, data acquisition and analysis.
  • Experience with CAD software and machine shop or 3D-printing to make custom fixtures for holding samples in the XCT machines.
  • Experience with maintaining, calibrating, and servicing X-ray sources.
  • Experience with using XCT for failure analysis and root cause analysis for microelectronic and aerospace parts
  • Experience with Volume Graphics, Avizo, and/or Dragonfly

  • Experience across multiple Identity and Access Management disciplines, including Identity Governance, Directory Services, Authentication, Authorization, and Privileged Access Management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CISSP, Microsoft Identity, CyberArk, or similar professional certifications.

  • Experience working within highly regulated and global enterprise environments.

  • Knowledge of enterprise security frameworks, governance models, and compliance standards.

title: Home-Based Video Editor
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

Hiring Priority: Active Hiring

The DCX Client Services - Home-Based Video Editor will work as a full-time employee for a growing business based in the United States. You will get a chance to learn new skills as well as demonstrate skills you've learned in the past. You will be responsible for closely following the instructions and processes outlined by our client.

The daily tasks will vary, so it will be necessary to be very flexible in this position. Other necessary characteristics of the job include having a strong attention to detail,the ability to work well with co-workers, and a desire to learn new work skills.

REQUIRED CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Creative & Technical Proficiency – Demonstrates strong short-form video editing skills, creative judgment, and an understanding of social media trends, pacing, hooks, retention, captions, B-roll, and visual storytelling.

  • Exceptional Attention to Detail – Consistently produces polished, accurate, and client-ready work, with particular attention to captions, timing, audio, visual consistency, and brand standards.

  • Organization & Time Management – Highly organized and structured, able to manage high-volume workloads, prioritize multiple projects, maintain organized files, and consistently meet tight deadlines without sacrificing quality.

  • Communication & Ownership – Communicates clearly and proactively, responds well to feedback, works independently, and takes ownership of projects by making thoughtful creative decisions and suggesting improvements when appropriate.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Short-Form Video Editing

  • Edit high-volume short-form social media content primarily for:

    • Instagram Reels

    • TikTok

    • YouTube Shorts

    • Similar short-form platforms

  • Take footage from raw files through to a polished, client-ready final video.

  • Work with a variety of source content, including:

    • Scripted/skit-based content

    • Testimonials

    • Podcasts

    • Long-form YouTube videos

    • Interviews

    • Events

    • Talking-head content

    • Client-specific footage and other media

Editing & Post-Production

  • Cut, organize, and assemble raw footage.

  • Identify the strongest clips, moments, and hooks when needed.

  • Remove dead space, filler words, ums/uhs, and unnecessary content.

  • Create strong pacing designed specifically for short-form social media retention.

  • Add, proofread, and correct captions.

  • Add B-roll, including:

    • Client-provided or internally shot footage

    • Stock footage when appropriate

  • Incorporate supporting creative elements when appropriate, including:

    • Music

    • Sound effects

    • Images

    • GIFs

    • Memes

    • Other visual elements

  • Create basic motion graphics and animations.

  • Use keyframing, punch-ins, speed ramping, and other modern editing techniques.

  • Perform audio cleanup and basic audio mixing.

  • Perform basic color correction and color grading.

  • Recreate the editing style of provided reference Reels, TikToks, and other examples.

  • Adapt editing styles and follow brand standards across multiple clients.

Creative Decision-Making

  • Follow edit briefs, scripts, shot lists, concepts, and reference videos.

  • Make independent creative decisions when appropriate.

  • Identify opportunities to improve:

    • Hooks

    • Pacing

    • Clip selection

    • Structure

    • Visual changes

    • Overall viewer retention

  • Proactively suggest improvements rather than simply following instructions.

  • Develop a strong understanding of modern short-form social media editing and retention strategies.

Revisions & Collaboration

  • Implement revisions from the internal team and clients.

  • Communicate clearly regarding questions, challenges, and project needs.

  • Take feedback professionally and apply it accurately.

  • Work independently while maintaining alignment with project expectations and brand standards.

File & Project Management

  • Maintain organized project files, assets, raw footage, and final exports.

  • Follow SLF Media's internal file organization and naming structures.

  • Ensure projects are properly organized and easy for other team members to access when needed.

Production Volume & Turnaround

  • Comfortably complete approximately 6–7 short-form videos during a full editing day, depending on complexity.

  • Handle monthly production volumes that may exceed 200 videos during busy periods.

  • Typically work within 1–2 week turnaround windows for batches.

  • Be comfortable handling occasional rush projects requiring completion within 1–2 days.

  • Work quickly without sacrificing quality or attention to detail.

Role Description:

The Regulatory Reporting Industry Engagement & Advocacy Lead is responsible for representing the firm's interests within key industry forums and working groups, influencing non-financial regulatory reporting standards, and ensuring that industry developments are effectively communicated and assessed across the organization.

The role serves as a subject matter expert (SME) on regulatory reporting obligations and partners closely with internal stakeholders to support compliance, policy interpretation, and strategic regulatory change initiatives.

This role will be inclusive of working with the following stakeholders: Change Management, Trade Reporting Control Group (TRCG), Global Compliance and Operational Risk (GCOR), Legal, Operations, Technology, Business Representatives, Industry Trade Associations and Working Groups and Regulatory Bodies and Market Infrastructure Providers

Responsibilities:

  • Actively participate in industry working groups and regulatory forums, representing the organization's interests and articulating the firm's position on regulatory reporting-related matters.
  • Build and maintain relationships with industry participants, trade associations, regulators, and market infrastructure providers to stay informed of emerging regulatory developments and industry practices.
  • Understand BofA position on regulatory interpretations to influence industry-led decisions in order to minimize impact on BofA/protect BofA interests.
  • Contribute to discussions, consultations, and advocacy efforts within key industry groups, including but not limited to: ISDA EMEA Data & Reporting Working Group, ISDA US Data & Reporting Working Group, ISDA MiFID Implementation and Advocacy Steering Group, ISDA APAC Regulatory Reporting working group, Global Foreign Exchange Division (GFXD), UK Finance Reporting Working Group, DTCC Working Groups, UnaVista Working Groups
  • Monitor regulatory developments and changes to reporting frameworks across relevant jurisdictions, providing timely analysis and updates to support ongoing compliance with regulatory obligations.
  • Assess the potential impact of new regulatory requirements, industry standards, and market practices on existing reporting processes and controls.
  • Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders, including Change Management, Trade Reporting Control Group (TRCG), Global Compliance and Operational Risk (GCOR), Legal, and business partners to ensure consistent interpretation and implementation of reporting requirements.
  • Support the development of firm-wide positions on regulatory reporting issues and industry consultation responses where required.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and advisory support to business, operations, technology, compliance, and change teams on regulatory reporting requirements and industry best practices.
  • Assist in identifying regulatory reporting risks and opportunities for process improvement, control enhancement, and operational efficiency.

What we are looking for:

  • Strong knowledge of global regulatory reporting regimes and associated industry standards.
  • Experience participating in industry working groups, trade associations, or regulatory forums.
  • Deep understanding of transaction reporting, trade reporting, and regulatory reporting obligations across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Ability to interpret complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical business impacts and implementation considerations.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders and represent the organization externally.
  • Experience working across Compliance, Legal, Operations, Technology, and Change functions.
  • Excellent analytical, presentation, and written communication skills.

Skills that will help:

  • Effective representation of the firm's interests in industry forums.
  • Timely communication and escalation of relevant regulatory developments.
  • Strong alignment across internal stakeholders on regulatory reporting requirements.
  • Successful assessment and implementation of regulatory and industry changes.
  • Delivery of high-quality SME support and regulatory reporting guidance across the organization

title: Field Supervisor (Part Time)
description:
Job Title

Field Supervisor (Part Time)

Agency

West Texas A&M University

Department

Education

Proposed Minimum Salary

$30.00 hourly

Job Location

Canyon, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

A field supervisor (FS) is a contracted certified educator employed by WTAMU that will observe teacher candidates, and monitor their performance by evaluating and providing constructive feedback to the novice teachers to improve their effectiveness as developing educators. Field supervisors serve as a liaison between the school district and the university to create a positive and valuable experience for interns and clinical teachers. They are instrumental in the growth of educators by sharing feedback with the teacher candidate using effective coaching strategies, and collaborating with the mentor/cooperating teacher(s) and administrator(s).

Field supervisors will be involved with field observations and support for their assigned candidates. Field Supervisors will conduct formal observations and informal observations when the candidate is completing their clinical teaching experience or internship. In addition, the field supervisor will keep documentation of their work with their assigned novice teacher.

This position works during the Fall and Spring semesters in alignment with local school district calendars.

Formal observations

Field Supervisors will conduct preconferences, classroom observations, and post-conferences (POP cycles) with candidates. The in-person classroom observation must be a minimum of 45 minutes, while the individualized preconference and interactive post conference is approximately 15-30 minutes. The preconference can be done via zoom, phone, and/or email. The post-conference must be synchronous by phone, zoom, or face-to-face to meet TEA requirements. The Field Supervisor will submit written evaluation feedback to the candidate, mentor, and administrator. The FS will be given three hours of time credit for completing a formal observation (which includes preconference, classroom observation, post-conference, and write-up of observation report).

Informal observations

The informal walkthrough observation is a brief 15-minute check-in with the candidate to see how they are doing on the action steps provided to them during their formal observation(s). During the informal walkthrough observation, the field supervisor provides additional feedback to the candidate. The FS will be given one hour of time credit for completing an informal walkthrough observation

Trainings for Field Supervisors:

The field supervision position requires completion of mandatory training Texas Education Agency (TEA)-approved T-TESS Field Supervisor Observation training and WTAMU’s EPP training for Field Supervisors.

TEA-approved T-TESS Field Supervisor observation training

This training is required by TEA of all Field Supervisors to help them to be prepared in how to coach and support a teacher candidate. The T-TESS Field Supervisor Observation Training must be provided by an approved trainer. Once this training is complete, you will be provided a certificate for your records that you must submit to WT’s EPP. If the FS has a T-TESS appraiser certificate that is active, they may submit the appraiser certificate to WT for documentation in lieu of the TEA-T-TESS FS observation training.

  • Note: Once the appraiser certificate goes inactive, the mandatory TEA T-TESS Field Supervisor training and certificate is required.
  • Note: starting 9/1/2026, all Field Supervisors will need re-trained on the T-TESS Field Supervisor observation training every three years (unless they hold the valid, active T-TESS appraiser certificate).

Educator Preparation Program (EPP) Training

  • The EPP training is to go over the expectations, processes, and forms used by WT Field Supervisors. This training will be provided at least twice a year. Compensation for completing the training will be two hours.

Travel and mileage reimbursement

Field Supervisors must be willing to utilize their personal vehicle to travel to visit preservice teachers and to submit required paperwork to receive reimbursement for mileage. WTAMU will provide processes and forms to help Field Supervisors get reimbursed monthly for their travel. WT FS should be willing to travel within a 100-mile radius to supervise clinical teachers or interns.

Workload & Pay for WTAMU Field Supervisors

Fields Supervisors will be assigned clinical teachers (known as student teachers) and ACP interns (known as PACE interns); the load can be from 8-14 candidates depending on the semester. Field Supervisors cannot work more than 19 hours per week or (5-6 candidate observations a week, if possible).

The Department of Education will pay supervision costs including observations at the following rates:

  • $90.00 per formal observation report plus mileage for a Clinical Teacher (CT) or ACP intern.
    • Each observation completion will be counted as three hours in the WT workday system. The three hours includes drive time, pre- and post-conference time, classroom observations, and submission of written coaching feedback to the candidate.
  • $30.00 per informal observation for a CT or ACP intern.
    • Each observation completion will be counted as one hour in the WT workday system.

Necessary Qualifications:

  • Valid certification in the class in which supervision is provided
  • Hired by the educator preparation program (EPP)
  • Must complete the Texas A&M System hiring paperwork through HR.
  • Must have three years of creditable experience and current certification in the class in which supervision is provided
  • Participates in Texas Education Agency-approved T-TESS Field Supervisor Observation training to observe clinical teachers and ACP interns.
  • Or provide a certificate of completion of this TEA one-day T-TESS Observation Field Supervisor training from another program/institution for our TEA records.
  • Or hold an active T-TESS appraiser training certificate (three-day)

Preferred:

  • Texas Instructional Leadership training. Can be provided by WTAMU over the year.
  • Preferably has advanced credentials

Items to Submit:

  • Letter of interest
  • Resume/Curriculum Vitae
  • Two letters of recommendations
  • TEA ID in TEA ECOS system and TEAL account
  • Copy of TEA Educator Certificate

Items to submit after official hiring and for WT TEA files

  • Signed Educators’ Code of Ethics and Standard Practices for Texas Educators (TAC §247.2)
  • Service Record
  • Attestation Form verifying your accomplishment as an educator as shown by student learning. (form signed by previous administrator or direct supervisor) or provide documented evidence of growth in student learning
  • Evidence of completion for all required TEA Observation training.
  • TEA- Field Supervisor Observation training (one-day) paid by WT
  • Or active T-TESS appraiser certificate training certificate (three-day)

Points of Contact for Field Supervision for WTAMU

  • Mr. Gilbert Antunez, Associate Director of Educator Preparation, Director of Field Placements and Supervision, gantunez@wtamu.edu, 806.651.2908
  • Dr. Crystal Hughes, Executive Director of Educator Preparation, Associate Professor, chughes@wtamu.edu, 806.651.2605
  • Pyxa Sovilay, PACE Coordinator, psovilay@wtamu.edu, 806.651.2613

Being part of a global cross-functional team of analysts, developers and testers, you will play a key role in the analysis and refinement of both functional and non-functional requirements from partners throughout the commodity trading lifecycle, using structured business analysis tools, techniques, and methodologies. Primary Skills

  • Expectation of proven experience designing, planning, implementing, maintaining, and documenting digital products and market risk solutions within commodity trading environment or other financial intuitions.

  • Strong communication skills will be massively important for the role for both partner and delivery of the global market risk team. This includes technical content in business context.

  • Ability to engage and influence and able to decompose technical considerations that everyone can understand is key.

  • Experience using AI tools to support ideation, backlog creation, and overall product development.

title: Rock Hauler
description:
BURNCO is a leading supplier of construction materials, proudly serving communities across North America. We are committed to quality, safety, and customer service, and we’re building a team that reflects those same values.

Do you have the experience, focus, and safety-first mindset needed to operate a tractor trailer in a fast-paced construction environment? We are hiring a Rock Hauler for our site in Justin, Texas who take pride in safe driving, reliable material transport, and maintaining their equipment. If you have commercial driving experience and a strong commitment to safety, we want to hear from you!

You will be responsible for safely operating a tractor trailer combination and ready-mix truck to transport aggregate materials between our plants and customer sites. You will play a key role in supporting a strong safety culture by following DOT regulations, maintaining your equipment, communicating operational concerns, and helping keep our facilities clean, safe, and efficient.

What you will be doing

  • Safely operate a Tractor Trailer Combination & Ready-Mix Truck in urban and rural areas with tight construction sites at times
  • Completing routine maintenance of equipment, including reporting minor mechanical issues and thorough cleanliness of unit daily
  • Contribute to keeping areas in and around the plants clean and hazard free
  • Follow all BURNCO policies as well as local, state, and federal regulations, including DOT and company driving standards
  • Communicate and escalate any operational or safety concerns to the supervisor
  • Crosstrain in other areas as needed to support team operations
  • Perform related duties as assigned

What we would like from you

  • 21+ years old
  • Possession of a valid Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) is required for this position
  • Two years of experience driving a tractor trailer combination, or 1 year over the road with a tractor trailer combination
  • Consistent, reliable attendance with the flexibility to work irregular hours, including scheduled Saturdays
  • Ability to pass PSP, MVR, background check, drug & alcohol testing and a physical assessment
  • Ability to lift up to 50lbs
  • Flexibility to work from other BURNCO Plants based on business needs
  • Clear commitment to safety, customer service, and teamwork in all aspects of the job
  • Active FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse registration (required for all CDL drivers)
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent preferred

Location and other key details:

  • This is a full-time permanent field-based position at our plant in Justin, Texas
  • This is a safety-sensitive position requiring successful completion of PSP, MVR, background check, pre-employment drug test, and DOT physical assessment prior to hire
  • Regular outdoor work with exposure to a range of weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, and snow
  • Required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) including safety shoes, vests, and glasses, ear plugs, and hard hats, with additional PPE for special jobs as required
  • Frequent use of hand-eye coordination and near / far vision to operate equipment safely
  • Regularly required to stand, walk, sit, climb, bend, reach, lift or carry up to 50 lbs
  • Utilize fine motor skills, gross motor skills, manual dexterity, color discernment, and active hearing / listening throughout work
  • Exposure to loud noises, heavy machinery, moving equipment, oil, debris, solvents, smoke, gases, fumes, and aggregate materials typical of plant and construction environments

Why BURNCO?

  • Be part of a supportive, high-performing team that values your growth and success
  • Enjoy competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, paid time off, and more
  • Experience our inclusive, collaborative, and safety-focused culture
  • Take part in team events, professional development activities, and community initiatives

BURNCO is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

We thank all applicants for their interest. Only those chosen for an interview will be contacted.

Growth mindset with a focus on challenging the status quo and driving creative solutions.

Self-motivated, organized and capable of managing work independently!

Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, highly agile and iterative development environment.

Construction Materials Field Supervisor

Requisition Number: 2026-1800-21


S&ME is seeking a dedicated, enthusiastic, experienced leader with a background in Construction Materials Testing as a Field Supervisor to become part of our Construction Services team in Atlanta, Georgia. Join S&ME today and help us provide engineering solutions to our clients!


At S&ME, we have a history of delivering innovative geotechnical, civil, environmental, and construction material testing for over 50 years. Over the decades, we have grown into a trusted partner for clients across various industries, including transportation, energy, water, waste management, education, government, commercial, industrial, and more. Our commitment to technical excellence and integrity has established us as a leader in our field.

Why Work at S&ME?

  • Employee Ownership: As a 100% employee-owned company, our ESOP gives you a personal stake in our success and the opportunity to build long-term wealth while helping shape our future.
  • Career Growth: We invest in your success with mentorship, training, and leadership opportunities.
  • Exciting Projects: Big or small, simple or complex, we do it all. Our projects are as diverse as they are exciting, so every day brings something new.
  • Supportive Culture: Collaboration, respect, and positivity fuel our team environment.
  • Flexibility: Work-life balance matters to us, helping you thrive inside and outside the office.
  • Community Impact: Your work will directly improve the communities where we live, work, and play.

About The Role:

As a Construction Materials Field Supervisor, you will oversee a dedicated team of construction materials testing professionals, managing daily operations across multiple project sites. Your role will be pivotal in ensuring the success of projects by providing high-quality testing services, maintaining strong client relationships, supporting growth initiatives, and driving operational efficiency. You will balance team management with personal project contributions, ensuring quality, safety, and efficiency. Your leadership will be key in client coordination, managing multiple projects concurrently, and upholding the highest safety standards.

  • Direction and Scheduling: Provide supervision and oversight to field staff, organize schedules with clients and contractors, and manage personnel for field assignments.
  • Coordination: Frequently coordinate with Services Managers and Project Managers on the progress of current and upcoming projects.
  • Training and Certifications: Train staff on field testing and inspections, oversee certification opportunities, and maintain a summary of current employee certifications.
  • Safety: Lead safety efforts for field staff, conduct regular safety meetings, and coach staff on the use of PPE and safety protocols.
  • Equipment and Quality: Ensure staff has appropriate testing equipment, assist with equipment maintenance and calibration, and support the Quality Assurance Supervisor.

About You:

  • You have a High School diploma or GED
  • You have a Bachelor's degree in Civil, Structural, or Geotechnical engineering or a construction-related field, a plus
  • You have a minimum of 2 years of experience in construction materials testing/inspecting of soil, concrete, masonry, and/or asphalt
    • Experience in a supervisory or management role
  • You have active Construction Materials industry certifications such as:
    • American Concrete Institute (ACI): Field Testing Grade I; Strength Testing Technician; Laboratory Technician and/or International Code Council (ICC): Special Inspector (Reinforced Concrete, Masonry, Soils), a plus
  • You have strong communication skills (speaking, reading, and writing) in the English language

You Are Willing and Able to:

Perform the physical demands of the position with the use of company-provided Personal Protective Equipment such as:

  • Working the majority of the time outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Walking over rough, uneven terrain and standing for potentially up to 12 hours a day
  • Routinely lifting and carrying 40-50lbs (field/laboratory samples and equipment)
  • Maneuvering field equipment safely, such as a loaded wheelbarrow, on uneven ground around active construction sites

Grow With Us:

At S&ME, your career growth matters. You'll receive professional training, work on exciting projects, and be part of a company that truly invests in its people. This is more than a job; it's a chance to build a long-term career in the engineering and construction industry. S&ME provides a comprehensive benefits package to support you and your family, as well as career development resources. Come grow and thrive with us at S&ME!

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Plans with HSA and FSA options
  • 100% Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) with a 5% company contribution
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Paid Holidays and Paid Time Off (PTO) - with rollover options
  • Paid Maternity/Parental Leave
  • Employee Recognition Program
  • Credential Incentive Program
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Company Vehicle with Fuel Card for Project-Based Work
  • $2,000 Referral Bonuses & More!

Join us at S&ME!


This full-time role offers competitive pay based on experience. Candidates must comply with our Fleet Management, Substance Policy, and Reference Check requirements. title: Import Analyst
description:
Job Description:

Saab, Inc. is growing, and import compliance is being stood up as its own discipline within Trade Compliance, separate from logistics execution. The successful candidate is a self-starter who is motivated to advance U.S. import compliance and customs authorization for defense and commercial programs, build relationships across sites and brokers, write import policies and turn them into understandable operational procedures, and help design how U.S. imports are authorized, documented, and measured. In this role, you will authorize the cross-border move and maintain compliance. Supply Chain’s logistics team will book freight, create BOLs, and settle carrier invoices.

Responsibilities:

  • Construct, improve, and run the U.S. import control framework for Saab, Inc., including entry review, exception handling, and CBP inquiries.

  • Build relationships with site shipping, programs, brokers, and forwarders so the handoff works, with shipment facts in and compliance direction and authorization out.

  • Draft and operationalize import policies and SOPs, including clearance, Temporary Import Bond (TIB), Carnet, DSP-61 temporary import license, permanent import, Duty-Free Entry (DFE), broker engagement, and recordkeeping.

  • Engage with Saab, Inc.’s international affiliates and other entities to coordinate imports into and exports from the U.S.

  • Clear imports through Customs by reviewing entry packets and resolving classification, valuation, origin, and document issues before the broker files.

  • Assign and maintain HTS classifications, add and track items in the system, and coordinate ECCN/USML questions with the export team.

  • Administer DFE under HTSUS 9808.00.30 by adding eligible contracts in Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), coordinating Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) certificates with brokers, and keeping DFARS 252.225-7013 documentation complete.

  • Manage TIBs, carnets, and ITAR temporary import authorizations, including DSP-61 licenses and exemptions, as well as tracking, close-out, and retention.

  • Support ACE for imports, including Periodic Monthly Statement duty accuracy, protest flags, and payment authorization. Logistics and Accounting code the same statement to cost centers.

  • Support customs bonds, including U.S. and Non-Resident Importer (NRI) Canada, and Powers of Attorney and the authorized-filer list under subject matter oversight.

  • Manage the compliance side of broker and forwarder relationships, including SOPs, the authorized-broker list, and compliance KPIs. Logistics owns rates, booking, and freight-invoice approval.

  • Approve International Shipping Requests (ISR) and domestic tariff questionnaires as assigned.

  • Put import and temporary import/export activity into a durable system of record, such as OCR EASE, SharePoint, or an equivalent platform, and help shape how that looks as tools mature.

  • Use SharePoint and practical process-improvement skills to replace informal knowledge with an understandable and repeatable process that sites can follow.

  • Assess sites against the import requirements you help prepare, then address gaps directly rather than work around them.

  • Travel domestically and possibly internationally, 5%-10% annually.

Compensation Ranges:

Auburn Hills, MI, East Syracuse, NY, Grayling, MI, Orlando, FL: $64,600 - $80,700

Bristol, RI, Cranston, RI: $71,000 - $88,800

Ashburn, VA, Quincy, MA, Washington, DC: $77,400 - $96,800

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in international business, supply chain, or a related field with 3+ years in U.S. import/customs operations or import compliance (including entry packets, HTS, and broker coordination), or a Master’s degree with 1+ year of experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Working knowledge of CBP entry, HTS classification, and how a broker files.

  • Sufficient export control literacy to flag DSP-61, TIB, Carnet, or ITAR issues and escalate them while providing clear information and options to enable decision-making.

  • Experience writing or improving a procedure, playbook, or SharePoint/tracker that other people then used.

  • Strong communication skills to clearly explain issues and requirements rather than simply state them.

  • Microsoft Excel proficiency, comfort working in ACE or a GTM tool, and willingness to work in internal systems and platforms.

  • Must be a U.S. person. Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance may be required depending on activities. This position may require access to export-controlled technical data.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience within the defense industry.

  • Security clearance or eligibility to obtain a security clearance.

  • Experience working with foreign entities and an appreciation of cultural differences.

  • Ability to work independently as well as under direction.

  • Strong organizational skills to perform and manage multiple substantive and administrative activities concurrently.

  • Ability to build and cultivate strong working relationships with brokers, site shipping, programs, and other key stakeholders.

  • Enjoys challenges, identifies improvements, and finds solutions.

  • Motivation to learn and improve.

  • Interest in sitting for the Customs Broker License exam later with Saab, Inc.’s backing (subject to company policy and approval).

The compensation range provided is a general guideline. When extending an offer, Saab, Inc. considers factors including (but not limited to) the role and associated responsibilities, location, and market and business considerations, as well as the candidate's work experience, key skills, and education/training.

Skills and Experience:

Citizenship Requirements:

Must be a U.S. citizen, Permanent Resident (green card holder), or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

Drug-Free Workplaces:

Saab is a federal government contractor and adheres to policies and programs necessary for sustaining drug-free workplaces. As a condition of employment, candidates will be required to pass a pre-employment drug screen.

Benefits:

Saab provides an excellent working environment offering professional growth opportunities, competitive wages, work-life balance, a business casual atmosphere and comprehensive benefits.

Highlights include:

  • Medical, vision, and dental insurance for employees and dependents

  • Generous paid time off, including 8 designated holidays

  • 401(k) with employer contributions

  • Tuition assistance and student loan assistance

  • Wellness and employee assistance resources

  • Employee stock purchase opportunities

  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage

About Us:

Saab is a leading defense and security company with an enduring purpose, to help nations keep their people and society safe. Empowered by its 28,000 talented people, Saab constantly pushes the boundaries of technology to create a safer and more sustainable world. In the U.S., Saab delivers advanced technology and systems, supporting the U.S. Armed Forces and the Federal Aviation Administration, as well as international and commercial partners. Headquartered in Syracuse, New York, the company has business units and local employees in ten U.S. locations.

Saab is a company where we see diversity as an asset and offer unlimited opportunities for advancing in your career. We are also a company that respects each person’s needs and encourage employees to lead a balanced, rewarding life beyond work. Saab values diversity and is an Affirmative Action employer for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. description:

Hybrid | Barcelona or Asturias, Spain | Antwerp or Brussels, Belgium

Creating essential chemistry that the world needs

At Chemours, our people are redefining how the world thinks of chemistry by approaching everything we do with a commitment to delivering Trusted Chemistry that creates better lives and helps communities thrive.

Powered by chemistry, our products are used in applications that make the products we rely on, processes, and new technologies possible. In key sectors such as clean energy, advanced electronics, high-performance computing and AI, climate friendly cooling, and high-quality paints and coatings for homes and industrial infrastructure, sustainable solutions and more modern living depend on Chemours chemistry.

Chemours is seeking an EMEA Product Stewardship & Regulatory Consultant to join our growing Thermal & Specialized Solutions Business Sustainability Team. This position can be based in Barcelona, Asturias, or Brussels and reports directly to the Business Global Sustainability Leader.

As the EMEA Product Stewardship & Regulatory Consultant, you will serve as the bridge between regulatory experts and the business across EMEA. While this role is regionally focused and does not hold global responsibility, it works closely with a global product stewardship and sustainability team to support business objectives and share expertise. You will help translate evolving chemical regulations and sustainability requirements into practical business actions that ensure Chemours products remain compliant, trusted, and commercially successful throughout their lifecycle.

The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following:

As the EMEA Product Stewardship & Regulatory Consultant, you will serve as the bridge between regulatory experts and the business across EMEA. While this role is regionally focused and does not hold global responsibility, it works closely with a global product stewardship and sustainability team to support business objectives and share expertise.

  • Monitor and assess emerging regulatory and sustainability developments impacting the product portfolio.

  • Lead product stewardship reviews and identify emerging compliance risks.

  • Support product sustainability activities for new product development projects.
  • Provide stewardship guidance for management of change (MOC) decisions.
  • Work closely with commercial, technical, sustainability, operations, and product management stakeholders across EMEA.
  • Support implementation of evolving regulatory requirements across the business.

The following is required for this role:

  • Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or another related scientific discipline.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant industry experience.
  • Product Stewardship, Regulatory Affairs, Product Compliance, Chemical Compliance, EHS, or related experience.
  • Experience working within a highly regulated industry.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to translate complex technical and regulatory information into clear business guidance.
  • Strong project planning and coordination capabilities.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a global team.
  • Fluency in English.

The following is preferred for this role:

  • Experience with fluorochemical products or organofluoride chemistries.
  • Knowledge of PFAS-related regulatory developments.
  • Experience with EU REACH, UK REACH, Turkey REACH, or F-Gas regulations.
  • Experience supporting product sustainability programs.
  • Experience working with SAP, Salesforce, or data analytics tools.

POSITION SUMMARY

Responsible for configuration, deployment, testing, maintenance, upgrades, management, monitoring and troubleshooting the enterprise LAN and WAN network components to provide a secure, high performance network. Ensure network stability and operational excellence.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Must have knowledge of internet, computer, routers, switches, firewall, etc., in order to perform network maintenance and system upgrades including service packs, patches, hot fixes and security configurations.

  • Experience with Cisco Enterprise networking solutions, VOIP environments, and advanced understanding of LAN/WAN technologies.

  • Must possess the ability to increase job knowledge through continuing education and/or other professional development opportunities.

  • Strong understanding of network infrastructure and network hardware with the ability to implement, administer, and troubleshoot network infrastructure devices, including wireless access points, firewall, routers, switches, controllers.

  • Able to diagnose, resolve, and document hardware/ software and network problems and provide end user training and support as required.

  • Experience with firewall, intrusion prevention, VPN, and authentication systems.

  • Ability to interact and maintain working relationships with stakeholders and constituents internal/external to the organization to ensure business needs are met.

  • Attend or lead meetings to solicit ideas and/or recommendations for process improvements.

  • Ability to work with all levels of staff within and outside the IT organization.

  • Strong understanding of network security concepts and practice, IP addressing, DNS, DHCP and other common network protocols.

  • Able to quickly learn new or unfamiliar technology and products using documentation and other readily available resources.

  • Strong attention to detail and time management with the ability to prioritize assignments in an organized manner.

  • Must be able to monitor network performance to determine if adjustments are necessary.

  • May be asked to provide specific detailed information for hardware and software selection.

  • Must be able to convey technical, administrative knowledge or complex information to others in nontechnical terms.

  • Must be a self-starter with the ability to work independently and in a team-oriented, collaborative environment; must be dependable, flexible and adaptable to change.

  • Must have excellent interpersonal, listening, oral and written communication skills to present reports, contracts and/or proposals for internal audiences and external organizations.

  • Must be able to provide exemplary customer service.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Normal physical job functions performed within a standard office environment. Reasonable accommodations may be made to individuals with physical challenges to perform the essential duties and responsibilities. Occasionally may be required to lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree with three (3) years of experience in related field.

  • Current and valid Texas driver’s license required for off-site travel.

  • On-call, work hours may extend beyond the regular, eight hours, Monday-Friday, workday, including weekends and holidays to provide immediate support due to system failures on a 24/7 basis.

  • Official transcripts will be required.

  • Bilingual preferred.

*** Will be subject to a criminal background check. Some positions may be subject to a fingerprint check. ***

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Establishes and maintain networking environment by documenting and ensuring system standards.

  • Maximizes network performance by monitoring performance; troubleshooting network problems and outages; scheduling upgrades; collaborating with network architects on network optimization.

  • Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities.

  • Implement systems using procedures consistent with established Dallas College guidelines, industry standards and the Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL), including change control and management.

  • Performs disaster recovery operations and data backups as required.

  • Diagnose, resolve, and document hardware/software network issues for local and remote locations.

  • Configure, manage and maintain firewall, VPN, Identity and authentication systems.

  • Maintain IPAM, DNS and DHCP systems, network load balancer, PKI system and certificates, system logging along with other network related systems and software.

  • Responsible for company domain name registration.

  • Tests and monitors network performance and provides network performance statistics as requested.

  • Confers with diverse IT staff, network users, contractors and vendors within the Dallas College community network in the management of network security solutions.

  • Interact and negotiate with vendors, outsourcers, and contractors to secure network products and services.

  • Coordinate computer network access and use.

  • Responsible for monitoring and assessing the functionality of the network routers, ensuring all internet security software is updated regularly.

  • Responds to incoming notifications via various methods (principally SMS alerts) regarding network connectivity problems and other exceptions.

  • Supports development and implementation of networking projects, prioritizing tasks, meeting deadlines and adhering to allocated budget.

  • Prepares, maintains and adheres to procedures for logging, reporting, and monitoring of statistical network data.

  • Interfaces with an array of stakeholders and constituents within the Dallas College community network daily to ensure district needs are met.

  • Completes required Dallas College Professional Development training hours per academic year.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Incumbents may be directed to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description. Position requires regular and predictable attendance.

Since 1965, Dallas College, formerly Dallas County Community College District, has served more than three (3) million students. title: Granule Line Operator
description:
The Line Operator's position involves monitoring and operating equipment on the product line. Responsibilities include keeping the product within specifications and maintaining high quality - will be required to work with the Quality Assurance department and Drum Operators to accomplish this. Must be able to professionally delegate duties; assist other operators / positions where needed; and assist in the training of personnel. Will identify any maintenance needs on the flake line and communicate this to the Shift Manager and/or shift mechanic.


Position Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Follow the approved Standard Operating Procedures of the flake line to produce products within their appropriate specifications.
  • Assists with the training and direction of personnel who may be assigned to assist on the line for clean-ups and shutdowns, etc.
  • Operates the line to maximize the output of good, finished product with minimal waste.
  • Responsible for starting and stopping the line at appropriate times.
  • Area of responsibility begins at the flume and continues through to the packaged goods area.
  • Ensure the holding tank is kept clean and well maintained. Ensure all other equipment (including the flake slide, knife bars and snifter tubes), floors, and all area of responsibility is kept in a clean and sanitary condition at all times.
  • Directs the periodic clean-ups of all equipment within the area, works with the sanitation supervisor to ensure a thorough cleaning and sanitizing of equipment is successfully completed at regularly scheduled intervals.
  • Take timings, readings, and temperatures hourly and record the results. Make any necessary changes to temperature, etc. so that the quality of the product is maintained. Record in detail all changes and line adjustments in the log book. Records must be legible, accurate, and complete, in English.
  • Properly mix the additive as necessary for the product being produced.
  • Check additive rates at least once an hour, more often as needed. Ensure the correct additive level is added to the mash. Record exact amounts of additives when checked, and record any additive adjustments made. This should be done every time the additives are checked.
  • Log date codes and lot numbers of additive(s) used in the log book.
  • Adjust the knife on the drums so it cuts properly, without exceeding 30 psi. If cutting is difficult, the knife will need to be changed.
  • Work with the QA Lab to ensure the product being produced is in grade and complies with the specifications for the product. Advise the Shift Manager or other appropriate authority if the product is out of grade.
  • Know moisture limits for each product and maintain consistent moisture without exceeding moisture limits.
  • Communicates on a daily basis with other shift Flake Line Operators to assure proper transition between shifts.
  • Keep the yield and peel time as low as possible. Verify with the Drum Operator that all dirty mash is removed.
  • Check the slabber knife and ensure the slice thickness is correct. Verify the slabber knife is cutting cleanly.
  • Follows safe working practices at all times. Abides by all Lock Out, confined space, fall protection and forklift policies. Ensures all safety policies are followed by anyone assigned to the line or assisting with periodic clean-ups.
  • Keeps the shift manager informed of progress and/or problems.
  • Completes all other duties as necessary. Will likely be cross trained on other production lines.

Knowledge and Skills:

  • Knowledge of flake line production policies and procedures to ensure the safety of product and personnel.
  • Ability to give instruction and teach others regarding processes and equipment operation.
  • Ability to complete paperwork and reports; basic math skills needed.
  • Good communication skills, both written and oral.
  • Good time management skills.
  • Good people skills.
  • Ability to monitor self and processes to make improvements or take corrective action.
  • Ability to work well with all levels of staff.
  • Must be safety and quality conscious.

Education:

Education must be of such level as to allow for the accurate reading, writing, calculation and communication of the required materials and instructions to complete the job responsibilities. High school diploma/equivalent or higher education preferred.


Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to stand, bend, sit or move repetitively for up to 12 hours.
  • Must be able to lift on a regular basis up to 50 lbs. without assistance and up to 100 lbs. with assistance.
  • Ability to tolerate dust or chemicals.
  • Ability to work safely around moving parts and equipment.
  • Bending, stretching, lifting, reaching, climbing, crawling, and fingering required. Must be able to see and hear sufficiently to operate equipment safely in an environment with high levels of noise and low-lit areas.
  • Willing to work weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed.

  • Translate business requirements into scalable, practical solutions that deliver operational and financial value.
  • Conduct business analysis, process design, requirements gathering, and solution advisory activities.

  • Communicate effectively with clients, partners, and internal teams through clear written and verbal communication.

What we are looking for:

This role is to partner and support Global Fixed Income, Currency & Commodities Operations (GFICCO) teams and senior leaders to proactively identify, quantify, prioritize, and mitigate risks, improve controls and maintain a focus on operational excellence and sustainable solutions. As a first line of defence team, GMO Risk is responsible for demonstrating, monitoring and managing the effectiveness and adequacy of the risk and control environment in line with the enterprise risk framework supporting responsible growth. GFICCO teams processes include trade control, confirmations and settlements. GMO provides end to end operational support to our clients and business partners day to day in the processing and settling of transactions of cash and securities.

Members of the GFICCO Risk team are trusted advisors to GFICCO functions and leadership by providing independent oversight and assessment of their risk environment. It is our role to strengthen the control environment, improve control culture & practices embedding a robust risk culture across the organisation. We aim to create open channels of communication with GFICCO teams to maintain trust and promote transparency in reporting root cause of issues and escalations.

  • Close interaction and engagement with GFICCO functional leadership to provide guidance on identified risk and control issues, escalation triage, formal capture of audit issues & operational events and development of associated remediation plans

  • Collaborate and debate with Audit, Compliance & Operational Risk partners on findings and emerging themes
  • Ensure compliance with critical deadlines for risk identification, escalation, and remediation

  • Extensive people/stakeholder management skills at all levels of seniority
  • Analytical skills, attention to detail and objective problem solver

  • Experience in connecting with a diverse set of clients to understand future business needs - is a continuous learner

  • Participate in and drive collaborative efforts to advance tools, technology, and ways of working to better serve an evolving client base

UK

title: Assistant Investment Analyst
description:
Assistant Investment Analyst - DFH801

We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the future.

Assistant Investment Analyst - Municipal Credit Research

Position Summary

HIMCO (The Hartford Investment Management Company) is seeking an Assistant Investment Analyst to join the Municipal Credit Research team. This individual will work closely with senior members of the team to identify, analyze, and monitor investment opportunities across the municipal bond market. The role combines fundamental credit analysis, relative value analysis, and the study of economic, political, and public policy developments that influence credit quality and market performance.

This position is well suited for a highly curious, self-motivated individual who is passionate about investing and the intersection of public policy and financial markets. The ideal candidate is eager to develop investment views, challenge assumptions, explore new analytical approaches, embrace AI and workflow automation, and contribute meaningfully to a collaborative research platform.

Job Duties

  • Assist in the fundamental credit research process to evaluate investment opportunities and monitor existing municipal bond holdings
  • Analyze issuer financial statements, budgets, news alerts, economic trends, and political and public policy developments across a variety of municipal sectors
  • Build, maintain, and enhance financial models and analytical tools used to assess credit quality and relative value
  • Conduct independent research on emerging credit themes, market developments, and investment opportunities
  • Participate in issuer meetings, industry conferences, rating agency discussions, and investor calls
  • Assist in preparing investment recommendations, credit opinions, and presentations for portfolio managers and other key stakeholders
  • Identify opportunities to improve research processes, data management, analytical frameworks, and workflow efficiency, especially via AI and workflow automation
  • Collaborate with analysts across sectors and contribute to broader research initiatives within Public Credit Research
  • Network with key stakeholders across the municipal bond market, including issuers, rating agency analysts, and sell side professionals

Technical / Functional Skills & Qualifications

  • Strong academic background with an undergraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Public Policy, Political Science, Government or a related field
  • 0-2+ years of relevant experience in credit research, fixed income investing, public finance, government, or economic research
  • Demonstrated intellectual curiosity in investing, public policy, financial analysis, and economics, and the ability to synthesize information from across these disciplines
  • Understanding of financial statements, accounting concepts, and financial modeling
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills coupled with the ability to think critically and challenge conventional viewpoints
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with AI and workflow automation applications such as CoPilot, Visual Studio Code, and Power Automate a plus
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Self-starter who takes ownership of projects and pursues opportunities with limited direction
  • Team-oriented individual who welcomes debate, values diverse perspectives, and contributes positively to an intellectually rigorous investment environment
  • Progress toward or willingness to pursue the CFA designation a plus

As a condition of your employment for HIMCO, you will be required to affirm to HIMCO’s Code of Ethics and understand that you will be required to comply with the disclosure of accounts, holdings and pre-clearance of trades for the accounts of you and your household family members as more fully described in the Code of Ethics Key Points. If you will be deemed to be a “Covered Associate” under HIMCO’s Pay to Play Policy, you will also need to disclose all political contributions that you have given within the past 2 calendar years.

$80,062 - $94,938
