  • Identifies defects or issues and makes necessary adjustments according to established processes.

  • Prepares completed products for shipment using appropriate protective materials (bracing, padding, strapping) to prevent damage during transport.

  • Maintains a clean, safe, and organized work area, ensuring proper storage of tools and materials. Adheres to all company safety policies and procedures, participates in required safety training, and promptly reports hazards or safety concerns.

  • Performs work both indoors and outdoors, as required, and may be exposed to varying weather conditions depending on the facility.

Nature and Scope

  • Selects correct processes from clearly prescribed rules, past practices, or instruction. Seeks advice and guidance on non-routine or problem areas from supervisor. Deviations from the norm are cleared by the supervisor.

  • Under close supervision, exercises limited latitude/independent judgment. Work typically involves detailed checks or close review of output by a senior coworker and/or supervisor.

  • None.

Work Environment

  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds in a physical environment. Ability to stand for periods of time up to and exceeding 60 minutes. Ability to make repetitive movements, such as using a 10-key or calculator, bending, or squatting.

  • Typically requires overnight travel less than 10% of the time.

  • Performs duties in an outdoor environment with regular exposure to temperature extremes, mechanical equipment, high noise levels, and airborne particulates, necessitating compliance with established safety standards and procedures.

Education and Experience

  • HS Diploma or GED strongly preferred.

  • 0-2 years of experience in area of responsibility.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience reading and interpreting blueprints, shop drawings, work orders, and fabrication specifications

  • Proficiency using measuring instruments such as tape measures, calipers, gauges, and other inspection tools to verify product quality

  • Experience with fabrication equipment and hand tools in a manufacturing, construction, or industrial environment

  • Knowledge of construction, industrial, or building material products and their applications

  • Ability to safely operate forklifts and other material handling equipment; certification preferred

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain quality standards, identify discrepancies, and ensure accurate order fulfillment

  • Demonstrated ability to train, mentor, or provide guidance to less experienced associates

  • Bilingual (Spanish/English) proficiency is a plus

title: Corporate Communications Systems & Design Specialist - The Toro Company
description:
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

Who Are We?

The Toro Company is a homegrown, Minnesota-based company that has been in business since 1914. We pride ourselves on providing world-class equipment to help maintain the environment that we love, while putting an emphasis on giving back to the communities that surround us. From residential lawns and gardens, to venues such as St Andrews Links and Target Field, we are a company with a global footprint and a passion for helping people beautify whatever landscape they may be in. With 100 years of operation under our belt and a healthy tenure, come find out what makes The Toro Company the best place in the Twin Cities to build a career.

As the Corporate Communications Systems & Design Specialist, you will have the opportunity to help shape The Toro Company (TTC) employee experience by combining your expertise in internal communications software, graphic design and writing. You will manage and optimize global internal communications technology platforms by serving as platform administrator, designer, power user and trainer, while also ensuring TTC’s communications are effective, visually engaging, on-brand and aligned with company priorities.

What Will You Do?

In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for:

  • Serve as the primary administrator and subject matter expert for internal communications systems, including intranet, email, digital signage, project management and other digital communication tools.

  • Manage platform governance, user access, workflows, training, content standards and best practices for all digital communication tools.

  • Partner with IT and external vendors on platform enhancements, integrations, upgrades, troubleshooting and ongoing issue resolution.

  • Design digital and print communication materials, including graphics, signage, infographics, templates, PowerPoint presentation assets and campaign materials that align with TTC brand standards.

  • Contribute to the creation of engaging employee-facing content for the intranet, digital signage, email communications and other internal channels.

  • Use analytics, employee feedback and channel performance data to recommend improvements that enhance communication effectiveness, adoption and the employee experience.

  • Evaluate and implement AI-enabled tools and workflows that improve content creation, design, publishing, analytics and communications efficiency.

  • Provide consultative support and training to content contributors and internal clients, helping them develop, maintain and publish effective content across communication platforms.

  • Manage communication templates, media assets, content libraries and publishing processes to ensure channels remain current, useful, consistent and on-brand.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

What Do You Need?

To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, marketing, graphic design, digital media, information systems or related field preferred. Equivalent work experience considered.

  • 5+ years of experience in corporate communications, digital communications, intranet management, content management, graphic design or related fields.

  • Experience administering digital communication platforms, intranets, content management systems or similar technologies.

  • Demonstrated writing, editing and proofreading skills, with the ability create clear, engaging employee-focused content.

  • Strong visual design skills and proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite, including Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.

  • Advanced Microsoft PowerPoint skills, including presentation design, executive presentation support and visual storytelling.

  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365; basic HTML/CSS knowledge and SharePoint experience preferred.

  • Experience using communication analytics, reporting tools and performance metrics to evaluate and improve content and channel effectiveness.

  • Experience with Microsoft Copilot or other AI-enabled workplace tools preferred.

  • Interpersonal, client service, organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

  • Detail-oriented, collaborative and committed to producing high-quality, brand-aligned communications.

What Can We Give You?

At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our employees know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive salary, an affordable and top tier medical/dental/vision plan, 401k, and many other great benefits - The Toro company offers employees at our Bloomington, MN HQ location a variety of perks, including:

  • Dress for your day - We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment.

  • Location – Conveniently located near both St. Paul and Minneapolis, we are centrally located for most commuters!

  • Food - Take advantage of our onsite café, which serves both breakfast and lunch. With a Caribou Coffee attached, you can grab a snack and a coffee at any time during your day.

  • Wellness - The Toro Company’s HQ offers complimentary use of our onsite fitness facility to employees. In addition to physical wellbeing, TTC offers a variety of mental health and financial health resources to all employees.

  • Volunteerism - The Toro Company is proud to provide employees 20 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community.

  • Summer Hours – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at our Bloomington HQ are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday.

  • Flexible Work Arrangements – This team is currently implementing a hybrid work schedule. The opportunity to collaborate in a hybrid way, with some time spent in office and some from home, has promoted team building and flexibility. ​#LI-Hybrid​

  • Competitive Salary – The pay range takes into account skills, experience, education, and location. It is not common to be hired at or near the top of the range; compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the annual pay range is between ​$95,000​ - ​$110,000​. Cash compensation is one piece of our competitive total rewards package. If you need to, you can access your pay early with the dailypay app.

At The Toro Company, we are committed to fostering a secure and trustworthy recruitment experience for our applicants. Recruitment fraud is a growing concern for job seekers, so please be aware that throughout our recruitment process, you’ll never be required to pay any fees or disclose personal financial details when applying to TTC opportunities. All legitimate job opportunities must be applied for directly through our official careers page at jobs.thetorocompany.com or via Workday, our applicant tracking system.

The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. We are committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees.

title: Vice President, Government Relations & Public Policy
description:
Who You Are: (Job Summary)

You are a strategic, pragmatic public policy leader with deep experience navigating complex, multi-jurisdictional policy environments. You understand how European Union institutions, the UK government, and national and regional authorities shape outcomes for large-scale infrastructure investment.

You bring credibility, judgment, and precision to politically sensitive and highly regulated environments. You own and translate policy developments into business-relevant insight and focus relentlessly on outcomes, lowering risk, increasing certainty, and creating durable competitive advantage for QTS.


What You Will Do: (Job Responsibilities)

As VP, Government Relations & Public Policy, you will own and lead QTS’s European government relations and public policy agenda across the European Union, the United Kingdom, and priority regional and local jurisdictions. You will shape policy and regulatory conditions that enable QTS’s European growth strategy, support market entry and expansion, protect development timelines, and reduce risk across major infrastructure investments. Serving as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and as QTS’ senior European representative on public policy matters, you will influence external stakeholders, align closely with Blackstone Government Relations, and orchestrate cross-functional engagement across internal teams.

European & UK Strategy and Advocacy

• Develop and execute QTS’s government relations and public policy strategy across the European Union, the United Kingdom, and relevant national and regional jurisdictions.

• Lead engagement on European and UK initiatives to expand domestic compute capacity, including programs, incentives, and regulatory frameworks designed to accelerate digital infrastructure growth.

• Advocate for QTS priorities before EU institutions, UK government departments and regulators, and national and regional governments in key markets.

• Anticipate and interpret EU directives and regulations, UK legislation, and member state policies related to data center standards, data localization and compute sovereignty, energy markets, water use, permitting, sustainability, taxation, and AI infrastructure.

Policy Development and Thought Leadership

• Lead development of policy positions, briefing materials, consultation responses, and executive communications, particularly on issues tied to European digital infrastructure expansion.

• Provide strategic insight on key policy debates including compute sovereignty, data governance, sustainability requirements, and resource constraints such as power and water availability.

• Translate complex EU and UK policy developments into clear, actionable insights for internal teams and senior leadership.

• Partner with Legal, Energy, Development, Finance, and Economic Development teams to ensure alignment between policy positions and business priorities.

Stakeholder and Relationship Management

• Build and maintain relationships with EU policymakers, UK ministers and officials, national governments, regulators, and regional authorities in priority markets.

• Represent QTS in European and UK trade associations, coalitions, and industry groups, particularly those shaping policy related to digital infrastructure growth, sustainability, and sovereignty.

• Coordinate closely with Blackstone Government Relations to ensure consistent engagement strategies and aligned messaging across shared priorities.

• Manage and coordinate external advisors and advocacy partners across multiple jurisdictions to ensure disciplined, high-impact engagement.

Cross-Functional Integration

• Work closely with internal teams to align European and UK engagement strategies with broader global government relations efforts.

• Support data center development projects by proactively identifying and addressing policy risks and opportunities across EU, UK, and member state frameworks.

• Provide forward-looking analysis on emerging issues, including compute capacity expansion objectives, evolving data center standards, grid constraints, and water resource policy.

Governance and Compliance

• Ensure compliance with lobbying, transparency, and ethics requirements across the EU, UK, and relevant jurisdictions.

• Support internal governance, reporting, and coordination of government relations activities across Europe.

What You Will Need to Be Successful: (Required Qualifications, Education, Experience, Certifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in public policy, government, law, or a related field.
  • Significant experience (typically 13+ years) in government relations, public policy, or regulatory affairs in Europe and/or the United Kingdom.
  • Demonstrated experience advancing policy outcomes in complex, multi-level governance systems.

Other Key Skills: (KSAs)

  • Deep understanding of EU institutional processes and UK legislative and regulatory frameworks.
  • Familiarity with national and regional policymaking across key EU member states.
  • Experience engaging on issues such as digital infrastructure growth, industrial policy, energy and water policy, and data governance.
  • Strong policy judgment with the ability to balance advocacy, credibility, and long-term relationship building.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to brief senior executives with clarity and precision.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.
  • High degree of integrity, discretion, and professionalism.

The duties and responsibilities described here are not exhaustive and additional assignments, duties, or responsibilities may be required of this position. Assignments, duties, and responsibilities may be changed at any time, with or without notice, by QTS in its sole discretion. We provide individuals with disabilities reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment in accordance with applicable law. title: Social Services Director
description:
Healthcare, Dental, Vision

Paid Time Off

Excellent Pay

Your Job

The Social Services Director will be responsible for planning, developing, organizing, evaluating and directing the overall operation of the Social Services department in accordance with the National Association of Social Workers (NASW) Code of Ethics and in compliance with Federal, State, and Local guidelines and regulations, company policies and procedures, and governing agencies. Responsible for fostering a climate, policies and routines that enable residents to maximize their individuality, independence and dignity. This climate should provide residents with the highest practical level of physical, mental and psychosocial well-being and quality of life. Responsible for identifying psychosocial, mental and emotional needs along with providing, developing, and/or aiding in the access of services to meet those needs.

Qualifications

• One year of supervisory social work experience in a healthcare setting working directly with geriatric individuals.

• Minimum of 2 years of nursing experience in a Skilled Nursing Facility preferred.

Principal Responsibilities

• Plans, organizes, implements, evaluates, and directs a comprehensive Social Services program.

• Assist the Social Service Consultant in the planning, developing, organizing, implementing, evaluating, and directing of the social service programs of the facility; Participates in reviewing and setting policies concerning resident care and quality of life; Participates in developing facility social work policies.

• Prepares Social Services department for annual survey.

• Works with Social Services staff, interdisciplinary team, and administration to promote and protect resident rights and the psychological well-being of all residents/residents. Prevents and addresses resident/resident abuse as mandated by law and professional licensure.

• Completes social history and psychosocial assessment for each resident that identifies social, emotional, and psychological needs; Completed relevant parts of the minimum data set (MDS); Utilizes the minimum data set to guide the care plan.

• Maintains accurate and timely documentation which complies with federal/state regulations, The Company Corporate policy, and specific center practices, including, but not limited to, Advanced Directives, Minimum Data Set, Social Service History and Assessment, Raps, Care Plans, Social Service Progress Notes, Behavior Tracking, monitoring of cognitive and psychosocial changes, PASARR and Discharge Planning documentation, and psych services.

• Supports each resident’s/resident’s right to self-determination; Documents resident/resident refusal of services offered; Informs resident/resident of any therapeutic alternatives to the refused service; Involves others, as appropriate, to help educate the resident/resident about the alternatives.

• Participates in the development of a written, interdisciplinary plan of care for each resident that identifies the psychosocial needs/issues of the resident, the goals to be accomplished for those needs/issues, and the appropriate social worker interventions.

• Ensures or provides therapeutic interventions to assist residents in coping with their transition and adjustment to a long-term care facility, including their social, emotional, and psychological needs.

• Ensures or provides support and education to residents/family members/significant others to assist in their understanding of placement and facility issues in addition to referring them to the appropriate social service agencies when the facility does not provide the needed services.

• Coordinates the resident discharge planning process and make referrals for appropriate home care services prior to the resident’s return to the community.

• As part of interdisciplinary care team, identifies discharge teaching needs; Communicates with center team members the estimated discharge date and updating Point Click Care; Makes referrals as needed for post discharge care to appropriate agencies and suppliers.

• Initiates and participates in completion of Discharge Transition Plan & Discharge packet materials and orienting the resident/resident and family around the process.

• Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or assigned at any time with or without notice.

description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the national security space (NSS) enterprise. DSG is unique at Aerospace as it not only directly supports major customers, including the U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, Air Force Materiel Command, and senior leadership at the Pentagon, but also provides a broad range of technical support across the national space enterprise, maintaining vertical responsibilities with customers’ portfolios as well as horizontal, matrixed responsibilities across the corporation. Additionally, DSG provides deep technical expertise to the Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) in the conception, design, acquisition, launch and operations of satellite, launch vehicle, ground control, and range systems.

The Sr. Systems Engineer (SE) in the Responsive Space Branch within the Agile Acquisition Directorate (AAD) will support the program office acquiring a critical space system for the Space Rapid Capabilities Office (RCO). The Space RCO is rapidly developing and fielding highly classified critical space capabilities for the space enterprise. The Sr. SE will actively participate in all phases of a system lifecycle to ensure an operationally dominant space capability is delivered at the speed of warfighting relevance. This role will also be responsible for Aerospace reach-back and backplane activities.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at Kirtland Air Force Base.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Support program reviews, design, development, test, and transition to operations efforts

  • Act as principal technical representative directly supporting Program Manager (O-5)

  • Understand and ensure implementation of requirements for system design, mission concept of operations, prototype and test, initial checkout, operations, and operational transition support

  • Provide mission assurance and assist with integration efforts

  • Witness critical test efforts, verifying procedures and plans are followed appropriately

  • Support integration and test anomaly investigations, providing key expertise in protecting schedule, cost, and hardware

  • Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills; experience presenting and writing technical information

  • Travel is required (10-25%)

  • This position requires a current TS/SCI security clearance with SAP eligibility, which is issued by the US Government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

  • Past demonstration of Aerospace’s Leadership Competency Model elements: leading change, operating strategically, fostering innovation, delivering results, and engaging with impact

Our unmatched transaction volumes provide differentiated, data-driven perspectives that help our clients achieve their most critical goals. To learn more about Houlihan Lokey, please visit HL.com.



Corporate Finance

The Houlihan Lokey Corporate Finance business has extensive expertise in mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, activist shareholder and takeover defense, and other related advisory services for a broad range of clients. In addition, we have the proven ability to engineer and execute financing solutions that are essential for growth and success and offer access to financing in the public and alternative capital markets through the issuance of debt, equity, or hybrid securities. In EMEA, we work with a wide spectrum of companies, from middle-market privately owned enterprises to large multinational organizations. With a growing platform of Corporate Finance professionals and offices across the region, in addition to our global reach and in-depth knowledge across a broad range of industries, we have the breadth and targeted expertise to provide exceptional client service.



Please note that we are currently only looking for candidates who are available to start work from March 2027 onwards. Houlihan Lokey's Amsterdam office offers 3-month internships throughout the year, so if these timings are not suitable for you, we would ask that you look at our other opportunities to find a position that works with your schedule.

Throughout the year, Houlihan Lokey offers 3-month internship opportunities at their Amsterdam office. The internship is an excellent opportunity to work alongside investment bankers in a stimulating environment on various M&A, Debt, or Equity advisory assignments for clients in various industries.

As an intern, you will have the opportunity to gain valuable on-the-job training. Throughout your internship you will get similar levels of exposure as a first-year analyst, assisting in the preparation of materials for clients and conducting market, industry, and company analyses. Furthermore, you will gain experience in financial modelling, valuation analyses, and supporting the due diligence processes.

Basic Qualifications

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with fluency in both English and Dutch (additional language skills are also advantageous)

  • You must either be an undergraduate, in your final year of study, or studying for a Masters, and still, be in full-time education during your internship

  • You will have a strong academic track record and must be studying for, or achieved, a degree in accounting, economics, and or finance

  • Have an understanding of valuation theory, methodologies, and applications

  • Strong quantitative, financial, and analytical skills

  • A demonstrated interest in M&A

  • Previous internship experience within investment banking and /or related fields is desirable

Preferred Qualifications

  • International experience is also desirable, but not essential

Houlihan Lokey aims to attract talented students who share our passion for excellence and commitment.

The opportunity

Hitachi Energy is a leader in high-voltage technology, offering a wide range of high-voltage products up to 1,200-kilovolt (kV) for AC and 1,100-kilovolt for DC. We help to enhance the safety, reliability and efficiency of power networks while minimizing environmental impact with following primary offerings for switchgears, circuit-breakers, generator circuit breakers, power quality products, surge arresters, disconnectors, instrument transformers and high-voltage service.

Join Hitachi Energy and work in a team that is dedicated to creating a future where innovative digital technologies allow greater access to cleaner energy.   • Identify supply chain risks and implement recovery plans to minimize project impacts.

title: Vice President, Health & Wellness
description:
Zeno Group is the fiercely independent and global, integrated communications agency, born from PR. We bring together the boldest and brightest talent to help clients across industries and sectors unleash the power of strategic communications. Guided by our "Fearless Pursuit of the Unexpected," we push the boundaries to achieve real business value and societal impact for clients. Winner of the industry’s most coveted awards including the 2024 PRWeek U.S. Outstanding Large Agency of the Year, 2023 PRWeek Purpose Agency of the Year, 2022 PRWeek Global Agency of the Year, 2022 PRovoke Best Large Agency to Work For in North America and a three-time winner of PRWeek’s Best Places to Work. Zeno has also been previously recognized by the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. Zeno is a DJE Holdings Company.

Job Description:

Vice President, Health & Wellness

Do you thrive at the intersection of healthcare, business strategy and communications? Are you energized by helping organizations navigate complex healthcare environments, build trust with stakeholders and develop integrated communications strategies that deliver meaningful business impact?

As a Vice President, Health & Wellness at Zeno Group, you will lead integrated communications programs and senior client relationships across biotech, consumer health, medical devices and other areas of healthcare. Working closely with executive stakeholders, agency leadership and cross-functional teams, you will develop strategies grounded in deep industry expertise, business priorities and evolving stakeholder expectations.

This is an opportunity for a senior communications leader to shape high-impact client programs, deepen and grow client partnerships, develop talent and contribute to the continued growth and evolution of Zeno's Health & Wellness practice.

About the Role:

  • Health Communications Strategy & Executive Counsel: Serve as a trusted advisor to senior executives and communications leaders, developing integrated strategies that connect business priorities, stakeholder needs and reputation considerations to measurable outcomes.

  • Industry Expertise & Strategic Leadership: Apply deep knowledge of healthcare markets, regulatory considerations and emerging trends to help clients navigate complex business and communications challenges and identify new opportunities.

  • Integrated Communications Leadership: Lead complex, integrated programs across disciplines and geographies, bringing together earned, digital, social, creative, data and other capabilities to deliver cohesive client solutions.

  • Client Growth & Business Development: Deepen senior client relationships, identify opportunities to expand engagements and lead organic growth and new business efforts that contribute to the continued growth of the Health & Wellness practice.

  • Financial & Operational Leadership: Oversee account performance, forecasting, profitability, staffing and resources while balancing client needs, team effectiveness and sustainable business growth.

  • Team Leadership & Talent Development: Lead, mentor and develop senior and emerging talent while fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment where people can learn, grow and do their best work.

  • Practice Development & Innovation: Help advance Zeno's Health & Wellness capabilities by identifying emerging client needs, developing new approaches and bringing forward perspectives on the trends shaping healthcare and communications.

About You:

  • 15+ years of experience in public relations, communications or related fields within an agency or similar environment.

  • 8+ years of experience in Health & Wellness communications.

  • Proven success leading complex healthcare communications programs and senior client relationships within regulated environments.

  • Deep understanding of biotech, pharmaceutical, consumer health and/or medical device sectors, including market dynamics, stakeholder expectations and emerging industry trends.

  • Ability to translate complex scientific, business and regulatory information into clear strategies and compelling narratives.

  • Demonstrated success counseling senior executives and building trusted, long-term relationships with client stakeholders.

  • Experience leading integrated communications strategies and cross-functional teams across disciplines and geographies.

  • Proven success growing client relationships, expanding scopes of work and leading new business efforts.

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience managing budgets, forecasting, profitability and account performance.

  • Exceptional writing, storytelling and presentation skills, including experience leading executive-level presentations and new business pitches.

  • Proven leadership experience, including mentoring, developing and supporting senior and emerging talent.

  • Collaborative leadership style with the ability to build alignment, navigate evolving priorities and bring diverse teams together around shared goals.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading integrated healthcare programs across earned, digital, social, creative, data and other communications disciplines.

  • Experience counseling organizations through significant business, regulatory, reputation or transformation moments.

  • Experience contributing to healthcare practice development, thought leadership or capability innovation.

  • Familiarity with emerging technologies, data and AI-enabled approaches shaping healthcare communications.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Healthy, happy employees make Zeno better, so we have programs that support physical, mental and financial wellness. Our culture and benefits are designed to promote flexibility, celebrate diversity and support work/life balance. title: Data Protection Lead - Contract
description:
Data Protection Lead - Contract


Location: London, Bristol or Manchester (Hybrid)

Contract Length: 6 Months

Day Rate: £600.00 - £650.00

IR35 Status: Inside IR35

Security Clearance: BPSS


AgileSource are seeking experienced Data Protection Leads to join a growing Data Governance function supporting major digital transformation programmes within government. The successful candidates will operate at a senior level, partnering with product, engineering, architecture and business stakeholders to embed privacy-by-design principles across complex digital services and data-driven initiatives.


This is a highly collaborative role requiring strong technical understanding of data protection within digital environments, alongside the ability to influence senior stakeholders and enable programme delivery while effectively managing privacy risk.


Key Responsibilities


  • Provide expert data protection and privacy advice across large-scale digital transformation initiatives.
  • Embed Privacy by Design principles into product development, technology delivery and operational processes.
  • Work closely with developers, software engineers, architects and delivery teams to ensure privacy requirements are understood and implemented effectively.
  • Conduct and review privacy risk assessments and advise on mitigation strategies.
  • Support data sharing initiatives and ensure appropriate governance controls are in place.
  • Engage confidently with senior leaders and stakeholders, presenting recommendations and risk positions clearly.
  • Balance compliance obligations with delivery objectives, positioning data protection as an enabler rather than a blocker.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of the wider Data Governance and Data Protection function.
  • Operate independently across multiple workstreams while collaborating effectively with colleagues across the organisation.


Essential Skills & Experience


  • Significant experience in a senior Data Protection, Privacy or Information Rights role.
  • Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and wider data protection legislation.
  • Experience supporting large-scale transformation or digital programmes.
  • Proven experience working within technical environments alongside developers, engineers and data architects.
  • Demonstrable experience embedding Privacy by Design into digital products and services.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including engagement with senior leadership teams.
  • Ability to work effectively in ambiguous and fast-moving environments.
  • Experience developing pragmatic, risk-based solutions that support delivery outcomes.


Desirable Experience


  • Experience within Central Government, Civil Service or wider public sector organisations.
  • Experience supporting digital product delivery teams.
  • Data sharing governance experience.
  • Broader understanding of information security principles (although this is not a security-focused role).
  • Microsoft 365 proficiency.

title: Nutrition Education Associate
description:

Job Description

About Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service – EFNEP

The Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP) is a flagship initiative of Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, funded by USDA’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) since 1969. EFNEP serves young families and youth with limited resources across Texas—those most at risk for hunger, food insecurity, and lacking access to community support systems. Through locally delivered, evidence-based nutrition education, EFNEP empowers families and youth to make lasting improvements in diet quality, healthy habits, and overall well-being.

EFNEP classes are taught by paraprofessional educators, many of whom are bilingual, ensuring culturally relevant, accessible instruction both in person and virtually. Adult and youth programs utilize research- and practice-tested curricula, available in English and Spanish. Adult education focuses on nutrition, physical activity, food resource management, food safety, and food security, while youth education covers MyPlate, food groups, food safety, and physical activity, all aligned with Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS) standards.

EFNEP collaborates with schools, faith-based organizations, housing authorities, shelters, parenting programs, and a variety of local agencies to identify and reach families in need. By partnering with these organizations, EFNEP is able to build strong, lasting community relationships and deliver impactful education where it is needed most. With data showing that 21% of Texas families with children under 18 live below the poverty level, EFNEP’s mission is vital to communities across the state.

EFNEP is delivered through county extension offices located in ten urban communities: Bexar, Cameron, Dallas, El Paso, Fort Bend, Harris, Hidalgo, Nueces, Tarrant, and Travis Counties.

Working for EFNEP means joining a dedicated team committed to improving health outcomes for Texas families and youth. Staff members receive training, resources, and support to help empower participants with practical skills for healthier living. If you are passionate about nutrition education, community outreach, and creating meaningful change, consider becoming part of Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s EFNEP team.

Position Information

This position works in the Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program known as EFNEP. The Nutrition Education Associate, with training and supervision, teaches (in-person and/or virtually) about nutrition, food resource management, food safety, and physical activity in culturally sensitive and appropriate ways for adults and/or youth, for low-income audiences in various community locations.

This position is funded by a Federal grant and is therefore contingent upon availability of funds.

Note to Candidates: This position will start on or after October 19, 2026.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

The following are the functions essential to performing this job.

  • Recruits adults and/or youth who meet program guidelines.

  • Uses research-based, approved educational materials to instruct youth and/or adults either in-person and/or virtually.

  • Prepares food for recipes and instructs youth and/or adults through food demonstrations.

  • Collects and tracks program data.

  • Assists in mentoring and/or training Nutrition Education Assistants when needed.

Knowledge, Abilities, & Skills

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred.

  • Proficient computer skills – Microsoft Office programs – Word and Power Point; Excel, etc.

  • Working knowledge of Zoom and/or Microsoft Teams to conduct virtual lessons.

  • Ability to communicate effectively with adults and/or youth.

  • Ability to follow a curriculum including teaching and speaking publicly, strong communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently, be self-motivated and give attention to detail and maintain accurate records.

  • Ability to keep written logs of activities, complete reports, and organize materials.

  • Familiar with the community where the position is located.

Education & Experience

  • High School diploma or GED, additional education is not considered an advantage.

  • Six months of related experience working with youth and/or adult audiences.

  • Experience with low resource audiences and working cooperatively with support systems, networks, and agency programs available for low-income people/low resource audience.

  • Knowledge or teaching experience related to nutrition, food safety, food resource management and physical activity topics, guidelines, and best practices.

  • Experience teaching groups of people.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

  • Must be willing to work necessary hours to fulfill job responsibilities (some evenings and weekends). Hours worked will not exceed 40 per week.

  • This position will require daily travel to multiple work sites in county. Must be willing to travel to required trainings outside of county.

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service – EFNEP does not provide transportation and the position requires access to reliable transportation. The agency will follow applicable policies if personal vehicle is used, which may include reimbursement at a pre-established rate.

  • Must be able to lift, carry, and/or otherwise move instructional materials weighing up to 40 lbs from vehicle to work site and from work site to vehicle.

Preferred Registrations, Certifications, and Licenses:

  • Valid driver’s license.

  • Current liability insurance.

What You Need to Know

Salary: $18.71/hour

Position Funding: This position is grant funded and availability is contingent on grant funding.

Why Work at Texas A&M AgriLife?

When you choose to work for Texas A&M AgriLife, you become part of an organization that is an established leader in agriculture and life sciences with a wide range of capabilities to meet the needs of our statewide, national, and international constituents.

In addition, Texas A&M AgriLife offers a comprehensive benefit package including the following:

  • Health, dental, vision, life and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M AgriLife contributing to employee health and basic life premiums

  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays

  • Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month

  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas

  • Employee Wellness Initiative for Texas A&M AgriLife

Applicant Instructions

Applications received by Texas A&M AgriLife must either have all job application data entered or a resume attached. Failure to provide all job application data or a complete resume could result in an invalid submission and a rejected application. We encourage all applicants to upload a resume or use a LinkedIn profile to prepopulate the online application.

All positions are security-sensitive. title: Principal AI Architect
description:
About Invoka Consulting


Invoka Consulting partners with clients across all industries and around the world to design, implement, and optimise innovative SaaS and AI solutions that deliver measurable business impact. We are an Elite Smartsheet partner, OpenAI and an Anthropic partner.


Our AI work is already in production, not on a roadmap. We have automated a regulatory compliance process for a national sporting body that now assesses every case in hours rather than weeks, we run daily AI workloads inside a global pharmaceutical business, and we have built our own Model Context Protocol server for Smartsheet with roughly ten times the tool surface of the public one.


We are now expanding our AI practice.


Overview of the Role


We are looking for a Forward-Deployed Principal AI Architect to serve as the technical anchor of Invoka's AI practice. This is a hands-on role. You will spend your time designing and building production AI systems, embedded with enterprise clients, and turning what we learn on each engagement into reusable capabilities.


We do not believe enterprise AI works when it is specified from the outside and handed over. Our delivery model puts engineers inside the client's business to understand how the work genuinely runs across departmental seams, and then to build against that reality. You will be the person who proves that model works, and the person who sets the standard everyone hired after you is measured against.


Alongside the delivery work, you will own our AI architecture standards, our evaluation and reliability practices, and our accelerator framework: the reusable components, prompt libraries and integration patterns that turn one-off projects into repeatable delivery. You will lead technical pre-sales on our most complex opportunities, and you will set the technical bar for the AI roles we hire in the UK and other geographies.


This is a role for someone who wants ownership. You are joining a practice early enough to shape what it becomes, with real enterprise clients to build for from day one.


Key Responsibilities


Architecture and Technical Standards


  • Design and sign off the solution architecture on AI engagements, working within Invoka's Responsible AI framework.
  • Establish and own our evaluation, testing and reliability standards for AI systems, so that performance is measured rather than assumed.
  • Set the technical standards, patterns and documentation practices the AI practice delivers against.
  • Stay at the frontier across Anthropic, OpenAI and Microsoft, and translate capability changes into delivery capability and commercial offerings.


Building and Embedded Delivery


  • Build production AI systems hands-on: agents, tool use, retrieval pipelines, MCP integrations and enterprise workflow connectors.
  • Embed with client teams to map how work actually runs across functions, then design and deliver against it.
  • Lead the delivery of a flagship cross-functional workflow end-to-end, as the reference case for the practice.
  • Act as the escalation point for complex technical issues on live engagements.


Capability and Intellectual Property


  • Own and productise Invoka's AI delivery IP: the accelerator framework, reusable components, prompt libraries and evaluation suites.
  • Take our in-house MCP servers from internal tools to supported, documented, sellable asset, and own its roadmap.
  • Develop our temporal data and change analysis capability, which we deliver as a service inside client engagements, where it intersects with the AI practice.


Pre-Sales and Client Engagement


  • Lead technical pre-sales on complex and high-value opportunities: discovery sessions, solution shaping, technical scope and feasibility.
  • Own the technical narrative in front of Director, VP and C-suite stakeholders, including sceptical security and legal functions.
  • Contribute to proposals, RFP responses and Statements of Work, ensuring what we sell is what we can deliver.


Practice and Team Development


  • Set and hold the technical bar for AI delivery hires: define the interview process, assess candidates, and mentor the engineers who join.
  • Write the technical onboarding for our Poland delivery hub, launching next year.
  • Contribute to case studies, technical writing and partner assets that build Invoka's reputation in the market.


Required Skills and Experience


  • Production AI systems you have actually shipped. You have designed, built and deployed LLM-based systems that run in production with real users, uptime expectations and sensitive data. We will want to talk about who uses them, how often, and what broke.
  • Evaluation and reliability engineering. You can explain how you measure whether a non-deterministic system is working, and how you would know six months later that it had degraded. Evaluation design, regression suites, golden datasets, failure taxonomies, guardrails and human review loops are familiar territory.
  • Model Context Protocol at authoring depth. You have written or substantially extended MCP servers, or equivalent agentic tool frameworks. We already run MCP servers in production, so we need someone who can extend, productise and maintain them.
  • Enterprise integration, security and data governance. Deep experience connecting AI to enterprise platforms, and fluency in what a CISO and a legal team will actually ask about data residency, PII handling, authentication and boundary crossing.
  • Python or TypeScript to a professional standard. Readable, tested, documented code.
  • Reusable assets, not just projects. You have built IP inside a consulting or product environment and understand that unversioned, undocumented work is not an asset.
  • Enterprise client presence. Credible and comfortable with Director, VP and C-suite stakeholders. You can explain an architecture to a sceptical CISO and a cost model to a CFO in the same meeting. Clear writing matters here as much as clear speaking.
  • Genuine appetite for embedded delivery. You are willing and able to sit with a client's operations team, learn how their work really runs, and build inside their world rather than at arm's length.


Nice to Have


  • Smartsheet development experience: API, Bridge, Data Shuttle. This is the intersection where much of our AI work sits.
  • Temporal or slowly changing dimension data modelling.
  • Multi-vendor fluency across Anthropic plus OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot or Azure OpenAI. Our advisory work is deliberately tool-neutral.
  • Experience in regulated sectors: pharmaceuticals and life sciences, financial services, or public sector.
  • Technical leadership of offshore or nearshore engineering teams.
  • Published technical writing, conference speaking, or open source contributions.


What the First Year Looks Like


  • First 90 days. Embedded as technical lead on a live enterprise engagement. Architecture standards and the evaluation framework documented and in use. Named technical lead on live proposals.
  • First six months. Your first accelerator shipped and reused on a second engagement, with the delivery time saving measured. A flagship cross-functional workflow delivered end-to-end. Owning the technical interview process for the AI team.
  • First twelve months. An accelerator library that measurably reduces delivery effort on repeat work. Architecture sign-off embedded across the practice. The technical onboarding written for our offshore hub. A track record of enterprise work won with you as the named technical lead.


Perks and Benefits

  • Equity participation.
  • Performance-related bonus.
  • Employer-paid private medical and Dental insurance.
  • Monthly employer pension contributions.
  • 25 days paid holiday plus 8 UK bank holidays plus your birthday off.
  • 1 additional paid Volunteer Day annually to support community initiatives.
  • Certification and conference budget, including Anthropic, OpenAI and Microsoft partner programme training.
  • Direct access to Anthropic, Microsoft and Smartsheet partner teams and roadmaps.
  • A supportive, collaborative and ambitious team environment, with the autonomy that comes from being early into a practice.


Initial screening for this role is being managed by our third-party recruitment partner, AES. Successful candidates will be contacted by AES, and all interviews are conducted by Invoka's leadership team.

title: Senior Scientist I - Quality Control - Data Review
description:
Senior Scientist I - Quality Control - Data Review

Position Summary:

  • Shift: M-F 8am-5pm
  • Location: Madison, WI

Catalent’s Madison, Wisconsin site is a state‑of‑the‑art biologics development and manufacturing facility supporting customers from research through early‑ and mid‑stage clinical production. Located at 726 Heartland Trail in Madison, the approximately 102,700‑square‑foot GMP facility specializes in mammalian cell line engineering, drug substance biomanufacturing, and biopharmaceutical development, utilizing flexible single‑use systems to enable rapid scale‑up and customization. The site is home to Catalent’s proprietary GPEx® and GPEx® Lightning technologies, which are used to generate high‑yielding mammalian cell lines for biologic therapies, and supports production scales ranging from 50 to 4,000 liters for clinical manufacturing. Following a $45 million expansion announced in 2025, the Madison site has significantly increased capacity, added new equipment, and created approximately 200 highly skilled biohealth jobs, further strengthening its role within Catalent’s global biologics network and Wisconsin’s growing life sciences ecosystem.

We have an opportunity for a Senior Scientist I - Quality Control - Data Review to join our team. In this role, you will execute and document cGMP Quality Control testing with precision. You will operate equipment, review analytical data, and ensure compliance with SOPs. You will also contribute to technical documentation and support laboratory operations in a collaborative environment.

The Role:

  • Review a variety of different tests
  • Review and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
  • Perform monthly routine checks of logbooks within the lab
  • Ensure adherence to protocols and methods
  • Follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Good Documentation Practices (GDP)

  • Assist with training of junior staff

The Candidate:

Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.

title: Director of Concrete Restoration & Building Envelope Operations
description:
The Director of Concrete Restoration & Building Envelope Operations, holds full operational ownership of Spire Building Solutions' project portfolio, leading project teams that deliver commercial concrete restoration and building preservation solutions across the region. Accountable for the complete performance of the regions enterprise, its people, its projects, its financial results, its client relationships, and its safety and quality outcomes, from preconstruction through closeout.

The role pairs executive-level judgment with hands-on concrete restoration, waterproofing, repair and building envelope operational command. The Director builds and leads a durable, enterprise-grade bench of Project Managers, Foremen, and site personnel; protects schedule and margin across the portfolio; serves as the senior operational point of accountability to internal leadership and external stakeholders; and embodies Spire's custom, process-driven approach to restoration, innovation, and transformation in every project and relationship.

Regional Portfolio Oversight

  • Hold end-to-end accountability for every active and pipeline project in the portfolio, ensuring each is delivered on schedule, within budget, and to Spire's restoration and preservation standards.
  • Balance and prioritize resources, labor, equipment, and management attention, across concurrent projects to optimize portfolio-level throughput, utilization, and profitability.
  • Establish and enforce consistent operating standards, processes, and reporting cadences across all project teams so performance is predictable, repeatable, and scalable.
  • Anticipate and resolve cross-project conflicts, bottlenecks, and risks before they affect cost, schedule, safety, or client confidence.
  • Partner with sales, estimating, and preconstruction to maintain a healthy, well-sequenced pipeline and a clean handoff of awarded work into operations.

Team Leadership & Management

  • Lead, direct, and develop multiple project teams, setting clear expectations, goals, and accountability for Project Managers, Superintendents, and Foremen.
  • Provide day-to-day operational direction and decision-making support to project leadership, removing obstacles and making the calls that keep work moving in the field.
  • Conduct regular performance reviews, field coaching, and mentorship to raise the capability and consistency of the entire regions operations organization.
  • Foster a culture of ownership, craftsmanship, accountability, and continuous improvement aligned with Spire's process-driven model.

Financial Management & Portfolio P&L

  • Hold profit-and-loss accountability for the regions portfolio, protecting and improving margin across all active projects.
  • Review and approve project budgets, forecasts, labor and equipment plans, and cost-to-complete projections; intervene early where performance diverges from plan.
  • Drive change-order identification, pricing, and approval so that scope changes and unforeseen conditions are captured, monetized, and integrated into budget and schedule.
  • Manage portfolio-level cost controls, labor productivity, equipment utilization, rentals, procurement, and subcontractor spend, to meet or exceed financial targets.
  • Partner with finance and accounting on billing, cash flow, work-in-progress, and revenue recognition for the regions work.

Client Engagement & Relationship Management

  • Serve as the senior operational relationship owner for regional clients, owners, associations, property managers, architects, and engineers.
  • Build and sustain trusted, long-term client relationships that drive repeat work, referrals, and Spire's reputation across the Regional market.
  • Lead high-stakes client communication, expectation-setting, issue resolution, and escalation across the portfolio.
  • Represent Spire's brand promise of custom, process-driven restoration in every client interaction and at every project milestone.

Staffing, Personnel Decisions & Talent Development

  • Own workforce planning for the region, forecasting staffing needs against the project pipeline and ensuring each project is correctly resourced and crewed.
  • Make hiring, assignment, promotion, corrective-action, and termination decisions for the operations team, in coordination with the VP of Operations and Human Resources.
  • Recruit, onboard, and retain a strong regional enterprise team of Project Managers, Superintendents, Foremen, and skilled site workers capable of self-performing concrete restoration and building preservation work.
  • Build career pathways, cross-training, and succession depth so the region can scale without sacrificing quality, safety, or continuity.
  • Champion certification, licensing, and ongoing technical development across the workforce (OSHA, scaffold and aerial-lift competencies, and trade-specific skills).

Quality & Safety Leadership

  • Own quality and safety outcomes across the entire portfolio, setting the standard and holding every team accountable to it.
  • Ensure full compliance with OSHA, jurisdictional, and Spire safety requirements; champion a zero-incident culture on every job site.
  • Enforce Spire's workmanship, quality, and building-preservation standards through inspections, mockups, and disciplined field oversight.
  • Drive corrective action and root-cause resolution on quality and safety issues, ensuring lessons learned are captured and standardized across teams.

Project Lifecycle, Preconstruction Through Closeout

  • Engage early in preconstruction, participating in estimate and scope review, constructability assessment, scheduling, staffing, and risk planning for awarded work.
  • Ensure clean mobilization, execution, and progress management across all phases of each project.
  • Oversee procurement, subcontractor selection, submittals, mockups, and schedule integration at the portfolio level.
  • Drive disciplined closeout across every project, documentation, punch resolution, final deliverables, client handoff, and warranty.

Reporting & Stakeholder Communication

  • Provide regular, accurate operational and financial reporting to the VP of Operations and executive leadership, portfolio status, schedule, cost, risk, safety, and forecast.
  • Maintain disciplined documentation and data integrity within Spire's systems of record (Procore, Sage, Microsoft Project, and CRM).
  • Keep internal stakeholders, executive leadership, estimating, finance, HR, and sales, informed and aligned with portfolio realities.
  • Keep external stakeholders, clients, design teams, authorities having jurisdiction, and subcontractors, updated, aligned, and confident.
  • Translate field reality into clear, decision-ready information for leadership and clear, confidence-building updates for clients.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • 10+ years of progressive construction operations experience, including multi-project or portfolio leadership in commercial restoration, concrete repair, waterproofing, facade, or building envelope work.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing teams of Project Managers, Superintendents, and field crews across concurrent projects.
  • Strong P&L and financial management capability at the portfolio or business-unit level.
  • Deep technical knowledge of self-performed concrete restoration, waterproofing, masonry, coatings, sealants, and building preservation work.
  • Proven client-facing leadership with owners, associations, property managers, and design professionals; Regional market relationships strongly preferred.
  • Proficiency managing within Procore, Sage, Microsoft Project, and CRM and reporting tools.
  • OSHA-30 required (OSHA-500 preferred); First Aid / CPR; working knowledge of motorized, suspended, and fixed scaffolds and aerial lifts.
  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or related field preferred, or equivalent experience.
  • Ability to travel throughout the Assigned region and to project sites as operational needs require.

title: Salesperson
description:
Job Description

What is a Salesperson?

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives. The role has good knowledge of store systems, basic automotive system knowledge and basic part knowledge. The role has the basic ability to source from stores, hubs, pdq, and external suppliers. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and maintenance processes. Position can be part time or full time. Fleet safety certification preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent selling experience for DIY customer visits and phone calls
  • Achieve personal sales goal and help store achieve its sales goals
  • Provide DIY services including battery installation, testing, wiper installs, etc.
  • Maintain store product and operational standards
  • Responsible for inventory processes including truck put away, shoot outs, cycle counts, Back stock, etc.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Store Cleanliness including floors, bathrooms, facing, dusting, parking lot
  • General stocking including truck stocking and back stock
  • Safely deliver parts to customers as needed

Success Factors

  • Basic driving and navigation ability
  • Ability to use delivery board system
  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Operating inventory systems and store equipment
  • Parts and automotive system knowledge skills
  • Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Expert at testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY service

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Salesperson

  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and management
  • Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, parts catalogs, and procedure manuals
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

  • 2-3 years of successful sales experience in a diverse retail environment, providing superior customer experiences

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: Program Administrator (Corrections Education)
description:
Description


View the complete description on our Jobs page.




The State Board for Community and Technical Colleges (SBCTC) is seeking to fill the recently vacated position of Program Administrator of Corrections Education.

This position will serve as a member of the leadership team providing statewide coordination and technical assistance for correctional education programs.These programs include basic skills, vocational, associate and bachelor's degrees, transitional educational reentry services and other agreed upon educational programs offered by sixteen community and technical colleges in partnership with the Department of Corrections at the ten adult correctional facilities.

This position reports to the Associate Director for Corrections with the focus of scaling equitable access to educational opportunities for justice-involved individuals across the community and technical college system.

Headquartered in Olympia, Washington, remote or hybrid work arrangements may be considered.


Duties

  • Provide support, guidance, and monitoring of Corrections Education Navigators to ensure understanding of and compliance with the SBCTC/DOC Corrections Education Agreement.
  • Facilitate collaboration between Corrections Education Navigators, DOC Navigators, and reentry center representatives to support continuity of services.
  • Identify strategies and design projects that deliver innovative, evidence-based professional development for Corrections Education Navigators.
  • Provide technical assistance and support to staff, faculty, and Corrections Education Deans and Directors.
  • Support colleges in reaching enrollment and completion goals in Adult Basic Education.
  • Collaborate with SBCTC colleagues and system stakeholders to reduce racial equity gaps across the community and technical college system, particularly by increasing access to college and supporting the success of students of color and other minoritized student groups.
  • Coordinate and plan professional development opportunities for corrections education representatives.
  • Collect, analyze, and apply program data to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and strengthen program outcomes.
  • Manage the Corrections Education web page.
  • Collaborate with relevant work groups focused on services for corrections education students.
  • Serve as a member of the Basic Education for Adults (BEdA) team, attending department meetings and following department processes and requirements.
  • Perform various activities to support the Associate Director for Corrections

Qualifications

  • Education and Experience

    • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education and experience.
    • Experience developing strategic partnerships and collaborating effectively with college and community partners.
    • Experience managing multiple activities and projects to successful completion.

    • Experience with education delivery platforms and the ability to provide technical support.

    • Education and Experience

  • Skills and Competencies

    • Excellent project management skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
    • Ability to work collaboratively, think creatively, act resourcefully, and communicate effectively in writing and orally.
    • Proven ability to lead with an equity mindset, think creatively and strategically, and act with cultural awareness and humility.
    • Demonstrated ability to develop and deliver equity-centered professional development and trainings.
    • Proficiency with the principles of Guided Pathways and concepts of advising.
    • Understanding of financial aid opportunities and access processes.

    • Ability to work, problem-solve, and collaborate remotely in a technology-rich environment.

  • Additional Requirements

    • Required to pass a Department of Corrections security background clearance.
    • Required to have a valid driver's license.
    • Required to be available for travel both in-state and out-of-state.

Supplemental Information

HOW TO APPLYInterested candidates may apply by submitting the following items:

  • Letter of formal application that addresses your interest in the position and ability to perform the responsibilities described in this announcement.
  • Detailed résumé of all educational and professional experience that demonstrates how you meet the qualifications.
  • List of at least three professional references with contact information. References are typically contacted after interviews.

Prior to a new hire, a background check including criminal record history may be conducted. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant's suitability and competence to perform in the job.

title: Senior Ground Systems Engineer
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Systems Engineering Division (SED) offers unparalleled expertise in systems engineering to the U.S. government and various public and private agencies, universities, nonprofit organizations, consortia, and commercial companies involved in the advanced development and application of space systems. From systems CONOPs and architecture development to system design and analysis, mission assurance, cost and schedule assessment, and economic market analysis, SED leverages a vast array of engineering and business disciplines across a diverse and dynamic portfolio of space programs and national challenges spanning the total space system lifecycle.

The Ground Systems Engineering Department (GSED) transforms innovative ground system concepts into operational realities. As trusted leaders in ground systems engineering, we deliver operationally focused solutions for space enterprise C3 systems, mission management, PNT, SATCOM, launch operations, and SIGINT missions supporting Space Systems Command, the National Reconnaissance Office, and the Intelligence Community. GSED leads ground systems and modernization efforts while leveraging deep technical experience and operational expertise to enable mission success across the space enterprise. We are seeking a Senior Ground Systems Engineer to join our team and contribute to the advancement of critical space ground infrastructure and help shape the future of space enterprise ground systems.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in Chantilly, VA.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Analyze and recommend innovative solutions for ground system requirements, software design, acquisition strategies, operations, and sustainment

  • Establish and implement Agile and DevSecOps development methods and metrics for ground system software modernization

  • Define comprehensive space-to-ground and ground-to-ground integration plans, including requirements verification and cross-disciplinary coordination with spacecraft systems and flight software teams

  • Design and develop mission-critical interfaces (organizational, physical, functional, hardware/software, operational) for space ground control systems

  • Lead and manage engineering teams by defining technical tasking, monitoring deliverables, and ensuring quality of engineering studies, recommendations, and analyses

  • Develop and analyze system requirements for engineering models, simulations, test beds, special test equipment, and end-to-end integration testing

  • Provide expert technical guidance to government customers on complex ground system engineering challenges

  • Apply operational experience and technical expertise to influence future ground system architectures and capabilities

What You Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements for the Senior Ground Systems Engineer:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science or mathematics

  • Minimum 12 years’ experience with multiple aspects of space ground systems experience such as enterprise integration, space vehicle to ground integration, ground systems development, and new technology insertion into existing systems

  • Demonstrated technical leadership and strong interpersonal skills required for interacting with peers, internal and external customers, and contractor representatives

  • Experience with requirements development, traceability, and validation methodologies

  • Experience with enterprise-level testing and integration of complex systems, including test planning and execution campaigns, test artifact review, and Independent Verification & Validation (IV&V) processes

  • Experience with ground system operations, sustainment, and integration of mission applications with processing platforms and network infrastructures

  • Must have demonstrated the ability to clearly define technical tasks, form and lead technical teams

  • Experience supporting government acquisition strategies, pre-solicitation efforts, and source selections

  • Ability to work across mission and program boundaries to identify common challenges and formulate recommendations

  • Experience with mission processing systems, constellation tasking and optimization, or space data transport (SDT)

  • Knowledge of modern satellite constellation architectures and distributed space systems

  • An active Top Secret/SCI clearance

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Advanced degree in engineering, science or mathematics

  • Experience with SIGINT and GEOINT mission systems and processing from multiple aspects of space systems integration, such as space-ground-user integration, payloads to spacecraft bus, spacecraft bus integration, ground software to hardware development and new technology insertion into existing space applications (e.g., system requirements, system integration and testing, spacecraft subsystems, manufacturing, test, and/or spacecraft operations

  • Demonstrated experience of Agile and DevSecOps programs

  • Experience with Ground as a Service (GaaS) models, cloud-native ground architectures, or commercial ground service implementations

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

(Min - Max)

$151,300.00 - $226,900.00

Pay Basis: Annual

Leadership Competencies

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

  • Operate Strategically
  • Lead Change
  • Engage with Impact
  • Foster Innovation
  • Deliver Results

Ways We Reward Our Employees

During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

  • Comprehensive health care and wellness plans

  • Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation

  • Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options

  • 401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Variable pay program for exceptional contributions

  • Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career

  • An inclusive work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect

We are all unique, from various backgrounds and all walks of life, yet one thing bonds all of us to each other—the belief that we can make a difference. This core belief empowers us to do our best work at The Aerospace Corporation.

title: Finance Performance Analyst
location: United States of America - Illinois - Chicago
description:
