description:
Job Title

Professional Counselor I

Agency

Texas A&M University - Kingsville

Department

Student Health & Wellness

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Kingsville, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

About Texas A&M University–Kingsville

Texas A&M University–Kingsville (TAMUK), the oldest institution of higher learning in South Texas and a proud member of the Texas A&M University System, stands as the region’s premier university. TAMUK offers the widest range of academic programs and degrees in South Texas, provides exceptional learning and residential facilities, conducts impactful research, awards substantial scholarships, and has awarded more than 80,000 degrees in the institution’s 100-year history. The university is recognized for its unwavering commitment to student success, meaningful research, and deep community engagement. With a welcoming campus culture and strong regional partnerships, TAMUK offers faculty and staff a unique opportunity to make a lasting difference in the lives of students and the broader South Texas region.

Location: The University is located in historic Kingsville, a friendly, safe city of 25,000 that is the home of the legendary King Ranch. Corpus Christi and its beaches are just 40 miles to the northeast, and the border with Mexico is 120 miles to the south at Brownsville or 119 miles to the west at Laredo.

For more information, click here.

Position Overview

The Professional Counselor I is an entry-level counseling position designed for emerging mental health professionals seeking to build clinical expertise in a supportive, collaborative university environment. Working under general supervision, the Professional Counselor I provides personal, academic, career, and substance use counseling services to students while developing advanced skills in assessment, crisis intervention, outreach, consultation, and program development.

This position offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on student success, well-being, and retention through individual and group counseling, wellness promotion, crisis response, and campus collaboration. The Professional Counselor I works closely with experienced counseling professionals and contributes to a culture of care, resilience, and student-centered support.

The ideal candidate is passionate about helping students thrive, committed to professional growth, and comfortable working in a dynamic environment that occasionally requires evening, after-hours, and weekend responsibilities to support student needs and university programming.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Clinical Counseling Services

  • Provide personal counseling and crisis intervention services to individuals, couples, and groups.

  • Provide academic, career, alcohol, and other drug counseling to individuals and groups.

  • Conduct assessments and administer, score, and interpret psychological tests and inventories as appropriate.

  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation, counseling records, referrals, and case management activities.

  • Participate in an after-hours crisis intervention on-call rotation and respond to urgent student mental health concerns as needed.

Consultation and Collaboration

  • Serve as a resource to students, faculty, and staff regarding student mental health, academic concerns, career development, and substance use issues.

  • Consult with university stakeholders regarding students who may benefit from counseling or supportive interventions.

  • Respond to inquiries regarding counseling services, programs, policies, and available resources.

  • Establish and maintain collaborative relationships with campus departments and community partners to strengthen student support services.

Outreach, Education, and Prevention

  • Design, coordinate, and facilitate psychoeducational programming focused on mental health, wellness, resilience, and student success.

  • Develop and deliver presentations, workshops, and trainings for students, faculty, staff, and campus organizations.

  • Assist with outreach initiatives, awareness campaigns, and educational programming that promote mental health and well-being across campus.

  • Develop educational materials and support classroom, conference, and community presentations.

  • Demonstrate flexibility in scheduling and participate in occasional evening and weekend presentations, outreach events, and special programs.

Supervision and Student Development

  • Assist in the mentorship and daily guidance of counseling practicum students.

  • Co-facilitate case consultation, supervision discussions, and educational training opportunities for practicum students.

  • Support the development of future counseling professionals through collaborative learning and professional role modeling.

Research, Assessment, and Program Enhancement

  • Participate in applied research, assessment, and program evaluation initiatives that support continuous improvement of counseling services.

  • Contribute to the dissemination of research and evaluation findings through presentations, publications, or other professional activities.

  • Assist in the development and enhancement of counseling center programs and services.

Administrative and Organizational Support

  • Assist with departmental operations, projects, and administrative responsibilities as assigned.

  • Support strategic initiatives and organizational goals that advance Counseling Center and university objectives.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Other Duties as Assigned

  • The above represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Education – Master’s degree in Counseling and Guidance, Social Work, Counseling, Clinical Psychology, or related specialty.

  • Experience – Practical/field placement relevant to college counseling or supervised experience.

Required Licenses and Certifications

  • Passed the National Counselor Exam (NCE)

  • Eligible for LPC‑Associate, LPC, LMFT, LMSW, or LCSW

  • Must maintain licensure for continued employment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Two or more years of post‑graduate clinical experience in a university or college counseling center

  • Experience providing crisis intervention and participating in after‑hours/on‑call rotations

  • Experience working with wide-ranging student populations, including first‑generation students, veterans, and historically underrepresented groups

  • Experience conducting outreach, psychoeducation, and wellness programming

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Clinical competency in multicultural counseling

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others

  • Adherence to ethical principles and state laws

Other Requirements

Other Requirements and Factors

  • This position is security sensitive

  • This position will require export-control authorization prior to starting employment.

  • This position requires compliance with state and federal laws/codes and Texas A&M University System/TAMU policies, regulations, rules and procedures

  • All tasks and job responsibilities must be performed safely without injury to self or others in compliance with System and University safety requirements

  • This is an entry-level professional counseling position that provides opportunities for clinical growth, mentorship, and professional advancement.

  • Standard work hours are primarily weekday business hours; however, flexibility is required to meet student and departmental needs.

  • Occasional evening and weekend work is required for outreach initiatives, workshops, presentations, special events, and university programming.

  • Participation in an after-hours crisis intervention on-call rotation is required.

  • May be called upon to assist with urgent situations outside of regularly scheduled work hours.

  • Opportunity to receive LPC-S supervision, when available, at no additional cost to the employee, supporting professional licensure and career advancement.

  • Access to ongoing professional development, clinical consultation, training, and mentorship opportunities.

  • Eligibility for wellness programs and incentives offered through Texas A&M University-Kingsville Human Resources, supporting employee health, well-being, and work-life balance.

  • Opportunity to work within a collaborative, student-centered environment committed to excellence in mental health care and student success.

Why Join the Javelina Nation?

Texas A&M University–Kingsville offers a supportive, mission-driven culture focused on excellence in teaching, research, and service. All employees enjoy:

  • A welcoming campus community

  • Opportunities for professional development

  • Competitive benefits through the Texas A&M University System

  • A rewarding experience of helping students achieve their academic and career goals

Shared Values: TAMUK employees uphold the Shared Values of Care, Integrity, Pride, Innovation, and Excellence, which form the foundation of the University’s culture and guide its strategic plan. More information on TAMUK’s Strategic Plan and Shared Values can be found here.

4DX: TAMUK employees actively engage in Franklin Covey’s 4 Disciplines of Execution (4DX) activities within their departments. TAMUK utilizes 4DX as the framework for pursuing strategic goals by creating a culture of high performance. This requires participation from all faculty and staff. More information on 4DX can be found here.

Caring Campus: TAMUK employees embody the Institute for Evidence Based Change’s Caring Campus mindset, maintaining a collegial and caring attitude towards students and each other to foster student engagement and a positive, collaborative work environment. More information on Caring Campus can be found here.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation: Commensurate with experience

Texas A&M University-Kingsville offers a career filled with purpose and opportunity in addition to competitive wages. In addition to base pay, TAMUK provides eligible employees a comprehensive Total Rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, professional growth, and financial security.

BENEFITS (rules, policies, eligibility apply)

With our generous benefit package, robust professional development opportunities, strong retirement programs, and dedication to service excellence, TAMUK is a truly engaging and rewarding place to work.

Insurance:

    • $0 - $30 per month for Employee Only coverage after university contribution ($920 value).

    • Up to 83% of premium covered by the university:

Additional Information

A federal proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Texas A&M University-Kingsville will not pay this fee. In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbott issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B petitions unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if sponsorship for employment visa status is required now or in the future, this moratorium may affect the university’s ability to employ the selected final candidate. TAMUK will adhere to applicable regulations regarding visa opportunities.

Application Instructions

title: Senior Claims Specialist - Workers Compensation
description:
Be Here. Be Great. Working for a leader in the insurance industry means opportunity for you. Great American Insurance Group's member companies are subsidiaries of American Financial Group. We combine a "small company" culture where your ideas will be heard with "big company" expertise to help you succeed. With over 30 specialty and property and casualty operations, there are always opportunities here to learn and grow.

At Great American, we value and recognize the benefits derived when people with different backgrounds and experiences work together to achieve business results. Our goal is to create a workplace where all employees feel included, empowered, and enabled to perform at their best.


This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

Who We Are

Strategic Comp is a leading provider of workers' compensation insurance for large employers committed to protecting their workforce. As part of Great American Insurance Group, we combine the strength and stability of a trusted organization with more than 150 years of history with the entrepreneurial spirit of a growing business.

Through our specialized insurance expertise and field-based service model, we build lasting partnerships and deliver exceptional results for our customers. Our culture is built on collaboration, excellence, and a shared commitment to serving our customers and one another.

Position Summary

Strategic Comp is seeking an experienced Senior Claims Specialist to manage Kansas and Missouri workers' compensation claims. This role is responsible for investigating claims, determining compensability, establishing reserves, negotiating settlements, and developing strategies that drive effective claim resolution.

We take an extremely aggressive and proactive approach to claims adjusting and are looking for the person who not only knows their jurisdiction’s comp laws, but also enjoys the role of putting that experience to good use. Because we focus on outcomes and not just processes, we look for the adjuster who is very skilled at developing strategies to bring claims to resolution. This is a remote position that requires working Central Time Zone business hours. Candidates may work from any state in the US.

Responsibilities

  • Manage Kansas and Missouri workers' compensation claims from inception through resolution.
  • Analyze claim facts and evaluate coverage, compensability, and benefits eligibility.
  • Develop and execute strategies to achieve timely and favorable claim outcomes.
  • Establish and maintain appropriate claim reserves.
  • Negotiate settlements and bring about claim resolution.
  • Communicate regularly with claimants, insureds, employers, and other stakeholders.
  • Prepare and present large loss reports to internal and external audiences.
  • Collaborate with defense counsel on litigation strategy and claim resolution.
  • Partner with medical case managers, surveillance vendors, and other external resources.
  • Ensure compliance with Illinois workers' compensation laws and regulations.
  • Maintain accurate and timely claim documentation.
  • Analyze claim trends and exposure to support effective decision-making.
  • Provide exceptional service while building strong relationships with customers and business partners.

Qualifications

  • Generally, 10+ years of Kansas and Missouri workers' compensation claims adjusting experience, including complex or high-exposure claims.
  • Strong knowledge of Kansas and Missouri workers' compensation laws, regulations, and claims practices.
  • Professional industry designations such as Associate in Claims (AIC) are preferred.
  • Ability to work Central Time Zone business hours and travel occasionally as needed.
  • You must be a great communicator, in both written and verbal form, and be able to work with a variety of internal and external contacts.

Business Unit:

Strategic Comp


Salary Range:

$100,000.00 -$115,000.00

Benefits:

We offer competitive benefits packages for full-time and part-time employees*. title: Sr. Data Scientist
description:
Function

Finance

Our Company

We’re Hitachi Vantara, the data foundation trusted by the world’s innovators. Our resilient, high-performance data infrastructure means that customers – from banks to theme parks ­– can focus on achieving the incredible with data.

If you’ve seen the Las Vegas Sphere, you’ve seen just one example of how we empower businesses to automate, optimize, innovate – and wow their customers. Right now, we’re laying the foundation for our next wave of growth. We’re looking for people who love being part of a diverse, global team – and who get excited about making a real-world impact with data.

Job description

In order to be considered, please submit your resume in English

The Team

Hitachi Vantara is looking for a Sr. Data Scientist to join its Global Analytics & Decision Sciences (GADS) team. Being a part of the Hitachi Vantara Finance Organization, this team connects the dots across multiple business functions to drive growth, enable data-driven decision-making, and solve complex business problems.

In this role, you will collaborate with a broad range of internal stakeholders, including and not limited to services, sales, marketing, product management, finance, pricing, and partner operations, as well as key business owners and stakeholders across multiple levels and functions within the organization. You will work with diverse data sources to analyze business problems, translate insights into action, and support executive decision-making.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform computer-aided quantitative and statistical analysis using advanced tools and scientific modeling techniques in support of the organization’s global strategies. The candidate must demonstrate strong attention to detail and data quality, along with the ability to adapt quickly in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

The Role

  • Collaborate with business stakeholders and cross functional teams to understand enterprise-wide analytical needs, frame key questions, translate requirements into actionable data and analytics solutions, and align objectives and measurable outcomes.

  • Provide thought leadership in advanced analytics, including statistical analysis and descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive modeling, to solve complex business challenges and shape analytical strategy.

  • Synthesize insights across multiple business dimensions, including financial performance, forecasts, products, geography, industries, competitive landscape, and customer segments, to drive data-driven decision-making and strategic direction.

  • Design and develop scalable data and analytics solutions using programming languages (e.g., Python, SQL), data platforms (e.g., SQL Server, Oracle), cloud technologies (e.g., AWS), and visualization tools (e.g., Power BI).

  • Apply advanced statistical and quantitative techniques, including high complexity predictive modeling, to develop data driven solutions and deliver actionable, fact-based insights.

  • Evaluate and utilize current and emerging technologies to identify trends, enhance analytical capabilities, and deliver innovative solutions and recommendations.

  • Lead cross functional projects and programs, communicating complex analytical findings through clear and concise presentations to management and executive audiences.

  • Drive adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) by leading initiatives, establishing best practices, and scaling capabilities across the team.

  • Mentor and develop junior team members in advanced analytics and data science practices and provide regular updates and insights to management.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Data Science, Quantitative Economics, Marketing Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field; Master’s degree with relevant professional experience preferred.

  • Minimum of 5+ years of experience as a Data Scientist or in a similar analytical, quantitative, or technical role.

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights.

  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, with hands-on experience in data engineering, data wrangling, feature engineering, and scalable data processing.

  • Experience with statistical analysis and machine learning techniques (e.g., regression, hypothesis testing, dimensionality reduction, predictive modeling, and data mining) to generate actionable business insights.

  • Experience working with diverse data sources, data platforms, and reporting/analytics tools (e.g., SQL Server, Denodo or similar technologies).

  • Experience with Cloud platforms, including storage, querying, and advanced analytics (AWS, GCP or Azure).

  • Strong data visualization and storytelling skills, with proficiency in tools such as Power BI and advanced Excel.

  • Strong understanding of data modeling principles, ML libraries and best practices.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and thrive in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to explore and leverage new data sources, tools, and methodologies to improve analytical capabilities and business outcomes.

  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience working across diverse teams and stakeholders.

  • Advanced English proficiency.

title: Lead Computer Vision Engineer
description:
Biometric Systems Lead


About iProov


iProov provides science-based biometric solutions that enable the world’s most security-conscious organisations to streamline secure remote onboarding and authentication for digital and physical access. Our award-winning liveness technology and iSOC offer unmatched resilience against deepfakes and generative AI threats while ensuring effortless, scalable user experiences. Trusted by leading governments and enterprises, including the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.K. Home Office, GovTech Singapore, ING, and UBS, iProov sets the standard in biometric identity assurance.


This global trust is built not only on our technology but on the strength of the people behind it. For us, diversity at iProov is about reflecting the customers we serve, holding the principles of equality and inclusion at the heart of everything we do and all that we stand for, embracing differences, creating possibilities, and growing together. We aim to foster a culture where individuals of all backgrounds feel confident in bringing their whole selves to work, feel included, and their talents are nurtured, empowering them to contribute fully to our purpose.


The Role


Reports to: VP, Biometric Operations

Location: WeWork Waterloo, London - Hybrid (At least once per week)

Comp: £90,000 to £100,000 (Base) + Company Performance Bonus (10%) + Share Options + UK iProov Benefits


The Biometric Systems Lead owns how iProov's biometric platform evolves, from research and prototyping through to production. Reporting to the VP, Biometric Operations, you'll lead the Biometric Systems function; scoping and delivering new systems, improving existing ones, and making sure they hold up against the measures that matter (precision, recall, bias, speed, cost and robustness). Bias detection sits with you, alongside the feedback-code work that shapes how real people interact with the technology, and the customer-specific features that arrive as awkward problems and need turning into workable solutions.


It's a varied, cross-functional role, spanning Biometric Operations, Product, Research and CSI, with a longer-term roadmap to build and a team to mentor. We're hiring first for collaboration, communication and mentoring, technical enough to earn the team's trust, and dependable enough that you can be handed a problem and trusted to come back with a solution.


How you can make an impact


  • Work with the Biometric Operations & Product teams to identify areas to improve the Biometric Platform
  • Own the research, prototyping, and productionalization of new Biometric systems and improve upon existing functionality;
  • Scoping of work items
  • Metrics for project success
  • Ensure work stays on track, and be aware of key design decisions that are being made
  • Raise key decisions, and risks to project delivery to the Head of Biometric Platform and Product
  • Ensure systems are effective, and meet expectations (Precision, recall, bias, speed & cost, robustness)
  • Work with the CSI team to ensure teams code quality
  • Lead and Guide Cross functional projects
  • Work with Research team to understand and take ownership of new technologies and methods
  • Build a roadmap for longer term strategic initiatives, meeting the current and future biometric needs of our customers
  • Mentor and support the Biometric Systems team
  • Delegate effectively, ensuring the team is motivated and understands the tasks assigned to them.
  • Ensure the team have the time and resources to be able to do their work efficiently and to a high standard
  • Support the team in their career and learning goals


What we would like to see from you


  • Experience in ML/Computer Vision
  • Python, Docker, OpenCV, sklearn, pytorch/tensorflow, Github, Claude Code
  • Can understand complex systems

title: Compliance Counsel, Commercial Franchise Business Partner
description:

title: Bomb Tech (Game Operator)
description:
The Company

BEAT THE BOMB is the next generation of immersive group entertainment, where customers step into real-life video games. We use an innovative digital, interactive game system to reimagine the intersection of technology and human social connection. In our classic Mission experience, teams wearing hazmat suits go through a series of interactive game rooms, including a laser maze, before facing the World's Largest Paint, Slime, and Foam Bomb! Our original Brooklyn location opened in 2018. We now have locations in Atlanta, Washington D.C., Philadelphia, Charlotte, Houston, and Denver. We've hosted over 500,000 players including hundreds of corporate team building outings, school groups, and non-profit organizations. Beat The Bomb is one of the highest rated experiences in all 5 markets. We offer a full range of special event services including STEM Camps, Kid and Adult Birthday parties, Corporate Tournaments, and Bachelorette parties. We also have a virtual team building platform called Beat The Bomb Virtual, serving remote teams across the globe. Our #1 goal is to ensure every player has a BLAST!

The Charlotte Location

Located on the border of the South End and LoSo neighborhoods of Charlotte, this is our Company's 5th location. The 10,000+ square foot location offers our classic Mission experiences with glass-walled bomb rooms blasting teams with Paint, Foam and Slime; 4 immersive arcade lounges ('Game Bays'); street food and a full selection of beer, wine, cocktails & signature slushies @ The Bomb Bar; a beer garden with sports viewing; and dedicated private event spaces for large groups.

title: Cabinet Estimator and Contractor Account Coordinator - Hartson Kennedy
description:
The Cabinet Estimator and Contractor Account Coordinator supports cabinet projects from initial plans and specifications through quotation, inside sales follow-up, cabinet order entry, order coordination, and job-site delivery. This role reviews project documents, prepares accurate material estimates and quotations, follows up on open quotes and contractor leads, converts approved quotations and customer purchase orders into accurate cabinet orders, coordinates order requirements and releases, and schedules deliveries based on project readiness.

Cabinet product and estimating training will be provided. The ideal candidate will bring strong numerical aptitude, attention to detail, customer communication skills, learning agility, and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Responsibilities

  • Review architectural drawings, cabinet layouts, elevations, specifications, scopes of work, and customer requests to identify project requirements.
  • Perform cabinet takeoffs and determine cabinet types, sizes, quantities, accessories, panels, trim, hardware, and related materials.
  • Prepare and revise accurate estimates, quotations, and supporting documentation in accordance with company pricing, margin, and documentation standards.
  • Provide inside sales support by following up on open quotes, contractor leads, customer inquiries, and pending approvals to help move opportunities through the sales pipeline.
  • Maintain accurate quote, lead, follow-up, customer contact, and opportunity status information in company systems, CRM tools, spreadsheets, or shared trackers.
  • Verify measurements, product selections, finishes, delivery requirements, assumptions, exclusions, and customer approvals before quotations or orders are released.
  • Identify missing, conflicting, or unclear information and obtain clarification from contractors, customers, or internal stakeholders.
  • Review customer purchase orders against approved quotations and resolve discrepancies before order entry or release.
  • Convert approved quotations and customer purchase orders into accurate cabinet orders, ensuring products, finishes, quantities, pricing, ship-to details, and delivery requirements are complete before release.
  • Coordinate order entry, order changes, additions, shortages, replacements, and other project requirements through completion.
  • Maintain current product, pricing, freight, lead-time, estimating, order, and project information in company systems and files.
  • Maintain project schedules and monitor critical milestones, including quote follow-up, approvals, order release, manufacturing, and delivery.
  • Provide proactive updates when schedules, requirements, commitments, approvals, or delivery plans change.
  • Coordinate delivery dates with customers, contractors, operations, and transportation personnel, confirming job-site readiness before dispatch.
  • Verify delivery address, site contact, access restrictions, unloading requirements, staging location, delivery sequence, and required equipment.
  • Sequence deliveries by project phase, building, unit, floor, or installation schedule when required.
  • Assist with resolving shortages, damage, incorrect material, failed deliveries, and other delivery-related issues.
  • Balance customer service needs with sales follow-up, production capacity, inventory availability, and transportation efficiency.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Two or more years of experience in construction, building materials, manufacturing, customer service, project coordination, logistics, inside sales, or a related environment.
  • Strong mathematical, numerical, and spatial-reasoning ability.
  • Ability to read dimensions and learn to interpret plans, elevations, schedules, and specifications.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Working proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and common business systems.
  • Ability to organize multiple active projects, prioritize work, and meet firm deadlines.
  • Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record if job-site visits are required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Cabinet, millwork, countertop, building-products, or construction experience.
  • Experience reading architectural plans or performing material takeoffs.
  • Familiarity with cabinet design, estimating, ERP, CRM, or project-management software.
  • Experience working with general contractors, multifamily contractors, installers, property managers, or builders.
  • Experience coordinating deliveries to active construction sites.
  • Associate degree or technical coursework in construction, design, drafting, business, or a related field.

title: Systems Director - Propulsion Systems
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the national security space enterprise. DSG is unique at Aerospace as it not only directly supports major customers, including the U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, Air Force Materiel Command, and senior leadership at the Pentagon, but also provides a broad range of technical support across the national space enterprise, maintaining vertical responsibilities with customers’ portfolios as well as horizontal, matrixed responsibilities across the corporation. Additionally, DSG provides deep technical expertise to the Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) in the conception, design, acquisition, launch and operations of satellite, launch vehicle, ground control, and range systems.

In the Vulcan Development and Operations (VDO) subdivision of DSG, we are seeking a Systems Director for Propulsion Systems. In this role, you will lead staff providing propulsion expertise to the US Space Force in procuring and assuring Vulcan space launches within the national security space launch (NSSL) program. Vulcan employs three propulsive cycles, each reliant on specialty design, unique materials and impeccable production and operation. Fortunately, you’ll be leading an FFRDC team with deep analytical and laboratory reach in each of these areas. You will ensure technically sound and objective assessments are provided, including actionable recommendations, within appropriate timelines and budget allocations. You will work with other managers in VDO to set strategy and achieve goals. And you will build, mentor, and sustain a team that provides technical depth and FFRDC unique capability while working closely with military, civilian, and contractor staff. The Vulcan rocket has been assigned the most exciting, unique, and critical launch missions. We seek someone to lead the team that ensures those missions can defy gravity to reach space.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in Los Angeles AFB in El Segundo, CA.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Lead the department providing expertise on development, production, and operation of Vulcan’s booster and upper stage propulsion systems
  • Perform day-to-day management of department activities and personnel, and matrixed support from Aerospace’s Engineering and Technology Group (ETG)
  • Build and maintain strong, interdisciplinary teams, working closely with Program Office customers to ensure customer satisfaction
  • Promote staff development and mentor Program Office and ETG personnel
  • Act as interface between staff, USSF SSC customer, launch vehicle contractor, and the NRO Office of Space Launch
  • Mentor new Space Force officers to help them gain familiarity with technical processes and tasks associated with technical analysis disciplines
  • Effectively communicate status and progress of management and technical activities, issues and accomplishments through written reports and presentations to Aerospace, Government customers, and contractor teams
  • Provide realtime support for tests, training, and launch of Vulcan missions
  • Interact frequently and work closely with Aerospace management team

What You Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements for Systems Director - Engineering Program Management and Systems Engineering:

  • Bachelor of Science Degree in engineering or related technical discipline from a recognized institution
  • 12 or more years of experience, relevant to launch vehicle propulsion, in at least one of the following technical areas: cryogenic liquid rocket engines, cryogenic system design and operation, solid rocket motors, rocket engine/motor structural design/materials, turbomachinery or hydraulic design/analysis/test
  • Experience in leadership of multi-disciplinary teams, including matrixed support
  • Experience with project management and development (including budgets), demonstrated ability to balance technical and programmatic perspectives
  • Experience with mission assurance/success processes and demonstrated ability to apply them in the NSSL program context
  • Ability to travel on a regular basis (approximately once per month)
  • This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance, issued by the US Government. US citizenship is required to obtain a clearance.

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Advanced degree in one of the disciplines identified as relevant to the position
  • Previous line management and personnel development experience
  • Strong interpersonal and team building skills, demonstrated thru work across organizations and up and down organizational levels
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills: ability to present clear, concise briefings and write well-crafted reports and assessments
  • Demonstrated complex problem solving, well-founded technical recommendations
  • Demonstrates enterprise-level perspective with prior Program Office(s) and ETG experience
  • Able to work in high intensity, fast-paced environment with rapidly changing priorities, and highly demanding customer
  • Experience in mentoring and training of peers, team members and/or customers

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

description:
Job Title

Job Description

About Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service – EFNEP

The Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP) is a flagship initiative of Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, funded by USDA’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) since 1969. EFNEP serves young families and youth with limited resources across Texas—those most at risk for hunger, food insecurity, and lacking access to community support systems. Through locally delivered, evidence-based nutrition education, EFNEP empowers families and youth to make lasting improvements in diet quality, healthy habits, and overall well-being.

EFNEP classes are taught by paraprofessional educators, many of whom are bilingual, ensuring culturally relevant, accessible instruction both in person and virtually. Adult and youth programs utilize research- and practice-tested curricula, available in English and Spanish. Adult education focuses on nutrition, physical activity, food resource management, food safety, and food security, while youth education covers MyPlate, food groups, food safety, and physical activity, all aligned with Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS) standards.

EFNEP collaborates with schools, faith-based organizations, housing authorities, shelters, parenting programs, and a variety of local agencies to identify and reach families in need. By partnering with these organizations, EFNEP is able to build strong, lasting community relationships and deliver impactful education where it is needed most. With data showing that 21% of Texas families with children under 18 live below the poverty level, EFNEP’s mission is vital to communities across the state.

EFNEP is delivered through county extension offices located in ten urban communities: Bexar, Cameron, Dallas, El Paso, Fort Bend, Harris, Hidalgo, Nueces, Tarrant, and Travis Counties.

Working for EFNEP means joining a dedicated team committed to improving health outcomes for Texas families and youth. Staff members receive training, resources, and support to help empower participants with practical skills for healthier living. If you are passionate about nutrition education, community outreach, and creating meaningful change, consider becoming part of Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s EFNEP team.

Position Information

This position works in the Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program known as EFNEP. The Nutrition Education Associate, with training and supervision, teaches (in-person and/or virtually) about nutrition, food resource management, food safety, and physical activity in culturally sensitive and appropriate ways for adults and/or youth, for low-income audiences in various community locations.

This position is funded by a Federal grant and is therefore contingent upon availability of funds.

Note to Candidates: This position will start on or after October 19, 2026.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

The following are the functions essential to performing this job.

  • Recruits adults and/or youth who meet program guidelines.

  • Uses research-based, approved educational materials to instruct youth and/or adults either in-person and/or virtually.

  • Prepares food for recipes and instructs youth and/or adults through food demonstrations.

  • Collects and tracks program data.

  • Assists in mentoring and/or training Nutrition Education Assistants when needed.

Knowledge, Abilities, & Skills

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred.

  • Proficient computer skills – Microsoft Office programs – Word and Power Point; Excel, etc.

  • Working knowledge of Zoom and/or Microsoft Teams to conduct virtual lessons.

  • Ability to communicate effectively with adults and/or youth.

  • Ability to follow a curriculum including teaching and speaking publicly, strong communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently, be self-motivated and give attention to detail and maintain accurate records.

  • Ability to keep written logs of activities, complete reports, and organize materials.

  • Familiar with the community where the position is located.

Education & Experience

  • High School diploma or GED, additional education is not considered an advantage.

  • Six months of related experience working with youth and/or adult audiences.

  • Experience with low resource audiences and working cooperatively with support systems, networks, and agency programs available for low-income people/low resource audience.

  • Knowledge or teaching experience related to nutrition, food safety, food resource management and physical activity topics, guidelines, and best practices.

  • Experience teaching groups of people.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

  • Must be willing to work necessary hours to fulfill job responsibilities (some evenings and weekends). Hours worked will not exceed 40 per week.

  • This position will require daily travel to multiple work sites in county. Must be willing to travel to required trainings outside of county.

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service – EFNEP does not provide transportation and the position requires access to reliable transportation. The agency will follow applicable policies if personal vehicle is used, which may include reimbursement at a pre-established rate.

  • Must be able to lift, carry, and/or otherwise move instructional materials weighing up to 40 lbs from vehicle to work site and from work site to vehicle.

Preferred Registrations, Certifications, and Licenses:

  • Valid driver’s license.

  • Current liability insurance.

What You Need to Know

Salary: $18.71/hour

Position Funding: This position is grant funded and availability is contingent on grant funding.

Why Work at Texas A&M AgriLife?

When you choose to work for Texas A&M AgriLife, you become part of an organization that is an established leader in agriculture and life sciences with a wide range of capabilities to meet the needs of our statewide, national, and international constituents.

In addition, Texas A&M AgriLife offers a comprehensive benefit package including the following:

title: Staff Project Manager - Organisational Change and Transformation
description:
Entity:

Technology


Job Family Group:

IT&S Group


Job Description:

Let me tell you about the role:

We are in a constantly evolving world with the rise of AI, geopolitical tensions and changes in energy demand. bp is evolving to a downstream and upstream model to best serve the changing world and within bp, Technology is at the heart of this evolution.

This role provides the opportunity to work alongside Technology leadership to deliver key initiatives that will fundamentally change the way that Technology works at bp supporting the business shift to a Upstream/Downstream model.

There will be the opportunity to work on broad initiatives with high levels of ambiguity. The role will evolve as priorities within the change agenda shift, but the role will maintain a high leadership focus to raise the bar as a Technology organisation.

What you will deliver:

  • Become a trusted advisor to Technology leadership in assignee portfolios

  • Embed changes to ways of working at a Technology portfolio (VP/SVP) level

  • Measurable impact in adoption of tools/processes

  • Methodology to track Technology wide initiatives and impact to specific portfolios

  • Maintain backlog of activities required to ensure Technology leadership success

  • Provide access to specialists and/or provide specialist consulting services to leadership to enable them to achieve their goals

  • Consistent governance structure to give visibility into work

What you will need to be successful (experience and qualifications) :

Required Qualifications & Experience:

  • Strong understanding of technology delivery, digital or physical

  • Experience working in matrixed, global environments with cross-functional teams.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and partner leadership skills.

  • Evidence of leading global change products, projects or programmes with a globally distributed team or interested parties.

  • Demonstrable skill in dealing with ambiguity and handling upwards to senior leadership.

  • Partnering with leadership (VP/SVP/C-Suite) to deliver organisational change

  • Evidence of working Customer back

  • Demonstrable experience of using data to drive decisions and commercial understanding.

Desirable Attributes:

  • 10 years+ work experience

  • Familiarity with transformation frameworks such as Disciplined Agile, SAFe, or similar is a plus.

  • Strategic perspective with the ability to translate vision into executable plans.

  • Experience with organisational change and transformation

  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity in complex environments.

  • Passion for continuous improvement and fostering a culture of innovation, inclusion and high performance.

  • Understanding of bp’s operating model and company structure

  • Evidence of being a committed team player

  • Change Management, Product Management or Programme Management background

  • Change, coaching, agility, project and/or project management qualifications

  • Experience mentoring and coaching others or active membership in employee founded support groups

You will work with:

The Transformation, Analytics and Insights (TAI) team reports directly to the EVP Technology and is distributed globally across US, UK, India and Malaysia. Our team Credo brings us together to ensure that we work as one team together regardless of location. We work to ensure that Technology is an efficient, effective and trusted partner for the bp business. Our activities span from creating tooling to support improved delivery efficiency to supporting transformation activity and mergers & acquisitions. We are tightly coupled across the team to Technology leadership and highly visible within the Technology organization.

Ways of working within the TAI team is a team of trusted advisors working alongside SVPs and VPs to deliver changes to working practices and embedding transformation change. We act as a consultancy, providing short engagements with longer term governance to ensure that initiatives are embedded that may be devised by the wider TAI team utilising a fail fast and scale mental model. We problem solve for our SVPs and VPs, leveraging deep relationships across the TAI team and Technology. The pace is fast and changable; we care deeply about each other, are kind even when it is tough to speak the truth and have each others back.

About bp

Our purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. For over 100 years,

bp has focused on discovering, developing, and producing oil and gas in the nations where we operate. EFNEP serves young families and youth with limited resources across Texas—those most at risk for hunger, food insecurity, and lacking access to community support systems. Through locally delivered, evidence-based nutrition education, EFNEP empowers families and youth to make lasting improvements in diet quality, healthy habits, and overall well-being.

EFNEP classes are taught by paraprofessional educators, many of whom are bilingual, ensuring culturally relevant, accessible instruction both in person and virtually. Adult and youth programs utilize research- and practice-tested curricula, available in English and Spanish. Adult education focuses on nutrition, physical activity, food resource management, food safety, and food security, while youth education covers MyPlate, food groups, food safety, and physical activity, all aligned with Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS) standards.

EFNEP collaborates with schools, faith-based organizations, housing authorities, shelters, parenting programs, and a variety of local agencies to identify and reach families in need. By partnering with these organizations, EFNEP is able to build strong, lasting community relationships and deliver impactful education where it is needed most. With data showing that 21% of Texas families with children under 18 live below the poverty level, EFNEP’s mission is vital to communities across the state.

EFNEP is delivered through county extension offices located in ten urban communities: Bexar, Cameron, Dallas, El Paso, Fort Bend, Harris, Hidalgo, Nueces, Tarrant, and Travis Counties.

Working for EFNEP means joining a dedicated team committed to improving health outcomes for Texas families and youth. Staff members receive training, resources, and support to help empower participants with practical skills for healthier living. If you are passionate about nutrition education, community outreach, and creating meaningful change, consider becoming part of Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s EFNEP team.

Position Information

This position works in the Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program known as EFNEP. The Nutrition Education Assistant, with training and supervision, teaches (in-person and/or virtually) about nutrition, food resource management, food safety, and physical activity in culturally sensitive and appropriate ways for adults and/or youth, for low-income audiences in various community locations.

This position is funded by a Federal grant and is therefore contingent upon availability of funds.

Note to Candidate: This position will start on or after October 19, 2026.

  • Prepares food for recipes and instruct youth and/or adults through food demonstrations

  • Collects and tracks program data

  • Ability to communicate effectively with adults and/or youth.

  • Ability to work independently, be self-motivated and give attention to detail and maintain accurate records.

Education & Experience

  • High School diploma or GED, additional education is not considered an advantage.

  • Experience with low resource audiences and working cooperatively with support systems, networks, and agency programs available for low-income people/low resource audience.

  • Knowledge or teaching experience related to nutrition, food safety, food resource management and physical activity topics, guidelines, and best practices.

  • Experience teaching groups of people.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

title: Data Quality & Research Analyst
description:
UTM Consultants are seeking a detail-oriented Data Quality & Research Analyst for a temporary assignment supporting a critical data normalisation programme across approximately 30 European markets.


This role is well suited to someone with experience in research, data validation, GIS, energy intelligence, planning data or structured data quality assurance.


Key Objective

Review and validate AI-generated wind farm project records, ensuring they are accurate, consistent and ready for ingestion into our intelligence platform.

The focus is on research and quality assurance rather than software development, data science or data engineering.


Key Responsibilities


Data Validation & Quality Assurance

• Review AI-normalised wind farm project records for accuracy and completeness.

• Validate project names and development phases against reliable public sources.

• Check that related developments are clustered correctly.

• Identify duplicate, superseded or obsolete records.

• Flag records that require further investigation.


Research

• Validate project information using planning portals, government energy registries, developer websites, industry publications, mapping tools and GIS sources.

• Investigate ambiguous, incomplete or conflicting information.

• Document findings clearly and maintain robust audit trails.


Data Management

• Apply agreed quality-review classifications consistently.

• Maintain consistent naming conventions across records.

• Escalate complex cases to the Product and Research team.


Process Improvement

• Provide feedback on recurring data-quality issues.

• Identify opportunities to improve AI-assisted review workflows.

• Contribute to QA documentation and procedures.


Essential Skills and Experience

• Excellent attention to detail and a consistent approach to quality.

• Strong desk-based research skills.

• Confidence working with spreadsheets and structured datasets.

• Ability to interpret and reconcile information from multiple sources.

• Clear written communication and documentation skills.

• Ability to work independently and follow defined processes reliably.


Desirable Skills and Experience

• Experience with renewable energy or wind projects, planning applications, GIS data, environmental datasets, or data cleansing and validation.

• Familiarity with Excel, Google Sheets, Airtable, GIS platforms or data-quality tools.

• Additional European language skills would be advantageous but are not essential.


Who We’re Looking For

We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds such as data quality, research, energy, GIS, environmental data, geography, planning or intelligence analysis.


Contract Details

Duration: 3–6 months

Location: Norwich (Hybrid) or remote within the UK

Start date: As soon as possible

Hours: Full-time preferred


Success Measures

By the end of the assignment, the analyst will have:

• Reviewed and validated project master lists across approximately 30 European markets.

• Reduced the backlog of records awaiting human review.

• Improved the consistency and reliability of project normalisation.

• Supported the timely expansion of the Onshore Wind Intelligence Platform.

Monday - Friday 9:00AM - 5:30PM | Position Pay Range $18.40 - $22.81
This position requires attendance of a mandatory, 2-week training period at our Diamond Hill center in Denver

Summary/Objective:

The Patient Service Representative (PSR) focuses on the delivery of patient care and facilitates the needs of the physician. Focuses purely on the patient in front of them and ensures the patient knows and feels that they are the most important person in that moment. Creates an environment where our patients know they are a priority and provides spectacular service by doing what is necessary to take care of the patient. Performs administrative tasks such as answering phones, data entry, patient check in/out, and assists in scheduling patient appointments. Enters charges, verifies patients’ insurance coverage, receives payments from patients, and issues receipts. Supports company initiatives by adopting new approaches, practices, and processes to deliver unmistakable quality, spectacular service, and operational excellence on a consistent basis.

Essential Functions

1. Answers inbound calls to the Center.

2. Provides a friendly and warm greeting to all patients and/or providers.

3. Checks scheduled patients in/out and ensures proper documentation is received from patient.

4. Collects co-pays, co-insurance, and deductible if necessary.

5. Listens and resolves patient, provider, and any customer complaints. Communicates to PSR Lead and/or Area Manager as needed.

6. Ensures accurate data entry for patient registration.

7. Assists with medical records as needed.

8. Ensures all queues are processed in a timely and efficient manner while adhering to all process & compliance requirements.

9. Manages eRIS Center workflow, including daily schedule, billing complete, priors grid, delinquent exams, waitlist, report delivery queues, and collection of TOS.

10. Stays abreast of known carrier related issues and is able to identify carrier specific concerns, (i.e. out of network, specific plan limitations, etc.)

11. Monitors schedule and ensures all data, attachments, history, etc. have been done before exam is completed.

12. Facilitates no-show appointments (calling patients, cancelling, rescheduling).

13. Reschedules and cancels appointments as needed/directed (receives incoming/outgoing calls to patients).

14. Monitors waiting room to avoid extended wait time and to assists patients as needed.

15. Requests orders and processes new/same-day requests.

16. Requests all patients complete a satisfaction survey after their exam.

17. Other duties as assigned.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Competencies

1. Communication Proficiency.

2. Organizational Skills.

3. Time Management.

4. Problem Solving/Analysis.

5. Customer/Client Focus.

6. Collaboration Skills.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has no supervision responsibilities.

Work Environment

This job operates in an outpatient clinical environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands and fingers to handle, feel or operate objects, tools or controls, and reach with hands and arms. The employee is frequently required to talk and hear.

Travel

No travel is expected for this position.

Job Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications/Experience:

 One plus year of experience providing exceptional customer service – healthcare environment preferred

 Detail oriented, self-motivated, a problem solver and a team player

 Ability to navigate multiple computer screens and browsers quickly and accurately

 Ability to excel in a very fast-pace team environment

 Ability to continuously “exceed” company and customer expectation

 Strong communication skills & professional demeanor

Education/Certifications:

 Minimum of High School diploma or equivalent (GED)

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

None required for this position.

Compliance

Adheres to Envision’s Code of Conduct and Compliance Policies and attends annual Compliance training as set forth by the Company.

Company Benefits

Below is a list of benefits that are offered to employees, once eligibility is met.

 Health Benefits: Medical/Dental/Vision/Life Insurance

 Company Matched 401k Plan

 Employee Stock Ownership Plan

 Paid Time Off + Paid Holidays

 Employee Assistance Program

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. Other duties may be assigned as needed by supervision.

title: Senior Advisor, Legal affairs
description:
As a senior legal affairs advisor, you help protect the organization’s legal interests by ensuring it complies with all laws. You also play a key role in making sure that its rights are protected and obligations are met. You represent the organization in situations involving its legal interests. You may be responsible for one or more sub-specialties, such as contested matters and the Office of the Corporate Secretary (ethics and professional conduct, official registries, meeting minutes, the general meeting, etc.). You lead and influence development projects and complex, highly innovative strategic initiatives involving multiple sectors. You help develop and recommend strategic directions and business positions. Your initiatives require extensive knowledge of your field. You make recommendations on the planning and execution of operationally and conceptually complex projects and initiatives that require comprehensive analysis and understanding of the organization and line of business. Coordination is critical, so you frequently interact with stakeholders working in a wide range of other fields. Interpersonal savvy is therefore essential. The Staff Software Engineer will serve as a principal technical authority, shaping the overarching vision, architecture, and strategy for the applications, platforms, and delivery systems supporting our global supply chain solutions. Operating at the strategic intersection of software engineering, cloud architecture, and operations, this role will drive platform modernization, establish organization-wide best practices, and lead high-impact engineering initiatives to maximize operational efficiency and scalability. What You’ll Do:

description:
Applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. CT on the day before the listed closing date.

  • All positions are considered on-site roles.
  • After six months of employment, some positions may be eligible to apply for a hybrid work arrangement based on job responsibilities, operational needs, supervisor approval, and Dallas College policy.
  • Academic (Faculty) positions require an on-campus presence, even when teaching online courses, in accordance with state law.

Position Type

Administrator

Shape the Future of Workforce Strategy at Dallas College

Dallas College is seeking a strategic, forward-thinking leader to serve as Senior Director, HR People Analytics and Workforce Planning. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence enterprise-wide workforce decisions by transforming data into actionable insights that drive organizational effectiveness, talent strategy, workforce planning, and business outcomes.

As a key member of the Human Resources leadership team, the Senior Director will partner across HR, Finance, Information Technology, Institutional Research, and executive leadership to develop workforce intelligence strategies that support one of the largest community college systems in Texas. The successful candidate will help guide critical decisions related to talent, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, retention, compensation, and long-term institutional priorities.

Why This Role Matters

The Senior Director will lead the advancement of people analytics and workforce planning capabilities across Dallas College by developing innovative approaches to workforce intelligence, reporting, forecasting, and strategic decision-making. This position will play a critical role in helping college leaders understand workforce trends, anticipate future workforce needs, and align resources to support student success and institutional excellence.

What You'll Have the Opportunity to Do

In this role, you will:

  • Lead enterprise-wide people analytics and workforce planning initiatives that support strategic decision-making.

  • Translate complex workforce data into meaningful insights and recommendations for executive leadership.

  • Develop workforce forecasts, scenario planning models, and talent intelligence strategies.

  • Partner with leaders across the institution to support workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, and operational excellence.

  • Advance data governance, reporting standards, and responsible AI practices within Human Resources.

  • Build and lead a high-performing analytics team while driving a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate combines analytical expertise with strong business acumen and the ability to influence at all levels of the organization. They are equally comfortable working with data, technology, and executive stakeholders, and have a passion for leveraging workforce insights to improve organizational outcomes.

Successful candidates will bring experience in people analytics, workforce planning, business intelligence, executive reporting, and cross-functional collaboration within a complex organization.

About Dallas College

Dallas College is one of the largest community college systems in Texas, serving students across multiple campuses throughout the Dallas-Fort Worth region. We are committed to providing opportunities for students, employees, and communities to thrive through education, innovation, and service.

Joining Dallas College means being part of an institution dedicated to student success, workforce development, and creating meaningful impact across the communities we serve.

Position / Job Summary

The Senior Director, HR People Analytics and Workforce Planning advances Dallas College’s people analytics, workforce planning, and workforce intelligence strategy by transforming complex HR, workforce, financial, operational, and external market data into actionable insights and recommendations. The role is responsible and accountable for the annual and quarterly workforce planning cycle, enterprise workforce planning analytics, headcount and staffing forecasts, scenario modeling, executive and board-level reporting, and business intelligence solutions supporting organizational effectiveness, compensation, talent, retention, compliance, institutional efficiency, and operational excellence. This position partners across Human Resources, HRIS, Finance, Information Technology, Institutional Research, and college leadership to ensure data integrity, scalable analytics, effective reporting, responsible AI-enabled HR analytics, ethical use of employee data, and alignment with institutional priorities and budget planning.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead Dallas College’s enterprise people analytics, workforce planning, and workforce intelligence strategy, aligning data initiatives with institutional priorities, staffing strategies, organizational design decisions, HR transformation goals, budget planning, and long-range workforce needs.

  • Lead and manage HR analytics professionals, providing strategic direction, coaching, development, and performance oversight.

  • Translate complex HR and workforce data into clear, actionable narratives, recommendations, risks, and opportunities for executive decision support and board-related workforce analytics.

  • Own the HR analytics product roadmap, including the strategy, governance, prioritization, design, adoption, and continuous improvement of Power BI dashboards, self-service reporting, metric definitions, and other HR business intelligence solutions to ensure usability, scalability, accuracy, and executive relevance.

  • Develop and implement predictive analytics and workforce scenario models to assess the impact of attrition, retirement eligibility, hiring velocity, vacancies, funding changes, organizational redesign, compensation changes, labor market conditions, and emerging skill gaps.

  • Lead workforce planning analytics and forecasting activities in support of the annual and quarterly workforce planning process in partnership with HR, Finance, and institutional leaders, including headcount forecasting, staffing assumptions, vacancy analysis, workforce supply and demand modeling, critical capability gap analysis, and multi-year workforce strategies aligned to Dallas College priorities.

  • Partner with Finance and HR leadership to reconcile workforce forecasts with budget planning, compensation assumptions, position management data, staffing investments, operating plans, and workforce-related financial planning.

  • Participate as Human Resources' analytics subject matter expert on the College Data Governance Council and Institutional Effectiveness Council, contributing HR data expertise, workforce insights, governance recommendations, and reporting standards that support institutional decision-making.

  • Support HR AI governance initiatives by implementing approved responsible AI standards, analytics guardrails, data stewardship practices, privacy protections, bias monitoring, transparency requirements, human oversight, and risk mitigation practices for HR reporting, workforce insights, and AI-enabled decision support.

  • Conduct external labor market research, peer and industry benchmarking, and workforce trend analysis to inform talent, compensation, organizational, and workforce decisions.

  • Partner with Compensation, Talent Acquisition, HR Business Partners, Employee Experience, Information Technology, Institutional Research, and other stakeholders to evaluate workforce trends, organizational structures, staffing models, talent pipelines, compensation competitiveness, and operational effectiveness.

  • Provide data-driven support for organizational design, role alignment, span-of-control analysis, workforce segmentation, succession planning, and strategic talent initiatives.

  • Establish and maintain standards for HR metrics, data definitions, data quality, reporting governance, privacy, regulatory compliance, ethical workforce analytics, and responsible use of employee data and AI-enabled insights.

  • Lead the design and delivery of standardized and ad hoc HR reporting, working closely with HRIS to define reporting requirements, validate data sources, improve report accuracy, and serve as a primary point of contact for institutional HR analytics and reporting needs.

  • Drive automation and optimization of HR reporting processes across platforms such as Workday, Cornerstone, and Phenom.

  • Increase data literacy and system utilization through stakeholder engagement, training, system documentation, and user guides.

  • Complete required Dallas College Professional Development hours per academic year. All employees are required to complete a minimum of 19 hours. People leaders are required to complete an additional 16 hours of leadership development.

  • Perform other duties not listed as assigned.

The following duties are required for People Leader roles specifically:

  • Exercise full discretion and decision-making authority in the recruitment, selection, hiring, mentoring, coaching, development, and termination of staff, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, budgetary constraints, and workforce planning strategies.

  • Drive high performance by administering the performance management process timely, setting clear expectations, conducting performance evaluations, and implementing initiatives that enhance employee engagement, motivation, and retention.

Minimum and Preferred – Education, Experience, and/or Certifications

Required Qualifications for Role (necessary or mandatory)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

  • Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in people analytics, HR analytics, workforce planning, data science, workforce intelligence, HRIS analytics, business intelligence, or a closely related field.

  • Two or more years of leadership experience managing analytics professionals, technical teams, or cross-functional analytics initiatives.

  • Demonstrated experience applying statistical analysis, data visualization, predictive modeling, and business intelligence to workforce or organizational questions.

  • Demonstrated experience developing executive-level analytics, recommendations, dashboards, and presentations for senior leaders.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting workforce planning cycles, financial or budget-informed workforce analysis, data governance, institutional reporting, responsible AI governance, or ethical workforce analytics initiatives in a complex organization.

  • Technical proficiency with Power BI and relevant analytics tools or languages, such as SQL, Python, R, DAX, SAS, or advanced Excel.

  • Current and valid Texas driver’s license required for offsite travel.

Other Preferred Qualifications for Role (not mandatory, but advantageous)

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Economics, Human Resources, or a related quantitative field. PhD preferred but not required.

  • Advanced people analytics or data science credential, such as Wharton’s People Analytics certificate or a comparable recognized program.

  • Experience in higher education or public-sector HR analytics.

  • Experience with compensation modeling, organizational analytics, workforce benchmarking, and labor market intelligence.

  • Experience integrating and analyzing data across enterprise platforms such as Workday, Cornerstone, Phenom, or comparable systems.

  • Professional certification such as SHRM-SCP, SPHR, PHR, Power BI, Tableau, or another advanced analytics certification.

*** Will be subject to a criminal background check. Some positions may be subject to a fingerprint check. ***

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Required Qualifications for Role (necessary or mandatory)

  • Expert knowledge of people analytics, workforce metrics, data strategy, statistical methods, predictive modeling, and data visualization.

  • Ability to translate complex quantitative findings into clear business narratives, recommendations, and decisions for executive and nontechnical audiences.

  • Advanced skill in Power BI dashboard development, data modeling, DAX, data visualization, and analytics product governance.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with HRIS and technology partners to translate workforce and HR reporting needs into accurate, scalable, and user-centered reporting solutions.

  • Ability to aggregate, validate, analyze, and interpret data from multiple HR and enterprise systems while maintaining data integrity, privacy, and compliance.

  • Knowledge of workforce planning cycles, headcount forecasting, workforce segmentation, scenario modeling, organizational effectiveness, compensation analytics, talent analytics, retention analysis, external benchmarking, HR data governance, institutional reporting, ethical workforce analytics, and responsible AI-enabled analytics practices.

  • Ability to partner with Finance, HRIS, HR leaders, and institutional stakeholders to connect workforce insights to budget planning, staffing strategy, position management, and long-range organizational priorities.

  • Ability to lead analytics strategy, prioritize competing requests, establish reporting standards, and deliver scalable solutions in a complex organization.

  • Strong relationship-building and consultation skills with executives, HR leaders, technical teams, institutional partners, and subject matter experts.

  • Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills, including executive and board-level communication.

  • Proven ability to coach, develop, and motivate analytics professionals and cross-functional project teams.

  • Strong judgment, problem-solving, organizational, customer service, and stakeholder engagement skills.

​Competencies

Dallas College seeks to identify core and professional competencies for each role and level which helps define the level of expertise needed and desired to demonstrate success in the role.

Individual Competencies:

  • Ensures Accountability

  • Empowers Teams

  • Leads Strategically

  • Ensures Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Communicates Effectively

People Leader Competencies:

  • Ensures Accountability

  • Empowers Teams

  • Leads Strategically

  • Ensures Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Communicates Effectively

Work Condition Environment / Physical Requirements

Normal physical job functions performed within a standard office environment. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to individuals with physical challenges to perform the essential duties and responsibilities.

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job and shall not be construed as a declaration of the total of the specific duties and responsibilities of any particular position. Incumbents may be directed to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description. Position requires regular and predictable attendance.

About Us

Since 1965, Dallas College, formerly Dallas County Community College District, has served more than three (3) million students. Comprising seven campuses located around the Dallas/Fort Worth area, we are one of the largest community college systems in the state of Texas. We strive to be a leader in the community college space, placing students at the center of everything we do.

Dallas College is committed to cultivating an environment of opportunity and belonging for all students and employees. We recognize that the Dallas College workforce, and the diverse talent that stems from it, is directly linked to our success.
