title: Therapist - Level 1
description:
Join Our Mission at Lambs Farm

At Lambs Farm, we are passionately committed to enriching the lives of adults with developmental disabilities by providing meaningful opportunities, person-centered support, and a vibrant community where people can grow. For more than six decades, our residential, vocational, recreational, and community-based programs have helped participants build independence, pursue their goals, and enjoy fulfilling lives.

Our Specialty Care Center expands that mission by providing accessible behavioral health services designed to support participants' emotional well-being, behavioral health, and overall quality of life. Through individualized treatment, evidence-based interventions, and interdisciplinary collaboration, our clinical team helps participants develop skills, navigate challenges, and work toward meaningful personal goals.

Do you have a passion for behavioral health and want to grow your clinical expertise while making a meaningful impact in the lives of adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities? Lambs Farm may be the place for you.


Summary

We are seeking a compassionate and motivated Level I Therapist to provide individual, family, and group therapy services to adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities through our Specialty Care Center. In this role, you will conduct behavioral health assessments, develop individualized treatment plans, provide evidence-based therapeutic interventions, and collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to support meaningful participant outcomes.

Reporting to the Behavioral Health Clinical Director, you will practice under clinical supervision while working toward independent licensure. This role offers an opportunity to strengthen your clinical skills, receive ongoing professional development and supervision, and contribute to the continued growth and innovation of behavioral health services at Lambs Farm.


The Role

  • Provide individual, family, and group therapy using evidence-based, person-centered, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive approaches
  • Complete comprehensive behavioral health assessments, including IM+CANS assessments, in accordance with agency and payer requirements
  • Develop, implement, review, and update individualized treatment plans based on participant goals and identified clinical needs
  • Monitor participant progress and use clinical judgment to modify treatment approaches and interventions as appropriate
  • Help participants develop coping strategies, emotional regulation skills, communication skills, and healthy relationships
  • Complete assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, therapy documentation, and other required clinical records accurately and within established timelines
  • Submit appropriate clinical documentation to support billing and reimbursement requirements
  • Maintain accurate electronic health records in accordance with organizational and regulatory standards
  • Ensure clinical documentation demonstrates medical necessity and uses appropriate professional clinical language
  • Maintain participant confidentiality in accordance with HIPAA and applicable state and federal requirements
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary team members to coordinate participant care and treatment planning
  • Communicate professionally with participants, families, guardians, healthcare providers, and community partners
  • Participate in case consultations, staffing meetings, and interdisciplinary treatment planning
  • Coordinate referrals and connect participants with community resources when appropriate
  • Participate in ongoing clinical supervision while progressing toward independent professional licensure

title: Deputy Head of Training
description:

The Training Center Operations and Standards Leader acts on behalf of the Head of Training within assigned Training Center(s) and is responsible for ensuring the effective delivery, quality, standardization, and regulatory compliance of training programs.

Operations

  • Represent the Head of Training within assigned Training Center(s).

  • Monitor and maintain operational data to support business and training decisions.

Training and Standards

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, collaboration tools, and internet-based systems.

title: Program Manager, Preclinical Programs
description:
Who We Are:

Neurocrine Biosciences is a leading biopharmaceutical company with a simple purpose: to relieve suffering for people with great needs. We are dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. The company's diverse portfolio includes FDA-approved treatments for tardive dyskinesia, chorea associated with Huntington's disease, classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, endometriosis* and uterine fibroids*, as well as a robust pipeline including multiple compounds in mid- to late-phase clinical development across our core therapeutic areas. For more than three decades, we have applied our unique insight into neuroscience and the interconnections between brain and body systems to treat complex conditions. We relentlessly pursue medicines to ease the burden of debilitating diseases and disorders, because you deserve brave science. For more information, visit neurocrine.com, and follow the company on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and YouTube. (*in collaboration with AbbVie)



At Neurocrine, strong leadership drives both business results and team success. We look for leaders who think strategically, anticipate what’s ahead and set clear direction, while building and empowering high-performing teams. Successful leaders foster an environment where people are motivated to do their best work and deliver meaningful, measurable impact through sound decision-making and accountability.



About the Role:

The Program Manager role supports the planning, execution, and operational effectiveness of Preclinical programs and initiatives. Provides program management leadership across multiple Preclinical functional sub teams, partnering with scientific and functional leads to translate cross-functional program strategies into integrated plans and coordinated execution spanning early research through Development Candidate selection, IND/CTA readiness, and First-in-Human development.

The Program Manager partners closely with subject matter experts across Toxicology, DMPK/ADME, Bioanalytical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, Clinical Pharmacology Bioanalytical, and Pharmacometrics, and interacts with stakeholders across Research, CMC, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Finance, and Program Management to facilitate alignment on program strategy, milestones, risks, timelines, resources, and critical-path activities.

The role also supports broader early-development portfolio visibility, ensuring that emerging program information, risks, dependencies, and decisions are appropriately communicated across functional, asset, portfolio, and leadership governance forums.

_

Your Contributions (include, but are not limited to):

  • Provides program management leadership for 6 or more Preclinical functional sub teams representing defined segments of the preclinical portfolio and partners with scientific leads and subject matter experts to coordinate execution across multiple assets and development stages

  • Facilitates team alignment and execution against integrated program plans, including management of key milestones, dependencies, risks/issues, critical-path activities, budgets, resources, and governance requirements from early development through IND/CTA and FIH readiness

  • Partners with subject matter experts across Toxicology, DMPK/ADME, Bioanalytical, Clinical Pharmacology, Clinical Pharmacology Bioanalytical, and Pharmacometrics to integrate functional plans, identify cross-disciplinary dependencies, and proactively surface risks or decisions that may affect program timelines

  • Develops and maintains integrated project plans, timelines, risk and action trackers, meeting documentation, dashboards, and program status updates. Monitors program performance and facilitates issue resolution and appropriate escalation to maintain progress toward development objectives

  • Supports preparation for key portfolio and development milestones, including Portfolio Entry, Development Candidate selection, IND/CTA readiness, and First-in-Human activities, ensuring appropriate functional planning and visibility ahead of major decision points

  • Partners with the designated Preclinical Representative to support effective representation of the integrated Preclinical perspective within cross-functional Asset/Core Teams, ensuring that relevant scientific considerations, functional risks, dependencies, and recommendations are appropriately aligned and communicated

  • Partners with Cross-Functional Program Management, CMC Functional Program Management, Regulatory Affairs, and other stakeholders to ensure that asset-level strategic decisions are effectively translated into coordinated functional execution and that emerging Preclinical risks and dependencies are appropriately communicated into broader asset governance

  • Supports IND Operations and regulatory readiness activities, including tracking of critical Preclinical reports and deliverables, cross-functional dependencies, submission timelines, and other activities required to support IND/CTA submissions

  • Supports portfolio-level tracking and communications, including dashboards, portfolio updates, milestone tracking, and leadership reporting to provide timely visibility into early-development program progress, emerging risks, and upcoming decisions

  • Partners with Finance and functional stakeholders to support long-range planning, annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial tracking for Preclinical program activities and external development spend

  • Identifies opportunities to improve processes, workflows, governance, information flow, and team effectiveness and recommends and contributes to continuous-improvement initiatives that enhance execution and collaboration across R&D

  • Assists with adoption and optimization of new systems, tools, dashboards, and digital capabilities that improve portfolio visibility, program management, knowledge management, and R&D operational effectiveness

  • Builds collaborative relationships across Research, Preclinical, CMC, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Finance, Portfolio Management, and Cross-Functional Program Management to support effective coordination and progression of programs through the development lifecycle

Requirements:

  • 6+ years of applicable experience AND Bachelor’s degree OR

  • 4+ years of applicable experience AND Master’s degree OR

  • 2+ years of applicable experience AND PharmD, or PhD

  • Working knowledge of drug discovery and development processes spanning early research, Development Candidate selection, IND/CTA readiness, and First-in-Human development

  • Understanding of Preclinical & Clinical Pharmacology disciplines and their role in integrated drug development, including Toxicology, DMPK/ADME, Bioanalytical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, Clinical Pharmacology Bioanalytical, and Pharmacometrics

  • Ability to integrate plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across multiple PCCP disciplines and development programs

  • Understanding of the cross-functional dependencies among PCCP, Research, CMC, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, and other development functions

  • Knowledge of key preclinical and early clinical development milestones and the planning and operational activities required to support progression through major program decision points

  • Familiarity with IND/CTA readiness and submission activities, including coordination and tracking of functional reports, data, documentation, dependencies, and timelines supporting regulatory submissions

  • Ability to partner effectively with scientific and functional subject-matter experts and translate complex scientific and technical activities into integrated program plans, milestones, risks, and execution priorities

  • Ability to identify and communicate scientific and operational dependencies, risks, and decisions that may affect program timelines or development objectives

  • Understanding of portfolio and program governance practices and the information required to support effective program, portfolio, and leadership decision-making

  • Familiarity with budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, and financial tracking associated with preclinical and early-development program activities and external development spend

  • Previous experience working in a scientific role within a preclinical or research environment is required

  • Experience supporting Preclinical/PCCP, Clinical Pharmacology, Toxicology, early-stage drug development, or related functions is preferred

  • Strong program and project management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex programs, projects, or workstreams with competing priorities and deadlines

  • Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to develop and maintain integrated plans, timelines, milestones, dependencies, critical paths, risks, and deliverables

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment, facilitate productive discussions, and drive execution in a matrixed environment

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex information, identify risks and dependencies, develop options, and make sound recommendations

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information and communicate program status, risks, decisions, and recommendations clearly to diverse audiences, including senior leaders

  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate meetings, planning sessions, governance forums, scenario discussions, and decision-making processes involving multiple functions and stakeholders

  • Ability to operate with a high degree of independence within established objectives, exercising sound judgment regarding when to resolve issues directly and when escalation or broader leadership involvement is appropriate

  • Strong understanding of risk, issue, dependency, and decision management practices and their application to complex development programs

  • Ability to understand broader organizational objectives and downstream impacts and translate strategic or program objectives into actionable plans, priorities, and execution activities

  • Strong continuous-improvement mindset, with the ability to identify and recommend improvements to processes, workflows, governance, tools, reporting, and ways of working

#LI-CL1

Neurocrine Biosciences is an EEO/Disability/Vets employer.

We are committed to building a workplace of belonging, respect, and empowerment, and we recognize there are a variety of ways to meet our requirements. We are looking for the best candidate for the job and encourage you to apply even if your experience or qualifications don’t line up to exactly what we have outlined in the job description.

_

The annual base salary we reasonably expect to pay is $130,800.00-$179,000.00. Individual pay decisions depend on various factors, such as primary work location, complexity and responsibility of role, job duties/requirements, and relevant experience and skills. In addition, this position offers an annual bonus with a target of 30% of the earned base salary and eligibility to participate in our equity based long term incentive program. title: Founding Program Director, Engineering
description:
Job Title

Founding Program Director, Engineering

Agency

Texas A&M University - Victoria

Department

College of Natural & Applied Science

$8,333.34 monthly

Job Location

Victoria, Texas

Job Type

Faculty

Job Description

Texas A&M University–Victoria seeks a full-time, 12-month faculty member for an appointment as a tenure-track Associate or Full Professor or a non-tenure-track Professor of Practice to serve as the Founding Director of the new Bachelor of Science programs in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Software Engineering. The Founding Director will provide leadership for launching, promoting, and advancing these programs and will teach courses within the programs.

Qualifications: The Bachelor of Science (BS) degrees in engineering are designed to serve the community in the Coastal Bend region of Texas. The Founding Director will serve as a primary point of contact for Texas A&M University-Victoria (A&M-Victoria), with a primary focus on developing and supporting the BS in Civil Engineering, Software Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering with a focus on the intersections between these disciplines. They will also need to satisfy the expectations of Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) and ABET in terms of academic credentials, as well as all other employment qualifications of the University. The programs are anticipated to be open for enrollment Fall 2027. The Founding Director will be employed by A&M-Victoria and will teach face-to-face courses within the University’s academic programs.

Victoria is about two hours driving time from Houston, Corpus Christi, Austin, and San Antonio. The Founding Program Director reports to Dean of the College of Natural and Applied Science, working within the Department of Engineering and Aviation Sciences, and has both administrative and instructional responsibilities.

The successful candidate should demonstrate the following qualifications:

· Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage professional, community, industry, and student audiences.

· Ability to plan and implement activities that increase the visibility and profile of the A&M-Victoria Agribusiness concentration within the regional community and agricultural industry.

· Demonstrated commitment to supporting and working effectively with students from diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds, as well as students with disabilities.

Responsibilities: The individual in this position will be expected to:

· Teach classes in service of A&M-Victoria engineering programs, in line with academic credentials and professional experience. Teaching assignments will include face-to-face classes in Victoria, Texas.

· Promote A&M-Victoria engineering programs in the greater Victoria region in collaboration with the Division of Enrollment Management.

· Direct and oversee the development and equipping of necessary lab and classroom teaching spaces for the proposed engineering degrees.

· Be responsible for administrative matters of the department, including teaching, laboratory and research facilities; class rotations and scheduling; budget; and equipment.

· Maintain good working relationships with the Independent School Districts and community colleges in Victoria and the surrounding area, as well as with industry partners in the region.

· Advise students interested in admission to A&M-Victoria for study in engineering.

· Coordinate with the Center for Student Success to ensure that engineering students receive academic advising necessary to foster academic success.

· Participate in student activities and campus life and facilitate mentoring for engineering students with industry professionals.

· Engage in philanthropic development and community engagement in collaboration with the Office of University Advancement.

· Actively participate in affairs of the University, including assisting the engineering programs achieve and maintain ABET program accreditation.

· Coordinate with the Career Development Center to develop industry partnerships beneficial to A&M-Victoria and the engineering programs.

· Perform other duties as may be necessary and assigned.

Because of the University’s outreach mission to serve the broader Texas Gulf Coast region, the position may require travel and occasional work outside of normal business hours.

For more information about Texas A&M University-Victoria’s programs and mission, visit www.tamuv.edu.

Education and Experience: The position requires an earned master’s degree in engineering or engineering technology. Because this is a professional-track appointment, relevant industry experience in engineering as well as industrial design is expected. An earned doctorate in engineering with prior classroom experience and a knowledge of ABET accreditation and experience leading a program through accreditation is preferred. A current licensure as a professional engineer (mechanical or civil) is strongly preferred.

Texas A&M University-Victoria Values: Together We Rise

Wisdom

Excellence

Respect

Integrity

Students

Empathy

Setting: Texas A&M University-Victoria is the most recent addition to the Texas A&M University System. The University was founded in 1973 as part of the University of Houston System and

was transferred to the Texas A&M University System during the 89th Texas Legislative Session. A&M-Victoria is the only four-year university in a 100-mile radius and is just 30 miles from the Texas Gulf Coast. The University is a Hispanic-Serving Institution located in the Coastal Bend region of Texas. It serves the educational needs, promotes economic well-being, and advances the community and region's quality of life through teaching, research, and service excellence. The university is accredited by the SACSCOC, and it offers more than 50 academic programs, as well as concentrations and certificates. The university also has several accreditations for specific areas and programs, including from the AACSB, ABET, CACREP and CCNE. In addition to its recent transition into The Texas A&M University System, A&M-Victoria is in the process of adding academic programs in three major areas: aviation, agribusiness, and engineering. In addition to academic excellence, A&M-Victoria has a thriving Athletics program that offers six competitive teams: baseball, softball, men’s and women’s soccer, and men’s and women’s golf. The Jaguars are part of the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA), and the baseball, softball and soccer teams compete in the Red River Athletic Conference. The golf teams compete in the Association of Independent Institutions Conference. Learn more about Texas A&M University-Victoria's history, academic programs, and campus facilities here.

Application: Review of applications will begin September 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applications should include a letter of application addressing qualifications, curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy, and contact information for three references. For more information regarding this position and to apply, visit here. If you have any questions related to the search, please contact Dolores Guerrero (GuerreroD5@tamuv.edu).

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

title: Director, Engineering and Design
description:
About Us

Highland Electric Fleets’ mission is to make electric fleets accessible and affordable for all, enabling communities to realize the benefits of cleaner, quieter and healthier fleets. Highland is North America’s leading provider of Electrification-as-a-Service (EaaS). Founded in 2019, Highland partners with school districts, municipalities, and fleet operators to make the transition to electric fleets simple and affordable.

Highland proudly serves as the Official Electric School Bus Provider of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA. From pioneering vehicle-to-grid technology to managing some of the nation’s largest electric school bus fleets, Highland delivers reliable, cost-effective solutions that support local communities and drive the future of transportation.

Role Summary

The Director of Engineering leads Highland's engineering and design team — drafting, project engineering, and utility interconnection — that supports a fast-moving portfolio of EV charging, battery energy storage (BESS), and edge compute sites from qualified sites through construction-ready.

This leader owns the engineering standards, the design package content and quality gates, and the throughput of the entire function, and partners with Project Development to deliver build-ready sites at portfolio scale and on an aggressive timeline.

Reporting to the Vice President, Development & Construction, the Director builds and leads a team of internal and external engineering resources. The Director serves as Highland's senior technical authority on utility and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements, owns the engineering inputs to project schedule and budget, and builds the standards, playbooks, and tooling that make design faster, more repeatable, and more cost-effective.

This position is remote with an expectation of approximately 10-15% travel.

Responsibilities Overview:

  • Lead and scale Highland's project engineering function — drafting, design engineering, and utility interconnection — with end-to-end accountability for taking a large portfolio of EV charging, BESS, and edge compute sites from qualified site to permit-ready and construction-ready.
  • Own the engineering function's throughput and quality: define the design package content and the internal approval gates for every stage — conceptual, 30%, Issued-for-Permit (IFP), and Issued for Construction (IFC) — and keep packages moving on an aggressive, portfolio-wide timeline.
  • Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of internal engineering resources
  • Own Highland's external engineering-partner strategy — select, contract, scale, and manage the performance of engineering design and interconnection consultants so that internal and external capacity flex with portfolio volume.
  • Set and enforce Highland's engineering, CAD, and design specifications and standards, and own the repositories of utility and AHJ requirements that make design compliant, consistent, and repeatable across the portfolio.
  • Serve as Highland's senior technical authority on utility interconnection and AHJ permitting across EV charging, BESS, and edge compute; resolve the most complex technical and jurisdictional issues and represent Highland's engineering position externally.
  • Own the engineering inputs to project schedule and budget — sequence and resource design, interconnection, and permitting milestones so each site is build-ready when construction needs it, and contribute to Highland's repeatable unit-cost installation model.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Development, Execution, Origination, Procurement, and Fleet Operations to align engineering with portfolio priorities and continuously improve the site-to-energized process.
  • Drive continuous improvement through tooling and process automation (e.g., Procore, Bluebeam, template- and data-driven design) to increase design velocity and improve unit economics as the portfolio scales.
  • Provide engineering leadership on technical due diligence, estimating, and risk for new opportunities, supporting Origination and Development on feasibility, buildability, and cost.

Qualifications:

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering discipline, or 12+ years of directly related professional experience.
  • 10+ years of progressive engineering experience in EV charging, renewable energy, power/electrical infrastructure, or utility-scale development, including design management from concept through construction.
  • 5+ years leading engineering teams, including managing managers and building or scaling a design organization.
  • Demonstrated ownership of engineering standards, design package content, and QA/QC across a portfolio of concurrent projects.
  • Proven experience selecting, contracting, and managing external engineering consultants at scale.
  • Deep working knowledge of utility interconnection, new electrical service, and AHJ permitting requirements.
  • Familiarity with interconnection standards and processes (e.g., IEEE 1547, utility tariffs, and interconnection rules).
  • Expertise with CAD-based design delivery (AutoCAD) and design/review tooling (Procore, Bluebeam).

Preferred

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • Experience delivering EV charging infrastructure, BESS, and/or edge compute / data-center power projects.
  • Experience building repeatable, unit-cost-driven design programs in a high-growth environment.
  • Master's degree in engineering or an MBA.

What You Can Expect from Highland:

  • Competitive base salary and performance-based bonus program
  • A supportive, highly collaborative, team-oriented environment
  • Ability to work with bright, innovative, and forward-thinking colleagues
  • Health, Vision, and Dental coverage for employees & their dependents
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • 401(k) program and company match

title: Supply Chain Planner
description:
This is a hands-on, high-impact role at the heart of Vegware's global supply chain. You'll play a key role in ensuring our products are available for customers around the world by combining demand planning, supplier management and logistics coordination.


You'll be joining a close-knit team of four within a fun, inclusive and supportive environment. Our office is located in Edinburgh's beautiful West End, and the role requires a minimum of three days per week on site.


Are you data-orientated, proactive and ready to take ownership? Are you a friendly and positive person who brings good vibes? We would love to hear from you.


What the role involves


We're looking for an organised and data-driven individual to shape demand plans, manage supplier partnerships and keep our products flowing seamlessly from production to warehouse. You'll have real ownership, visibility and influence across the business, helping support Vegware's continued growth.


Key responsibilities


Demand & Inventory Planning

  • Own inventory planning and forecasting across the product range to balance availability, cash flow and stock levels.
  • Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to understand usage, manage expectations and meet demand.
  • Identify supply risks, shortages and excess inventory.
  • Analyse sales and product performance to improve planning decisions.


Purchasing & Supplier Management

  • Raise purchase orders and manage supply plans with our manufacturing partners.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for supply-related matters.
  • Track production schedules and supplier commitments to ensure products are delivered on time and in full.
  • Resolve supplier queries, invoice discrepancies and order amendments.

Logistics & Warehousing

  • Coordinate inbound logistics across sea, road and air freight.
  • Monitor shipments and proactively manage delays.
  • Work closely with warehouse teams to ensure timely product availability.


Systems, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain accurate supply chain data within our ERP and other business systems.
  • Contribute to supply chain performance reports and provide insights to support decision-making.
  • Identify opportunities to improve supply chain performance and costs.
  • Support wider supply chain projects and continuous improvement initiatives.


The type of person we’re looking for


Skills and attributes

· Strong analytical mindset with the ability to analyse and interpret data to make informed decisions.

· Highly organised and reliable, with excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

· Excellent time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

· Confident using business systems and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

· Collaborative and approachable, with strong communication skills and the ability to build effective relationships across teams and with external partners.

· Eager to learn, be proactive and contribute to a supportive team culture.


Experience

· 1-3 years’ experience in a supply chain, procurement, operations or commercial role.


Desirable

· Excellent Microsoft Excel skills, including data analysis and reporting.

· Experience using ERP systems such as NetSuite.

· Understanding of demand planning, inventory management and supplier management processes.

· Experience within FMCG, food, manufacturing or packaging industries.

· Passionate about sustainability and the environment.


The perks

In addition to meaningful work and a supportive team culture, you'll enjoy a range of benefits including a salary up to £35,000 plus:


  • Company pension
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Company sick pay
  • Private Medical Insurance with lots of benefits
  • Hybrid working hours (min 3 days in the office)
  • Company provided breakfast and hot drinks
  • Bike to work scheme
  • Paid volunteering time
  • Comprehensive Employee Assistance Programme
  • Company bonus scheme


Why choose Vegware?


At Vegware, we're on a mission to transform the foodservice industry and accelerate the transition to a more sustainable, circular future. As a global leader in compostable foodservice packaging and a certified B Corp, we're passionate about reducing waste and creating positive environmental impact.


Founded in Edinburgh and now operating across the UK, Europe and North America, Vegware combines the energy of a growing international business with a clear purpose.


Why people love working at Vegware:﻿


  • Purpose-driven work – help accelerate the transition to a more sustainable, circular future through innovative compostable packaging solutions.
  • Real impact – take ownership, contribute ideas and make a tangible difference in a growing international business.
  • Great people and culture – work alongside passionate, supportive colleagues who care about people and the planet.

title: Senior SharePoint Architect
description:
ACLC is seeking a Senior SharePoint Architect to design, configure, develop, assess, and sustain enterprise SharePoint and Microsoft 365 solutions that operationalize NGB Knowledge Management requirements across NIPR/SIPR environments and geographically dispersed organizations.

This position is contingent upon contract award.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Design, build, configure, and sustain enterprise SharePoint Online/Microsoft 365 solutions aligned with KM governance, information architecture, taxonomy, metadata, content types, and lifecycle standards.
  • Translate KM requirements-knowledge-flow needs, taxonomy constraints, metadata models, governance rules, repository structures, and lifecycle standards-into practical technical solutions.
  • Configure SharePoint sites, site collections, lists, libraries, content structures, permissions, access controls, templates, and related KM-scoped components.
  • Develop Power Apps that support structured data capture, workflows, task management, knowledge-sharing processes, and decision-support activities.
  • Build and maintain Power Automate workflows for approvals, content lifecycle actions, governance tasks, notifications, issue tracking, and other approved KM processes.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and other visualizations that present repository health, lifecycle adherence, content activity, training throughput, Communities of Practice engagement, governance performance, issue trends, usage, and adoption.
  • Perform KM-scoped administration and assessments within Army NIPR/SIPR 365 environments, including permission and access management, site configuration, content organization, list/library configuration, and compliance checks.
  • Monitor KM automations, workflows, and Microsoft 365 solutions; track failures, errors, delays, bottlenecks, and process misalignments; recommend and implement approved optimizations.
  • Generate usage, content, workflow-performance, repository-health, metadata-compliance, adoption, and engagement reports for MSR, QSR, and ASR reporting.
  • Develop the KM automation tool and related prototype/production capability incorporating KPIs, projects, planning phases, applications, POAMs, metrics, heat maps, and reusable Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI components.
  • Assess emerging technologies, recommend pilot initiatives, define required platform structures, and plan integration efforts across NG 365 environments and KM-relevant tools.
  • Document, version-control, publish, and maintain all solutions, configuration standards, technical guidance, governance artifacts, and reusable components in the appropriate KM repository.
  • Develop and update SharePoint 365 governance policies, procedures, naming conventions, configuration standards, and lifecycle controls; coordinate approved updates through KMOWG and KMRWG governance bodies.
  • Coordinate with RM personnel to apply appropriate metadata, naming conventions, content structures, and permissions where SharePoint KM structures intersect records-management requirements. RM execution remains with the Government RM office.
  • Deliver recurring KM tools training, including at least one two-hour session per month covering SharePoint administration fundamentals, metadata/taxonomy, lifecycle practices, Teams, Power Apps, Power Automate, dashboards, reports, and KM repositories.
  • Provide technical assistance during governance meetings, workshops, knowledge-sharing events, training sessions, and leadership briefings as required.

Qualifications

  • At least five years of demonstrated experience designing, building, and sustaining enterprise-level solutions within the SharePoint 365 environment.
  • Experience with SharePoint Online architecture; Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI; enterprise site structures; metadata and taxonomy standards; content types; governance documentation; workflow automation; solution prototyping; testing; and development.
  • Experience with secure configuration and solution support across NIPR/SIPR environments, consistent with applicable Government policies and cybersecurity constraints.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate KM governance, information architecture, knowledge-flow, taxonomy, metadata, and lifecycle requirements into technical SharePoint and workflow solutions.
  • Experience developing scalable, reusable solutions suitable for enterprise-wide adoption across geographically dispersed organizations.
  • Foundational understanding of Knowledge Management principles, including taxonomy application, content lifecycle management, information governance, knowledge assurance, and stakeholder collaboration.
  • Secret security clearance and ability to satisfy applicable installation, CAC, background-investigation, information-system, IA/IT-certification, and training requirements when assigned duties require them.

description:
Job Description:

Rakuten International is a division of Rakuten Group, Inc., a Japanese global technology leader in services that empower individuals, communities, businesses and society. Headquartered in San Mateo, California with more than 4,000 employees worldwide, the Rakuten International business portfolio includes market leaders in e-commerce, digital marketing, advertising, communications and entertainment. We create products and services that provide exceptional value by aligning members and the businesses that want to engage them in a shared community.

Rakuten is the most rewarding way to shop, giving millions of members Cash Back when they buy from their favorite brands. As a leading shopping platform, Rakuten partners with thousands of top brands across apparel, beauty and wellness, grocery, travel, on-demand services, subscriptions, and dining, helping members save on everyday purchases. Since 1999, Rakuten members have earned more than $4.6 billion in Cash Back, making it the largest Cash Back platform of its kind. Learn more at Rakuten.com.


Job Summary:

You will help engineering squads adopt AI agent skills and use them daily to build better software, faster. You will act as their embedded expert, a forward-deployed engineer for AI agent skills, showing them how to use these tools, fixing issues, and closing gaps as they come up. Alongside that, you will also own core platform work: infrastructure, CI/CD, and quality engineering, keeping the systems squads depend on reliable and well-tested. You will be based in San Mateo, working closely with your manager for direct mentorship as you grow across our stack.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Acts as the embedded, forward-deployed engineer for AI tooling: finds slow or manual points in a squad's dev lifecycle, closes them with AI-powered solutions, and champions AI coding assistants and agents across the org.
  • Designs and integrates agentic and multi-agent AI systems (LangChain, Agent SDK, MCP) and external AI services (Anthropic, OpenAI, and others) into internal tools and squad workflows.
  • Strengthens quality through unit, integration, and end-to-end testing, using AI to generate and maintain coverage faster and resolve issues quickly.
  • Builds back-end services, APIs, and lightweight front-end components across the team's stack (Java, Python, Golang, React), ensuring proper integration within existing infrastructure.
  • Designs and manages data schemas and databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Kafka) for efficient storage and retrieval.
  • Builds and improves CI/CD pipelines, deployment tooling, and internal developer platform capabilities (templates, self-service infra) that squads depend on.
  • Acquires foundational knowledge of system engineering principles and practices relevant to assigned projects.
  • Analyzes basic system requirements and participates in the preparation of technical specifications.
  • Applies learned concepts to assist in system design and implementation for limited-scope projects.
  • Communicates progress and findings to team members and stakeholders during project reviews.
  • Coordinates with cross-functional teams to align tasks with project timelines and deliverables.
  • Develops basic documentation to support system architecture and implementation processes.
  • Escalates technical challenges or unresolved issues to senior engineers for guidance and resolution.


Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with LLMs and AI agents, and comfort with cloud AI services (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar on AWS/GCP/Azure).
  • Practical experience building agentic systems: Agent Skills, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and multi-agent workflows using frameworks like LangChain or Agent SDK.
  • A grasp of AI fundamentals: why models fail, hallucinations, grounding, and evaluation-driven development.
  • An automation-first instinct and a system design mindset, reasoning about tradeoffs and not just writing code.
  • 1–3 years building products end-to-end, from design through production deployment; strong, relevant internships also count.
  • Solid programming fundamentals in at least one of Java, Python, Golang, or React, plus Git and collaborative development practices.
  • Comfort working across the full stack rather than staying in one lane.
  • Exposure to CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions) and an interest in developer productivity/platform tooling.

Nice to Have:

  • Master's degree in AI/ML, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Experience with Docker/containers, Agent Skills, MCP, monitoring, or API frameworks like FastAPI.
  • Hackathons, programming competitions, or personal projects building your own AI agents and automations.

Please include your GitHub or portfolio so we can see what you've built.


Minimum Requirements:

  • 1–3 years relevant work experience Required
  • 1–2 years of programming experience in at least one of Java, Python, Golang, or React Required
  • Bachelor's Degree Required
  • Master's Degree Preferred

Why You Should Apply:

  • Works on real, open-ended problems, defining the approach and seeing solutions go live across the org.
  • Gets direct visibility and mentorship from a senior engineering leader, with real influence on how the company adopts AI.
  • Gains broad exposure across the stack and the business, at a leading global tech company.

Five Principles for Success
Our worldwide practices describe specific behaviors that make Rakuten unique and united across the world. We expect Rakuten employees to model these 5 Shugi Principles of Success.

Always improve, Always Advance - Only be satisfied with complete success - Kaizen
Passionately Professional - Take an uncompromising approach to your work and be determined to be the best
Hypothesize - Practice - Validate – Shikumika - Use the Rakuten Cycle to succeed in unknown territory
Maximize Customer Satisfaction - The greatest satisfaction for our teams is seeing their customers smile
Speed!! Speed!! Speed!! - Always be conscious of time - take charge, set clear goals, and engage your team

title: Project Manager I / II (Alaska Railroad)
description:
Job Description

PURPOSE OF POSITION:

Primary responsibility is to oversee, direct, and execute capital projects.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Provides oversight, direction, and coordination for assigned projects or project related efforts, which includes managing project design processes, conducting environmental studies and permitting processes; planning and coordinating internal force account work and coordinating contract development for construction by contractors and construction management contractors; and developing quality assurance programs for said contracts. Anticipates, develops and controls changes to projects and related contracts, budget estimating, development, management and execution (payment reviews, prioritization and re-allocation. Provides oversight for compliance with ARRC, state and federal regulations concerning the environment, contract execution, labor regulations, and railroad operational and occupational safety rules. Manages projects as assigned including scope, schedule, and budgets. Manages contractors and coordinates other ARRC staff as required for the delivery of capital projects.

Assists department managers in developing plans for assigned projects funded by federal and state grants or internal capital funds. A project plan may include: analyzing and formulating project concepts, goals, schedules, cost estimates, critical path issues and financing requirements. Analyzes options and identifies opportunities for performance improvements.

Coordinates project plans for assigned projects with architect, contractors, department program manager, etc.

Provides project support on ARRC engineering projects on an as needed basis. Assists ARRC project management team with unassigned projects as needed.

Coordinates with the Supply Management Department to ensure that all materials and/or services needed for assigned projects funded by federal and state grants or internal capital funds are delivered as required and/or specified in contractual agreements. Reviews and approves invoices for payment.

Provides written and oral updates on assigned projects funded by federal grants to ARRC representatives as well as federal, state, and community groups as required. Organizes meetings such as public hearings as required to accomplish project plan goals and deadlines.

Coordinates with the grant administration staff to ensure all financing procedures are properly followed to include, but not limited to, reporting requirements. Responsible for completion of assigned projects within approved budgetary amounts.

Will be required to drive on an as needed basis.

Manages, directs, oversees work by Project Managers. Administratively responsible for subordinate Project Managers work and development (Project Manager III only)

May be required to participate in Incident Command exercises and activities.

May have supervisory responsibilities for new or junior Project Management employees as required (PM II and III only)


FACTOR 1: Technical and Operational Knowledge

Knowledgeable of engineering principles, practices and specifications for civil or railroad construction projects. Demonstrates knowledge of project management principles and practices. Requires knowledge of applicable industry codes and regulations. Understands budgeting and cost control methods and of procurement practices and regulations. Exhibits a working knowledge of Excel, word processing, e-mail, and scheduling software. Shows proficiency in CADD and engineering design software. Knowledgeable in architectural, engineering, environmental, NEPA, and construction contracts including value engineering, project scheduling and contractual oversight is required to analyze, evaluate, and monitor assigned projects.

FACTOR 2: Analytical Skills & Impact

Shows familiarity with procurement processes, budgets and cost control methods, and value engineering to ensure that materials/services are delivered as specified and that costs are controlled, monitored, and reported in accordance with ARRC finance and grant reporting procedures. Manages, oversees, and directs all phases of assigned projects to include analyzing options and identifying opportunities for performance/cost improvements. Demonstrates quality of final product, good mid-project decision-making and ensures long term economic feasibility of the product which is of main importance to the ARRC.

FACTOR 3: Supervision and Control

Manages work performed on assigned projects to include the oversight and direction of ARRC employees and contractors working on assigned projects. Manages all resources needed to successfully complete assigned projects to include workforce requirements (ARRC employees and contractors), contract services, and materials. Responsible for successful completion of assigned projects within approved budgetary amounts. Project Manager II and III may have direct supervision of other Project Managers or staff.

FACTOR 4: Communication

Communicates with ARRC employees representing all levels of the organization and departments for the purpose of coordinating all phases of assigned projects. Works with contractors working on assigned projects to ensure work is being performed as required and/or as specified in contractual agreements. Works with federal, state, and local agencies to ensure that all regulatory requirements are met on assigned projects. Provides informational presentations to ARRC officials and interested community groups as needed.

FACTOR 5: Working Conditions

Works in corporate office environment and on construction sites. May be exposed to harsh weather conditions and noise.





Minimum Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS

Education Requirements

Associate’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or Surveying or related discipline is required. Where work may focus on a specific area (e.g. facilities, Signal/telecom, Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, etc), specific experience in those fields are required. Bachelor’s degree is preferred and will be credited as four (4) years additional experience.

Must be capable of effectively communicating with, and coordinating with other ARRC departments to expeditiously deliver capital projects.

II

>10

Work Experience

engineering, environmental, NEPA, construction contracts, related to marine projects and development is required.

Certification/License Requirements

Must have a valid driver’s license.

To be considered a valid driver's license, an employee must maintain a continuous three-year period free of any Driving Under the Influence (DUI) or Operating Under the Influence (OUI) convictions.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer license is preferred. Previous experience working with railroad projects is preferred. Proficiency in AutoCAD software is preferred.

description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

Position is responsible for serving as a clinical expert in the delivery and management of care for patients requiring autotransfusion during surgery in collaboration with the physician and the healthcare team. The position works collaboratively with the physician and healthcare team and reports directly to the Perfusionist Manager.

Job Description

Minimum Qualifications

Education: High School Diploma or GED

Licenses/Certifications: Certification in autologous transfusion training program or (actively pursuing to receive within six (6) months of hire date)

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • Ability to follow oral and written instructions
  • Demonstrates commitment to the Partners-in-Caring process by integrating our culture in all internal and external customer interactions; delivers on our brand promise of “we advance health” through innovation, accountability, empowerment, collaboration, compassion and results while ensuring one Memorial Hermann.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Performs duties in a manner to promote quality patient care and customer service/satisfaction, while promoting safety, cost efficiency, and a commitment to the CQI process.
  • Assembles and operates cell saver equipment for autotransfusion on all orthopedic and vascular cases and any other case when requested by the surgeon.
  • Cleans and prepares various components of the autotransfusion machine and helps maintain the inventory of supplies.
  • Maintains quality control data and monitors autotransfusion so that adequate records for medical and/or legal study will be available.
  • Assists in the provision for coverage for all autotransfusion cases.
  • Assists in the preparation of platelet gel products.
  • Reports needed equipment repairs to the Perfusionist Manager in a timely manner.
  • Responsible for knowing which type of fluid and antibiotics are safe to mix with the patient’s blood.
  • Experienced with identification of sterile components of the autotransfusion system.
  • Responsible for coverage of autotransfusion schedule including emergency/on-call schedule.
  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.
  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as preceptor, mentor and resource to less experienced staff.

experience.

description:
Job Description

.

What you will be doing:
In this role, you will conduct investigations into allegations of fraud by applicants and recipients of Public Assistance Programs, including the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Alaska Temporary Assistance Program, Adult Public Assistance Program, and Medicaid Programs. You will prepare cases for criminal prosecution and Administrative Disqualification Hearings.
You will represent the Department in cases presented for Administrative Disqualification Hearings or in criminal proceedings. This position will require phone and in-person contact with witnesses, public assistance recipients, and individuals accused of fraud.

The Division of Public Assistance is committed to promoting self-sufficiency and providing basic living expenses to Alaskans in need. At the Division of Public Assistance, we work for the common good of, and earn the respect of, the clients, families, and communities we serve.

We honor cultural, geographic, and economic diversity and seek community involvement in our decisions and service delivery.

We believe in your career growth and advancement opportunities within our division. We provide a competitive benefit package, flexible work schedules, and job stability.

This position may be located in Anchorage or Fairbanks. Depending upon the location of the most qualified candidate

title: Ultrasound OBGYN-RVT Technologist - PRN
description:
Health Images is looking for a Part Time Ultrasound OBGYN - RVT Technologist to join our Quail Crossing ( Westminster) team!
Position Pay Range - $42.35 - $54.60|

Summary/Objection

Performs ultrasound procedures to adult and pediatric patients for the purpose of diagnosis and/or treatment of anatomic and physiologic disorders. Assists Radiologist during specialized exams to obtain images at a satisfactory level with minimal supervision.

Essential Functions

1. Interfaces with patient to ascertain medical history and provides instructions and explanation of the procedure and/or exam to obtain the best possible image.

2. Reviews patient charts for missed clinical information and/or consent. Screens patients for surgical and other implants, contrast allergies, etc.

3. Performs ultrasound scans and prints images while attending to patient’s care before, during and following exam and notifies the appropriate party if patient’s condition changes at any time.

4. Assists Radiologist on specialized exams.

5. Transfers images to other locations as needed.

6. Coordinates scan protocols with Radiologist.

7. Maintains and regularly inspects equipment and immediately reports any quality concerns as well as equipment failures or deficiencies.

8. Interfaces with Lead Technologist & Center/Area Manager regarding any and all departmental concerns.

9. Other duties as assigned.

Competencies

1. Technical Capacity.

2. Ethical Conduct.

3. Thoroughness.

4. Time Management.

5. Personal Effectiveness/Credibility.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has no supervision responsibilities.

Work Environment

This job operates in an environmentally controlled outpatient clinical environment. Potential exposure to radiation, which is minimized by the use of Personal Protective Equipment. Possible exposure to bodily fluids, communicable diseases, toxic substances, ionizing radiation and other conditions common to a medical office environment. Often requires work in cool, dimly lighted rooms.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by and employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. The employee is regularly required to use hands and fingers to handle, feel or operate objects, tools or controls and reach with hands and arms. The employee is frequently required to talk and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Travel

No travel is expected for this position.

Job Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications/Experience:

  • Two plus years’ experience in Ultrasound- preferred
  • Ability to educate patients on procedures being performed
  • Detail oriented, self-motivated, a problem solver and a team player
  • Ability to navigate multiple computer screens and browsers quickly and accurately
  • Ability to excel in a very fast-pace team environment
  • Ability to continuously “exceed” company and customer expectation
  • Strong communication skills & professional demeanor

Education/Certifications:

  • Graduate of an accredited Sonography program
  • Current ARDMS Registered Vascular Technologist (RVT) or ARRT (VS) registry – preferred
  • Current license from state medical board (if applicable)
  • Current CPR/BLS certification

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

None required for this position.

Compliance

Adheres to Envision’s Code of Conduct and Compliance Policies and attends annual Compliance training as set forth by the Company.

Company Benefits

Below is a list of benefits that are offered to employees, once eligibility is met.

  • Health Benefits: Medical/Dental/Vision/Life Insurance
  • Company Matched 401k Plan
  • Employee Stock Ownership Plan
  • Paid Time Off + Paid Holidays
  • Employee Assistance Program

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. Other duties may be assigned as needed by supervision.

title: Chief Revenue Officer- CRO
description:
CHIEF REVENUE OFFICER

Sports Facilities Management, LLC

LOCATION: Clearwater, FL/Remote

DEPARTMENT: EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP

REPORTS TO: CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER (CEO)

STATUS: FULL-TIME (EXEMPT)


ABOUT THE COMPANY:

Sports Facilities Companies (SFC) is the nation's leading resource for managing and developing sports, recreation, wellness, and events facilities. We bring together strategy, development, operations, and commercial expertise to help communities and partners create places where people play, connect, and thrive.

SFC is a mission-focused, entrepreneurial, and team-oriented company with a culture centered on collaboration, accountability, excellence, and service. We are growing rapidly and have been nationally recognized as a US Today Top Workplace for five consecutive years. Our team members are encouraged to learn from the industry's best, pursue meaningful career growth, and enjoy the journey along the way.

POSITION SUMMARY:

SFC is seeking a Chief Revenue Officer to help lead its next stage of growth. This is an opportunity to expand on an already successful foundation and build on the high-performing teams, relationships, and commercial capabilities that have helped SFC earn its position in the market.

The CRO will lead the development and execution of a unified, scalable revenue strategy across SFC. This executive will connect sales, sponsorship, corporate development, marketing-driven demand generation, account expansion, and commercial strategy into a disciplined enterprise revenue engine-creating greater visibility, consistency, and leverage across the company.

This is not a role focused on starting from scratch. The successful leader will recognize and elevate the strengths already present across SFC, partnering respectfully with current leaders and teams while adding the systems, clarity, and enterprise-wide coordination needed for the next chapter. The CRO will be both strategic and hands-on, working closely with the CEO, executive leadership, Marketing, Finance, Operations, Legal, Sales, and business-unit leaders.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:

Build on a high-performing sales foundation

  • Partner with and expand the existing, high-achieving business development team.
  • Design and implement the next generation of enterprise sales structure across management, development, advisory, consulting, sponsorship, and other revenue-generating businesses.
  • Clarify roles, territories, account ownership, quotas, reporting lines, and performance expectations while preserving the strengths of the current organization.
  • Implement rigorous pipeline-management practices covering opportunity stage, ownership, probability, next steps, TCV, ARR, renewal dates, and close timing.
  • Establish standardized pipeline reviews and forecasting processes that give leadership an accurate, predictive view of future revenue.

Scale sponsorship and corporate revenue

  • Build on SFC's existing successful national sponsorship and corporate sales strategy to significantly increase enterprise sponsorship revenue.
  • Expand scalable capabilities across naming rights, multi-venue packages, category strategy, corporate partnerships, premium inventory, and other sponsorship opportunities.
  • Establish consistent rate cards, packaging, proposal development, negotiation, and approval processes.
  • Create a unified sponsorship and corporate sales pipeline integrated with the enterprise CRM and forecasting system.
  • Increase visibility into national and local sponsorship inventory and maximize enterprise-wide revenue opportunities.

Connect marketing, demand generation, and sales conversion

  • Create an integrated revenue strategy connecting brand marketing, digital marketing, RFP capture, outbound prospecting, inbound strategies, and other demand-generation channels to measurable revenue outcomes.
  • Develop a closed-loop process from lead generation through qualification, opportunity creation, sales conversion, and closed revenue.
  • Establish meaningful measurement of marketing-generated pipeline, conversion rates, customer acquisition economics, and closed revenue.
  • Evaluate the return on investment of marketing and demand-generation strategies and direct resources toward the highest-performing channels.
  • Strengthen attribution, sales follow-up, conversion rates, and shared accountability between Marketing and Sales.

Expand existing relationships and increase long-term value

  • Identify opportunities to deepen existing relationships through additional management contracts, development and advisory services, sponsorship, incentive revenue, and other SFC capabilities.
  • Develop cross-selling strategies across SFC, Power Wellness, Spirit Golf, and other company platforms and capabilities.
  • Establish account plans for strategic clients and ensure the right level of executive engagement with high-value relationships.
  • Develop strategies to increase client retention, wallet share, revenue per account, and long-term relationship value.
  • Establish metrics and reporting that provide visibility into renewal risk, expansion potential, and account-level revenue opportunities.

Protect commercial quality, pricing, and margin

  • Partner closely with Finance, Operations, and Legal so revenue growth translates into sustainable and profitable economic value.
  • Improve pricing discipline, contract terms, fee realization, sales-cycle efficiency, and margin contribution.
  • Increase sales-cycle speed while maintaining appropriate diligence and commercial discipline.
  • Evaluate opportunities based on revenue potential, operational complexity, contractual exposure, resource requirements, strategic fit, and margin contribution.
  • Develop commercial approval processes that balance ambitious growth with disciplined risk management.

Lead enterprise performance and culture

  • Build on the capabilities of current leaders and teams to create a high-performing, ambitious, growth-oriented, and accountable revenue organization.
  • Foster a culture of performance, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish clear expectations, measurable outcomes, and development opportunities for revenue teams.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and executive leadership team.
  • Balance aggressive growth objectives with disciplined pricing, profitability, operational alignment, and risk management.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS:

  • A clear, unified revenue strategy aligned with SFC's broader business objectives.
  • More predictable pipeline generation, forecasting, conversion, and closed revenue.
  • Scalable sponsorship and corporate sales capabilities that increase enterprise value.
  • Stronger account planning, cross-selling, retention, and expansion across SFC's platforms.
  • Improved commercial discipline, pricing quality, fee realization, and margin contribution.
  • A connected revenue organization that builds on current strengths and operates with shared accountability.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in sales, revenue leadership, business development, sponsorship, or related commercial functions.
  • Significant experience leading a complex, multi-channel sales organization.
  • A demonstrated record of scaling revenue and building predictable, repeatable sales processes.
  • Experience implementing or optimizing CRM, pipeline-management, forecasting, and sales-performance systems.
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen, including experience with pricing, contracts, margins, and deal economics.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams and aligning Marketing, Sales, Finance, Operations, and Legal around shared revenue objectives.
  • Exceptional executive presence, communication, negotiation, and relationship-management skills.
  • A consistent record of recruiting, developing, coaching, and retaining high-performing sales leaders and teams.
  • Experience leading enterprise sales development teams.
  • Experience managing national sponsorships, naming-rights opportunities, corporate partnerships, or multi-location commercial programs preferred.
  • Experience integrating multiple business units or platforms into a unified revenue strategy preferred.
  • Sound judgment, strategic thinking, strong ownership, adaptability, and the ability to operate effectively at both strategic and tactical levels.

WORKING CONDITIONS AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Ability to sit for extended periods while operating a computer.
  • Ability to stand, walk, or move through office, venue, and event environments as needed.
  • Office and event environments may include intermittent noise.
  • Travel is required for client meetings, conferences, industry events, leadership meetings, venue visits, and other company-related activities.

title: SAP Technical Architect
description:
Job Description

Be part of something bigger. Decode the future.

At Electrolux Group, as a leading global appliance company, we strive every day to shape living for the better for our consumers, our people and our planet. We share ideas and collaborate so that together, we can develop solutions that deliver enjoyable and sustainable living.

Come join us as you are. We believe diverse perspectives make us stronger and more innovative. In our global community of people from 100+ countries, we listen to each other, actively contribute, and grow together.

Join us in our exciting quest to build the future home.

All about the role:

The SAP Technical Architect is a strategic role that will enable business capabilities with SAP technology. The role includes creation of technology roadmaps as well as governance and support of existing deliveries and will be instrumental in modernising Electrolux technical landscape.

Working with the landscape in Electrolux means working with a wide range of applications in a global environment. Electrolux landscape includes applications from on premise ERP, SCM, EWM, etc to public cloud solutions like IBP, CCv2, C4C, etc. There is currently a big modernisation of the landscape moving into private cloud/RISE, Integration Suite, BW/4HANA, BTP and eventually S/4HANA.

The successful candidate is passionate about driving business value from technical solutions, analysing and designing solutions and collaborating with different level of stakeholders in a global setting. You will be part of a team of global architects with expertise in different business processes and technologies.

What you'll do:

  • Create and own the SAP landscape strategy and design technical landscapes, both on premise and cloud.

  • Establish and maintain SAP technical architecture principles, standards and guardrails to ensure scalable, secure and supportable solutions across the SAP landscape, for example considering data volume and performance.

  • Define and govern non-functional requirements including security, availability, performance, resilience, recoverability and operational supportability.

  • Own architecture decisions and review proposed solutions from functional and technical teams to ensure alignment with architecture standards.

  • Collaborate with SAP, implementation partners and internal teams to jointly resolve complex issues or design solutions.

  • Provide architecture leadership and guidance in high-priority support issues.

  • Create and own the roadmap for Application Lifecycle Management to ensure the applications used are efficiently supporting the IT processes.

  • Participate in ERP modernisation program, including move to private cloud, conversion to S/4HANA and implementation of Business Data Cloud (BDC).

  • Proactively monitor innovation and emerging technologies, including AI-driven capabilities, to identify business value opportunities.

  • Mentor and provide guidance to technical and functional teams and promote architecture best practices across the organization.

Who you are:

  • You possess excellent written and oral communication skills and ability to communicate complex concepts to senior IT management, technical, functional and business teams in English.

  • Demonstrate strong business acumen, with a solid understanding of SAP business processes and the ability to influence stakeholders through effective relationship management and communication.

  • Able to work independently and as part of distributed, multi-disciplinary, multi-national teams with good collaboration skills

  • Able to deal with ambiguity and manage multiple priorities

  • A proactive learner with a strong passion for continuously expanding your knowledge and skills across SAP technologies and the broader digital ecosystem.

  • Hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

  • Fluent in English.

Required qualifications:

  • 8+ years of SAP technical platform and architecture experience, including significant experience designing and governing enterprise-scale hybrid SAP landscapes.

  • Proven experience acting as SAP Technical Architect, Lead SAP Basis Architect, SAP Platform Architect or equivalent architecture leadership role.

  • Application Lifecycle Management, including e.g. transports, monitoring, testing and documentation using Solution Manager, CloudALM and/or third party tools.

  • S/4HANA conversion, preferably with experience in optimizing downtime.

  • Experience with SAP BTP platform architecture, account models, service enablement, for example linked to AI.

Nice to have:

The following experience is a plus, but not mandatory:

  • SAP Security, including roles and authorisation design.

  • Integration technology (PI/PO, CPI, Integration Suite).

  • Custom development on stack and side-by-side in BTP or non-SAP platforms.

  • SAP licensing and commercial models (on-premise, RISE, BTP and cloud subscriptions).

  • FinOps, linking cloud consumption with financial processes, both for public cloud and credit-based solutions such as BTP, BDC, AI and PCE/RISE.

  • Experience working with Enterprise Architecture frameworks.

Where you will be:

This is a full-time position based in Electrolux Group's headquarters in Stockholm in the Stadshagen district of Kungsholmen.

We offer 20% workplace flexibility, while maintaining the collaboration, connectivity, and team spirit that come from working together at our Global Headquarters.

With more than 60 nationalities under one roof, you will be part of a dynamic international environment where English is the common language and diversity is part of everyday life.

Benefits highlights:

  • Generous vacation allowance and a range of family-friendly benefits, including extended paternity leave.

  • Comprehensive insurance coverage.

  • Discounts on our award-winning Electrolux products and services.

  • Extensive learning and development opportunities, with flexible career paths.

  • Access to in-house sports facilities.

We look forward to receiving your application!

As part of Electrolux, we will continuously invest in you and your development. There are no barriers to where your career could take you.

title: Ontologist - Expert System Integrator
description:
Ontologist – Expert System Integrator

Are you an experienced Systems Integrator with deep expertise in GEOINT, ontology frameworks, and enterprise-level systems engineering? Mission Intelligence Group is seeking a highly skilled Ontologist – Expert System Integrator to support the evolution and integration of mission-critical capabilities across the National System for Geospatial Intelligence (NSG) and Allied System for Geospatial Intelligence (ASG) enterprise. In this role, you will drive the adoption of new data sources, guide ontology governance, and ensure seamless integration of capabilities that directly support national security missions.

Your Role

As an Ontologist – Expert System Integrator, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor supporting the Government's vision for enterprise-wide systems integration and data interoperability. You will lead the design, implementation, and governance of ontology frameworks, translate mission requirements into actionable solutions, and provide expert guidance that enables efficient planning, acquisition, and execution of GEOINT capabilities. This role requires a strategic thinker who can bridge mission needs, technical architectures, and stakeholder priorities across a complex Intelligence Community environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and oversee integration efforts across the NSG/ASG systems-of-systems enterprise
  • Provide expert technical guidance relating strategy, requirements, processes, and capability development

  • Partner with Product Managers to support backlog grooming, roadmap development, and feature prioritization
  • Analyze user workflows and identify opportunities for automation and process improvement

  • Lead technical teams responsible for ontology design, implementation, governance, and lifecycle management

  • Assist Government leadership with technical planning, project management, performance engineering, risk management, and interface design
  • Maintain Agile project schedules using tools such as JIRA, Confluence, or similar platforms
  • Operate effectively within multi-contractor and Government team environments while managing competing priorities and deadlines

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in:
    • Systems Engineering
    • Computer Science
    • Information Technology
    • Management Information Systems
    • Engineering
    • Physics
    • Mathematics
    • Operations Research
    • Engineering Management
    • Ontologies

OR

  • 18+ years of experience as a Systems Integrator in lieu of a degree

  • Expert-level experience in:

    • Systems Integration
    • Systems Engineering

  • Active TS/SCI clearance adjudication or ability to obtain SCI eligibility and successfully pass a polygraph

Desired Qualifications

  • Working knowledge of:

Location

📍 100% Onsite in Springfield, Virginia

Why Mission Intelligence Group

At Mission Intelligence Group, engineers are trusted to focus on mission outcomes, not bureaucracy. You will work alongside experienced GEOINT professionals who value clear communication, disciplined engineering, and systems that work as intended in operational environments.

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including:
