title: Head of Financial Crimes Compliance for UAE and Qatar
location: AE - Dubai - Dubai International Financial Centre - ICD Brookfield Place (655804)
description:
Job Description:

Job Title: Head of Financial Crimes Compliance for UAE and Qatar

Corporate Title: Up to Director

Location: Dubai

Company Overview:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

Being a Great Place to Work and providing a culture of caring is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:


This role will serve as the Head of Financial Crimes Compliance covering the UAE and Qatar. Bank of America Merrill Lynch’s business in the region is across the Global Banking and Markets space including a Dubai-based Equities desk, investment banking, corporate banking and transaction banking. The individual will serve as the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) for Dubai and Qatar regulated entities as well as being responsible for delivering the global financial crimes compliance framework in the region.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee compliance with obligations outlined within local Financial Crimes (Anti-Money Laundering/Counter Terrorist Financing, Economic Sanctions, and Anti-Bribery/Anti-Corruption) laws, rules, and regulations.

  • Oversee implementation of Financial Crimes requirements defined by the GFC Financial Crimes Programme, in coordination with appropriate GFC Regional Executive.

  • Determine actions required to ensure MLI DIFC & QFC Branches have met specific regulatory provisions around Financial Crimes laws and regulations.

  • Discharge any specific money laundering reporting officer duties required by local laws, rules, or guidance.

  • Receive and act upon any relevant findings, recommendations, guidance, directives, resolutions, sanctions, notices or other conclusions received from competent authorities.

  • Act as the primary local point of contact for the Front Line Units on matters related to financial crime compliance.

  • Act as the principal point of contact for in-country law enforcement and regulators relative to financial crimes prevention, detection, investigation and compliance.

  • Engage, as appropriate, Branch and regional senior management on matters relating to Anti-Money Laundering, Economic Sanctions and Anti-Bribery/Anti-Corruption.

  • In coordination with the appropriate GFC Regional Executive, engage relevant stakeholders for interpretation of laws, rules or guidance related to financial crimes.

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of financial crimes compliance regulation and guidance internationally and monitor regulatory change and best practice in UAE/DIFC & Qatar/QFC.

  • Keep the deputy MLRO informed of significant AML/CFT developments (whether internal or external) and work closely with local Compliance and Operational Risk.

Policies and Procedures

  • Work with Front Line Units to design and implement local procedures consistent with the Financial Crimes Programme and help ensure their requirements are embedded within their procedures and controls.

  • Coordinate with the appropriate regional GFC team members to ensure country specific requirements are adequately considered within global policy and procedures.

  • Identify and escalate to the appropriate GFC Regional Executive any conflicts between local law and GFC standards.

  • Ensure Front Line Units adhere to policies, standards, procedures, laws and regulations.

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable financial crimes standards such as those related to high risk jurisdictions and customer types requiring Enhanced Due Diligence to be in place. Ensure appropriate approvals (as necessary) are in place, and any additional monitoring is conducted as required by local laws, regulations, or guidance.

  • Ensure records pertaining to requirements of the Financial Crimes Programme (such as Customer Due Diligence / Enhanced Customer Due Diligence / Suspicious Activity Reports) are maintained and properly stored as required by global and country specific regulations.

  • Work with appropriate GFC Regional Executive to identify gaps in the Front Line Units’ GFC Programme implementation. Provide Front Line Units oversight in fixing gaps identified in the GFC checklist.

  • Ensure that the applicable UAE & Qatar Financial Crimes Country Standards are in place, up to date and reflects all current laws, rules and regulations.

  • Accountable for the management and oversight of Non-Financial Regulatory Reporting (NFRR) obligations, including the maintenance of NFRR procedures, regulatory reporting inventories, governance controls, and the submission of financial crime-related regulatory notifications to relevant authorities.

Training

  • Lead the design, periodic review, enhancement, and delivery of risk-based AML/CFT and financial crime training programme.

  • Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify MLI DIFC and MLI QFC Branch training needs.

  • Provide or coordinate Financial Crimes training/education to staff as required by local policies, local laws or regulations.

  • Ensure continued professional competence by undertaking relevant AML/CFT, sanctions, and financial crime training and maintaining compliance with DFSA continuing professional development requirements, including a minimum of 15 hours of CPD annually.

  • Keep abreast of emerging financial crime risks, regulatory developments, enforcement actions, and industry best practices relevant to the MLRO role.

Investigations and Reporting

  • Ensure that any potentially suspicious matters are being reported to the Company’s Financial Intelligence Unit via The Referral Management System (TRMS).

  • Act as the single reference point within the Front Line Units to whom all employees are instructed to promptly refer matters potentially suspected of being connected with a financial crime.

  • Ensure that where investigations are undertaken into potentially suspicious matters the investigation is appropriately conducted and the rationale for the conclusion is well documented.

  • Make any required suspicious activity filings to law enforcement or regulatory agencies within the timelines prescribed by local laws or regulations and in compliance with the Financial Crimes Policies and Standards.

  • Keep systemic records within approved case management applications for all matters investigated (reported and not reported), including all internal findings and analysis.

  • Responsible for any additional reporting requirements defined by law, rules, or guidance (e.g., Economic Sanctions reporting requirements).

Reporting to Senior Management

  • Report potential financial crimes in region to the GFC Regional Executive as appropriate.

  • Share information on financial crimes risks and issues with GFC senior leadership.

  • Ensure that the oversight and management groups are informed of any local or international financial crimes regulatory changes.

  • Coordinate the sharing of suspicious activity information, as allowed for by law, for escalation and risk management purposes.

Monitoring and Testing

  • Lead risk assessment activities for MLI DIFC & MLI QFC Branches regular annual risk assessments and ad hoc projects; ensure risk assessments are aligned to the Global Financial Crimes Compliance template and methodologies.

  • Conduct and/or oversee Monitoring and Testing activities for the local jurisdiction to ensure required Financial Crimes controls are working effectively.

Regulatory Interaction and Interpretation of Regulations

  • Develop a strong relationship with regulators, such as the DFSA & QFCRA.

  • Deal with the DFSA/QFCRA in an open and co-operative manner and must disclose appropriately any information of which the DFSA/QFCRA would reasonably be expected to be notified.

  • Act as the point of contact for competent U.A.E. and Qatar authorities and the DFSA/QFCRA regarding money laundering issues.

  • Respond promptly to any request for information made by competent U.A.E. and Qatar authorities, the DFSA/QFCRA.

  • Coordinate any local exams and engage GFC as required.

  • Ensure prudential annual reports such as Annual AML Return is promptly filed in accordance with DFSA/QFCRA regulatory guidelines.

  • Oversee the remediation of Regulator, Corporate Audit, or Self-Identified Audit Issues, and communicate status updates to senior management and regulators as appropriate.

People Leadership and Talent Development

  • Provide day-to-day management, supervision, and development of local GFC personnel.

  • Allocate responsibilities and oversee the execution of regulatory, governance, and financial crime compliance activities.

  • Ensure staff maintain appropriate knowledge, skills, and training to effectively perform their roles.

  • Provide guidance, challenge, and support to promote a strong culture of compliance and risk management.

Required Qualifications:

  • Several years’ experience in a financial crime compliance role at an international financial services firm.

  • Several years’ experience of managing financial crimes compliance risks in the Middle East.

  • ACAMS or other relevant financial crime qualifications.

  • Experience working directly with internal audit and regulators.

  • Strong business knowledge of institutional products and services – particularly Markets and Banking.

  • Experience managing executive business stakeholder relationships as well as challenging executive business leaders when needed.

  • Team-oriented – able to partner with colleagues across the business, support function and compliance organizations

  • Good oral and written communication skills

  • Strong analytical skills; ability to communicate complex analysis to a variety of non-subject matter expert stakeholders.

  • Proactive in terms of assessing opportunities for efficiency.

  • Flexible – able to adapt to changes in the organization and business model with ease.

Skills that will help:

  • Global Risk Management experience

Bank of America:

Good conduct and sound judgment is crucial to our long-term success. It’s important that all employees in the organisation understand the expected standards of conduct and how we manage conduct risk. Individual accountability and an ownership mind-set are the cornerstones of our Code of Conduct and are at the heart of managing risk well.

title: Senior Actuarial Analyst
description:

SUMMARY:

East Texas A&M University invites nominations and applications for the position of Director and Head of the Department of Art. This twelve-month, full-time administrative appointment carries senior faculty rank with tenure. Teaching expectations will be negotiated annually with the Dean. The successful candidate will provide strategic direction and administrative leadership for a comprehensive and dynamic department, guiding its next phase by assessing program strengths and opportunities, establishing clear priorities, strengthening alignment across the Commerce and Dallas locations, supporting faculty and student success, and building key regional partnerships. The Director and Head will identify opportunities for sustainable growth and innovation while ensuring decisions are grounded in evidence, institutional priorities, and long-term viability.

East Texas A&M University seeks a strategic and experienced academic administrator to serve as Director and Head of the Department of Art, which encompasses Visual Communication (Dallas-based), Studio Art (Commerce-based), and Art Education. The department has strong foundations, including a nationally competitive professional design program, excellent facilities, dedicated faculty, and accomplished alumni, and is positioned for a leader who can unify programs across locations, assess future opportunities, and develop a shared vision for the department’s continued success.

The department is ready to welcome a forward-thinking leader who will build on these strengths and take full-time responsibility for its academic, administrative, operational, and external-facing work. Supported by the institution’s commitment to the arts, the next Director and Head will shape a unifying vision that strengthens academic programs, fosters meaningful connections across campuses, and enhances the department’s impact throughout the region and beyond.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

The Director and Head will serve as the Department of Art’s senior academic and administrative leader, with year-round responsibility for strategic direction, operations, academic programs, personnel, facilities, enrollment, and external engagement. The Director and Head is expected to devote full professional effort to leadership of the department across its Commerce and Dallas locations. The role combines inward-facing responsibilities, including strengthening programs, faculty initiatives, and student success, with outward-facing responsibilities, including partnerships, regional presence, advancement, and visibility. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

Strategic Leadership & Program Development

· Conduct a comprehensive assessment of departmental programs during the initial years of leadership, with particular attention to enrollment trends, student outcomes, regional demand, resource utilization, and long-term sustainability.

· Develop and execute a strategic plan that strengthens the department’s distinctive regional role by emphasizing community partnerships, clear academic pathways, and effective leadership.

· Align departmental strengths with institutional mission and market opportunities.

· Make evidence-informed recommendations regarding program enhancement, restructuring, consolidation, or other actions necessary to support long-term success.

· Identify opportunities for program innovation and strategic growth based on assessment findings, faculty expertise, student needs, and institutional priorities.

· Position art teacher preparation as a valued pathway alongside professional design and studio practice, with strategic recruitment and curriculum enhancement to serve regional workforce needs.

· Lead the department across its two active sites, the Commerce campus and the Dallas location, exercising full year-round executive responsibility for faculty, curriculum, facilities, budget, and operations at both locations.

· Lead curriculum development and program assessment in alignment with university standards and professional expectations.

Program Integration & Faculty Leadership

· Ensure program continuity by developing strong leadership capacity within the department and cultivating a collaborative departmental community across both sites, Commerce and Dallas, through a culture of shared responsibility, transparency, and continuous improvement.

· Support faculty productivity, professional development, and scholarly and creative activity across all program areas, including exhibitions, publications, and professional practice.

· Manage faculty across disciplines, including design professionals, studio artists, and art educators, with respect for the unique expectations and benchmarks associated with each field.

· Lead faculty through necessary programmatic changes with transparency.

· Build consensus around strategic priorities while providing clear, timely decisions.

· Ensure academic quality and program innovation at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

· Oversee faculty hiring, evaluation, promotion, and tenure processes in alignment with university policies.

Partnership & External Relations

· Develop and strengthen strategic partnerships with regional educational, cultural, industry, and community organizations that advance student opportunities, departmental visibility, and institutional priorities.

· Build and maintain relationships with public and private K-12 school districts across East Texas for teacher preparation, professional development partnerships, and community engagement.

· Cultivate relationships with DFW arts organizations, design firms, galleries, and cultural institutions to enhance student opportunities and program visibility.

· Position the department as a regional cultural leader through exhibitions, community projects, public art, and partnerships that serve East Texas communities.

· Activate and expand the alumni network across all program areas, including Visual Communication, Studio Art, and Art Education, for mentorship, career connections, and advancement support.

· Enhance departmental visibility and reputation through strategic communications, exhibitions, awards, and media engagement.

· Pursue external funding opportunities through grants and donor cultivation.

Financial & Operational Management

· Manage the department budget strategically, allocating resources to align with departmental priorities.

· Make data-informed decisions about resource allocation, scholarship strategy, graduate assistant funding, and program development.

· Implement transparent budget processes that help faculty understand resource allocation and growth opportunities.

· Oversee facilities and specialized equipment across multiple studios and labs, including ceramics, sculpture/foundry, photography, painting/drawing, Dallas design labs, and letterpress.

· Maintain and enhance the department’s physical infrastructure in coordination with university facilities.

· Ensure compliance with university policies and any applicable accreditation requirements.

· Coordinate curriculum and scheduling across the Commerce campus and Dallas location.

Student Success & Enrollment Management

· Develop and implement strategies that support enrollment stability, student retention, degree completion, and long-term program health across all departmental areas, including graduate program viability.

· Provide vision for the student experience by integrating curricular and co-curricular opportunities.

· Support student professional development through exhibitions, competitions, portfolios, internships, and industry connections.

· Oversee academic advising processes and ensure students receive appropriate guidance.

· Foster a supportive and engaging learning environment that promotes student success.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

· Terminal degree (MFA or PhD) in studio art, design, art education, or a closely related field.

· Minimum of two years of progressively responsible administrative experience as a department head, director, program director, associate/assistant dean, or equivalent leader in higher education art programs.

· Demonstrated commitment to art teacher preparation as a central component of a comprehensive art program mission, rather than a peripheral or optional function.

· Proven record of student-focused initiatives associated with increased enrollment, retention, and graduation.

· Understanding of both professional design practice and studio arts traditions, with the ability to value and integrate multiple approaches to art-making and creative careers rather than privileging one over others.

· Demonstrated experience using evidence-informed decision-making to support program improvement, strategic planning, and resource stewardship.

· Record of building productive partnerships with academic units, K-12 institutions, or community organizations.

· Strong interpersonal and communication skills combined with demonstrated ability to make unpopular decisions when necessary for program health.

· Commitment to shared governance, faculty development, and student success.

· Eligibility for appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure. The appointment carries faculty rank and tenure, and the position is a twelve-month administrative appointment with teaching expectations to be negotiated annually with the Dean.

PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:

· Prior experience rebuilding, reimagining, or significantly restructuring graduate programs at regional comprehensive universities.

· Deep understanding of regional graduate education markets and competition, with demonstrated success in positioning programs distinctively.

· Experience with innovative graduate program models, including low-residency, cohort-based, community-engaged, or interdisciplinary models, beyond the traditional residential MFA.

· Track record of addressing structural enrollment challenges through programmatic change.

· Professional connections in the design or advertising industry, preferably in the DFW region, or a significant exhibition record and professional recognition in studio arts.

· Experience developing interdisciplinary programs or certificates involving multiple colleges or departments.

· Experience managing geographically distributed or multi-site programs, or demonstrated ability to lead across locations and integrate separated units.

· Grant-writing experience and successful external funding acquisition for program development or facilities enhancement.

· Understanding of creative technologies and their strategic integration with traditional studio practice.

· Fundraising and donor-relations experience.

· Experience at regional comprehensive universities balancing access, excellence, teacher preparation, and professional and creative practice missions.

· Knowledge of Texas teacher certification requirements and the K-12 art education landscape.

· Experience managing complex budgets and making strategic resource allocation decisions.

SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:

Full-time and part-time faculty and staff

COMPENSATION:

Competitive. Please note this is a 12-month administrative role with limited teaching responsibilities, established and reviewed annually in consultation with the Dean of the College.

NOMINATION/APPLICATION PROCESS:

The Search Committee will begin its review of applications on October 12, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For priority consideration, all materials must be received by October 9, 2026. Zoom interviews are scheduled for the first week of November, with finalist campus visits planned before Thanksgiving. Candidates for the position are asked to make themselves available for interviews during these times.

Application materials should include: (1) a letter of interest that addresses how the candidate’s experience and qualifications intersect with the priorities and desired leadership characteristics outlined in this profile; (2) a curriculum vitae; and (3) the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses of three references for future contact, including the professional relationship of each reference.

Applications must be submitted electronically through East Texas A&M University.

The starting date for the position is negotiable, with January 1, 2027 welcomed as a possible start date.

The search committee will be chaired by Dr. Debbie Lelekis, Associate Dean of the College of Humanities, Social Sciences & Arts and Professor of English. Nominations should be provided to Dr. Lelekis by email at Debbie.Lelekis@etamu.edu. Arrangements for a conversation about the opportunity may also be made with Dr. Lelekis.

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

Job Title

Sr. Director, Network Administration and Governance - MoneyPass Group

Sr. Director, Network Administration and Governance

We are seeking a Sr. Director of Network Administration and Governance to lead operational support, rule administration, and governance for the MoneyPass network. This role is responsible for maintaining the integrity, consistency, and effectiveness of network operating rules that support surcharge-free cash access at more than 70,000 ATMs nationwide.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the administration, maintenance, and governance of network operating rules for networks owned and operated by MPG.
  • Responsible for supporting rule management, compliance, and operational governance objectives.
  • Partner with pricing and analytics, product management, strategy, legal, and leadership teams to update, maintain, and release operating rules for existing and new network products and capabilities.

  • Oversee the MoneyPass Locator and ensure members and participants remain compliant with MoneyPass guidelines, including enforcement of fines or penalties for unresolved infractions.

  • Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities that increase efficiency, consistency, and scalability.
  • Provide routine updates to operating rules based on federal regulatory changes, industry evolution, corporate initiatives, and business priorities.
  • Collaborate with internal and external groups to understand, interpret, and deliver rule updates in a concise manner that can be understood by all MoneyPass network members and participants.
  • Translate operating rules into practical guidance and content for internal teams, external partners, clients, members, and participants.
  • Stay current on payments industry trends, terminology, and regulatory considerations to support informed rule administration and governance.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, technology, or a related field preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to tailor messaging for executive, internal, client, partner, member, and participant audiences.
  • Proven experience writing, editing, reviewing, and accurately distributing business-critical information.

  • Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and recommend effective solutions.

Ability to travel up to 10% as needed.

For complex agent implementations, coordinate troubleshooting and technical escalations with Professional Services, Product and Engineering to resolve blockers quickly.

  • Channel & Adoption Strategy: Own the channel strategy for AI solution dissemination and adoption, balancing direct customer delivery with channel enablement and partner engagement.
  • Measure and Drive Impact: Utilize data-driven insights to track AI adoption, resolution metrics, and gross revenue retention improvements. Continuously refine strategies to optimize outcomes and customer satisfaction.
  • Responsible AI & Compliance: Confidently advise customers on ethical AI practices, data governance, and compliance considerations — framing use cases within safe, explainable, and policy‑aligned guardrails.

What You’ll Need to Succeed

Strategic Skills & Expertise

  • Project & Program Management: Proven ability to orchestrate multi-phase technology adoption projects, managing diverse teams and timelines with clarity and agility.
  • Product and Technical Knowledge: Product expert who assesses customers' use case automation potential and technical readiness (generative AI, integrations, authentication), helps craft user journeys and translates features into value. Liaise with ProdDev teams to remove blockers for adoption, implement fixes and provide feedback on (beta) features.

  • Consultation & Communication: Strong stakeholder engagement skills—whether customer executives or internal teams—to advance AI adoption and sustain strategic partnerships.
  • Analytical & Outcome-Focused: Strong analytical capacity to interpret adoption data, develop predictive health scores, forecast retention/expansion, and translate metrics into prioritized action plans.
  • Forward-Thinking & Pragmatic: Visionary in embracing AI’s potential with a grounded, realistic approach to execution—balancing innovation with practical delivery feasibility.

Qualifications

  • Must have a minimum of 5+ years of related experience in Customer Success / Experience, 1+ years of AI related experience
  • Previous experience in go-to-customer/GTM roles in enterprise technology / SaaS — either customer success management, professional services/consulting, technical account management, or solutions engineering/pre-sales consulting
  • Demonstrated experience in using adoption and health analytics to forecast churn and expansion; surface early risk signals and recommended mitigations to secure retention and growth.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degrees; certifications in AI strategy or project management preferred.
  • Experience managing AI or software adoption programs with demonstrated impact on business metrics such as retention or satisfaction.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and executing success plans or roadmaps that drive measurable customer outcomes
  • Excellent program management and cross-functional influence skills.
  • Familiarity with emerging AI trends is a plus
  • Ability to distill complex AI concepts for diverse audiences, especially executive stakeholders.

Great to have

  • AI Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of AI capabilities within Zendesk’s platform, not necessarily hands-on technical, but sufficient to translate product features into business value and strategic initiatives.

100% Onsite

title: Tub Seaming Line Manufacturing Operator
description:
Job Description

Tub Seaming Line Manufacturing Operator

Support bringing the right people in the right place.

By creating desirable solutions and great experiences that enrich people’s daily lives and the health of our planet, we want to be a driving force in delivering enjoyable and sustainable living. We go to work every day determined to shape living for the better – for our customers and for the health of our planet.

For that, we employ great people from a wide variety of backgrounds – not just because it’s the right thing to do, but also because we believe that diverse perspectives make our business stronger and more innovative. If you share our values, come find your place in our global community.

You will be based in our Kinston, NC location. The shift will start at 7 am and end at 3:30 pm. This role supports the production line and will follow production needs.

Please be advised that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position at this time.

Summary:

The Tub Seaming Line Operator – Level 5 is a senior-level production role responsible for operating, monitoring, and optimizing tub seaming line manufacturing equipment to ensure safe, efficient, and high-quality output. This role serves as a subject matter expert on tub seaming line operations, provides guidance to lower-level operators, leads advanced troubleshooting efforts, and supports continuous improvement initiatives.

Your main tasks:

  • Operate and monitor automated and semi-automated tub seaming line equipment at advanced proficiency levels.
  • Perform advanced machine setup, changeovers, and calibrations to meet production schedules and specifications.
  • Troubleshoot complex mechanical, electrical, and process-related issues; coordinate with maintenance as needed.
  • Lead quality assurance efforts by ensuring products meet all specifications, regulatory requirements, and customer standards.
  • Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, reduce waste, and minimize downtime.
  • Train, coach, and mentor Tub Seaming Line Operators Levels 1–4 on procedures, safety, and best practices.
  • Review production documentation and ensure accurate completion of logs, batch records, and inspection reports.
  • Enforce safety policies and participate in safety audits, incident investigations, and corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with engineering, quality, and supervision teams on new products, equipment upgrades, and continuous improvement projects.
  • Serve as acting lead or backup supervisor when assigned.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or GED required, technical certification or associate degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of manufacturing experience, with significant experience operating tub line or similar production equipment.
  • Advanced knowledge of manufacturing processes, quality systems, and safety standards.
  • Proven ability to diagnose and resolve complex equipment and process issues.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Basic computer skills (production systems, data entry, email).
  • Ability to lead by example and effectively communicate with team members and leadership.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement training.
  • Forklift or industrial equipment certification.

Physical Demands:

  • Must be able to lift packages 40 lbs. or less on a consistent basis
  • Should be able to team lift any package greater than 35 lbs. but less than 71 lbs.
  • Should be able to handle repetitive twisting, lifting, pulling, pushing, reaching, and bending
  • Must be able to spend long periods of time on your feet
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disability to perform the essentials functions of the job.

Benefits:

At Electrolux, we take responsibility for our development in a supportive environment where we embrace our differences and learn from each other. In a truly multicultural setting, we shape living for the better and create remarkable experiences for employees and consumers, all around the globe.

title: Director, Full-Time MBA Program
description:
Job Title

Director, Full-Time MBA Program

Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

Mba Program Office

Proposed Minimum Salary

$14,583.34 monthly

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

A Glimpse of the Job

As Director of the Full-Time MBA Program, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for one of Mays Business School's premier graduate programs. In this highly visible role, you will guide the program's strategy, market positioning, student experience, and long-term success within the evolving landscape of graduate business education. Working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders, you will help shape and deliver an exceptional MBA experience from a candidate's first interaction with the program through graduation and career placement. As the program's primary advocate and connector, you will build strong relationships with students, faculty, employers, alumni, and institutional partners to ensure the program remains innovative and responsive to market needs. This is an exciting opportunity to lead the next chapter of the Full-Time MBA Program, leverage the strengths of Texas A&M University and Mays Business School, and explore new approaches to graduate business education.

What You Need to Know

Salary: $175,000 per year.

Cover Letter/Resume: A cover letter and resume will assist us in our review of your application materials. These can be uploaded on the application under CV/Resume.

Other Requirements and Factors: Some travel and evening/weekend work required.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in applicable field or equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Ten years of progressively responsible experience in management, program leadership, higher education, business, or a related field.

A Well-Qualified Candidate Will Also Possess:

  • Master’s degree; MBA or other graduate business degree preferred.

  • Leadership experience in higher education, graduate management education, business, or another complex, market-facing organization.

  • Experience leading a program, business unit, product, service, or other enterprise with responsibility for strategy and measurable outcomes.

  • Supervisory and team leadership experience.

  • Experience working across organizational boundaries and engaging senior leaders and external stakeholders.

  • Ability to lead change, foster innovation, and exercise sound judgment in complex and uncertain environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically and translate strategy into clear priorities, executable plans, and measurable outcomes.

  • Ability to understand student, employer, and market needs and translate them into a compelling value proposition and improvements in programs and experiences.

  • Strong leadership and team-building skills, including the ability to develop people, establish accountability, and create a collaborative culture.

  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-management skills, with the ability to build trust, work across organizational boundaries, and lead through both authority and influence.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to represent the program effectively with internal and external audiences.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and execution skills, including the ability to use quantitative and qualitative information to inform decisions and move complex initiatives from concept to implementation.

  • Ability to navigate a complex academic institution while maintaining a commitment to integrity, continuous improvement, and student success.

Opportunities to Contribute

Program Strategy and Leadership

  • Provides strategic leadership and overall direction for the Full-Time MBA Program, establishing priorities, goals, measures of success, and short- and long-term strategies related to recruiting and admissions outcomes.

  • Monitors developments in graduate management education, employer needs, student expectations, and the MBA market and translates those insights into program strategy and innovation.

  • Builds alignment among faculty, staff, students, school leadership, and other key stakeholders around the program’s direction and priorities.

  • Leads, develops, and supervises program staff, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and student success.

  • Works collaboratively with the leaders of other Mays graduate programs to identify opportunities for shared learning, coordination, innovation, and efficient use of resources.

  • Serves as a member of the Graduate Programs leadership team, representing the Full-Time MBA Program in broader school and university planning and contributing to strategy and initiatives across the Mays graduate portfolio.

Student Experience and Program Success

  • Leads an integrated, high-quality Full-Time MBA student experience from enrollment through graduation, maintaining strong relationships with students and an active understanding of their needs and experiences.

  • Works with faculty and staff to strengthen student engagement, belonging, professional development, academic and co-curricular experiences, retention, and overall student success.

  • Uses student feedback and outcomes to drive continuous program improvement.

  • Partners closely with Career Management to support student career readiness, internship and employment outcomes, and alignment between the program experience and evolving employer expectations.

  • Works with students and appropriate university partners to address complex student issues and ensure consistent, fair, and student-centered application of policies and procedures.

Market Position, Recruitment, and External Engagement

  • Serves as a visible advocate and spokesperson for the Full-Time MBA Program with prospective and admitted students, alumni, employers, advisory groups, professional organizations, and other external stakeholders.

  • Responsible for recruitment, admissions, marketing, and communications teams to develop and execute strategies that strengthen the program’s market position and attract a robust pool of prospective students who are well matched to the program.

  • Provides program leadership and subject-matter expertise in defining the Full-Time MBA value proposition, recruitment and admissions strategy, enrollment goals, and desired cohort composition.

  • Develops strong relationships with alumni, employers, corporate partners, and advisory groups to strengthen the program and create opportunities for students.

  • Partners with Career Management and other Mays units to strengthen employer engagement and connections between the program, students, and the marketplace.

Curriculum, Innovation, and Educational Experience

  • Works with graduate program leadership and faculty, contributing student, employer, and market evidence to curriculum discussions and surfacing recommendations for change, while faculty retain ownership of academic content and curricular approval.

  • Identifies and helps develop curricular, experiential, leadership, and professional development opportunities that strengthen the Full-Time MBA experience.

  • Supports assessment of program learning outcomes and uses findings to inform continuous improvement and innovation.

Operations, Assessment, and Stewardship

  • Manages the program’s budget and other resources in alignment with strategic priorities.

  • Uses enrollment, student, financial, career, market, and other relevant data to evaluate program performance and inform decisions.

  • Oversees program assessment, reporting, and required data requests, including those related to accreditation and rankings.

  • Ensures compliance with applicable requirements and identifies staffing, technology, facility, and other resources needed to achieve program goals.

Who We Are

Texas A&M University’s Mays Business School is a vibrant learning organization of more than 175 faculty members, 125 staff members, and 6,400 undergraduate and graduate students in accounting, finance, management, management information systems, marketing, and supply chain management. Mays Business School’s vision is to advance the world’s prosperity. To advance the world’s prosperity means providing a better future for generations who follow, including quality of life, environment, and economic systems. To fulfill this vision, our mission is to be a vibrant learning organization that creates impactful knowledge and develops transformational leaders.

Mays Business School Graduate Programs: Mays offers Full-Time, Professional, Executive, Flex Online MBA programs as well as a unique MBA + M.S. Analytics program. Our program helps students advance their careers by mastering core business knowledge, honing skills through high impact learning experiences, developing personalized leadership styles, and leveraging the power of the global Aggie Network.

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

  • Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts, and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums

  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays

  • Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month

  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas

  • Health and Wellness: Free exercise programs and release time

  • Professional Development: All employees have access to free LinkedIn Learning training, webinars, and limited financial support to attend conferences, workshops, and more

  • Educational release time and tuition assistance for completing a degree while a Texas A&M employee

  • Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experience. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.

Instructions to Applicants: Applications received by Texas A&M University must either have all job application data entered or a resume attached. Failure to provide all job application data or a complete resume could result in an invalid submission and a rejected application. We encourage all applicants to upload a resume or use a LinkedIn profile to pre-populate the online application.

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

The role provides experienced financial and compliance guidance, anticipates potential issues, supports sound decision-making, and works across teams to develop practical solutions that strengthen grant performance and financial stewardship.

The Director of Grants & Financial Administration will also develop and maintain strong partnerships with local, state, and federal government agencies and other funding organizations, helping to maximize grant and fundraising opportunities, ensure grants and programs operate efficiently and in compliance with applicable requirements, and support the New England Aquarium's overall financial strength and mission.

This is a full-time regular position offering a comprehensive benefits package. The schedule will be Monday-Friday 9:00 am - 5:00 pm with the option for a hybrid schedule, working some days on-site and some days remotely. Remote days are only available for residents of MA, RI, NH, ME, NY and VT.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Manage and coordinate the financial administration of grants and contracts throughout the full grant lifecycle, including pre-award, post-award, financial monitoring, reporting, and closeout.
  2. Optimize the grant administration process by coordinating with grant writers and internal partners, managing timelines and deliverables, tracking grant applications, and preparing and monitoring budgets and financial reports.
  3. Manage and support the proposal development process in partnership with the Development Office and other relevant staff, ensuring compliance with New England Aquarium and sponsor policies and managing proposed budgets for appropriate costing, indirect costs, and cost-sharing.
  4. Conduct thorough due diligence on subrecipient budget submissions, ensuring costs are reasonable, supportable, allowable, and compliant with funder and sponsor requirements.
  5. Collaborate closely with the Controller and Associate Director of Accounting on cost share, indirect cost recovery, budget requirements, and other financial considerations during proposal development.
  6. Ensure all internal approvals, certifications, representations, and authorized signatures are obtained prior to proposal submission.
  7. Ensure the timely and accurate submission of proposals.
  8. Negotiate with government funders and other sponsors regarding scope, budget, and grant or contract terms and conditions, in partnership with the manager, PI, Accounting, and other key stakeholders.
  9. Review new grant and contract award documents and subsequent modifications for compliance, financial requirements, and special award conditions.
  10. Produce and maintain grant fact sheets and records, including approved budgets, in the New England Aquarium's financial system, and proactively communicate key financial and award information to PIs, leadership, and relevant grant management staff.
  11. Provide proactive financial oversight of assigned grants, including budget-to-actual monitoring, expenditure review, forecasting, and identification of potential under-spending, over-spending, or other financial concerns.
  12. Advise PIs, project directors, and managers on adherence to grant award terms, conditions, budgets, and government regulations. Provide ongoing grant financial progress reports and proactively identify potential budget, compliance, or reporting concerns.
  13. Partner across departments to resolve grant-related financial and compliance issues, promote shared accountability, and ensure timely communication and follow-through.
  14. Serve as the New England Aquarium's primary interface with government program specialists, contracting officers, and sponsor representatives on compliance and reporting matters. Build effective, professional partnerships with funders and external stakeholders.
  15. Proactively identify financial, operational, and compliance risks related to grants and contracts and work collaboratively with appropriate stakeholders to develop practical and timely solutions.
  16. Identify opportunities to strengthen grant administration processes, financial controls, reporting, and cross-functional workflows to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
  17. Ensure grant files are complete, accurate, organized, and audit-ready in accordance with government rules, regulations, and sponsor requirements.
  18. Maintain a high degree of professionalism and work collaboratively with individuals and teams throughout the organization and with externally sponsored program representatives.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Training and Experience

  • A degree in business administration, finance, accounting, or an equivalent field.
  • A minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in grants administration, grants finance, sponsored programs, or contract administration is required; extensive hands-on experience managing complex grants and contracts is strongly preferred.
  • Proven success with compliance and financial administration of grant and contract awards throughout the full lifecycle, including pre-award and post-award activities.
  • Strong budgeting and accounting experience with knowledge of auditing policies and donor and funding-agency requirements.
  • Experience presenting findings, financial information, and recommendations to senior leadership.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Thorough understanding of GAAP, Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), and applicable federal grant requirements; knowledge of relevant OMB guidance preferred.
  • In-depth knowledge of sponsored program policies established by government awarding and regulatory agencies and an understanding of the roles and authority of program and contracting officers.
  • Strong partnership and collaboration skills with the ability to build trusted working relationships across Finance, Accounting, Development, Programs, leadership, and external funders.
  • Proactive and solutions-oriented approach with the ability to anticipate needs, identify risks or issues early, and follow through to resolution.
  • Demonstrated ability to work proactively, exercise sound judgment, identify issues early, and develop practical solutions in partnership with internal stakeholders.
  • Strong financial analysis, budgeting, monitoring, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong customer-service orientation and ability to work cooperatively with employees and management at all levels.
  • Ability to communicate complex financial and grant requirements clearly and present findings and recommendations to a variety of audiences.
  • Methodical and strategic thinking with strong judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Excellent organizational and project management skills.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, computerized General Ledger and other business systems. Advanced knowledge of Excel and spreadsheet design techniques is essential.
  • Well-organized, with strong attention to detail and the ability to consistently meet deadlines and manage multiple priorities.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Programming: Working proficiency in Power Apps, Power Automate, C#, Python and VBA/macros; ability to produce readable, reusable and supportable code.

Delivery capability: Requirements analysis, solution design, data mapping, testing, deployment, documentation and production support.

Professional skills: Structured problem-solving, stakeholder communication and the ability to work independently across business and technical teams in a consulting environment.

Secure and stable integrations; accurate and timely data exchange; reduced manual processing; clear technical documentation; effective user adoption; and solutions that are scalable, supportable and aligned with project governance and enterprise IT standards.

title: Petroleum Engineer Sand Management
description:
Job Family Group:

Subsurface Group


Job Description:

Please note that roles based out of SJS or Sunbury will move to Timber Square, Southwark, from Q4 2027.

Our purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. For over 100 years, bp has focused on discovering, developing, and producing oil and gas in the nations where we operate. We are one of the few companies globally that can provide governments and customers with an integrated energy offering. Delivering our strategy sustainably is fundamental to achieving our ambition to be a net zero company by 2050 or sooner!

Role Purpose

Over the past five years, sand‑related deferrals have routinely exceeded 2 mboed net (~1.3 mmboe/yr) equivalent to ~$80MM/yr at $60/bbl. This excludes the additional opex and capex required to restore well capacity, often resulting in paying twice for the same reserves and consuming rig time that could otherwise be directed toward new wells.

With lower oil prices and increasing development complexity, improving production reliability, capital efficiency, and simplicity becomes even more critical. In several operating regions (e.g., North Sea, Deepwater GoM, Asia Pacific), as well as for water injectors, the range of viable mechanical sand‑control options is often limited to lower cost solutions like Standalone Screens or Cased and Perforated, which increases the need for higher‑confidence sand prediction and assurance, particularly in environments that fall outside our historical operating experience.

As a greater share of production comes from complex, sand‑prone reservoirs, and as well costs continue to rise, bp requires an integrated sand management strategy that can detect, mitigate, and remediate sanding risks early. Strengthening sand management in operated assets also enhances our influence in NOJV and JV partnerships, which represent a material portion of our capital and production delivery.

The Sand Management Senior Petroleum Engineer plays a critical role by providing deep technical insight, integrating surveillance and modeling, shaping safe operating envelopes, and driving reliability across the four chokes (reservoir, well, facility, export). The role establishes standards and best practices, represents bp in partner and industry engagements, and leads capability‑building initiatives to elevate technical excellence across the organization.

About the Team

Global Subsurface Solutions (GSS) leverages global experience to deliver prioritized, fit-for-purpose products and unbiased technical support to regional businesses. The Sand Management Central Team plays a critical role in safeguarding asset integrity, optimizing production, and embedding proactive sand management practices across bp’s global portfolio.

Key Accountabilities

  • Provide technical guidance on sanding challenges, integrating surveillance data, predictive modeling, and mitigation strategies.

  • Influence regional safe operating envelopes and sand management plans through technical assurance and best practice recommendations.

  • Develop and maintain global standards, processes, and guidelines for sand management.

  • Lead capability-building initiatives, including training programs, knowledge-sharing sessions, and mentoring to uplift sand management competencies globally.

  • Collaborate with multi-discipline teams (completions, interventions, flow assurance, erosion-corrosion, operations, and subsurface) to embed proactive sand management strategies.

  • Ensure integration of sand management practices across the four chokes – reservoir, well, facility, and export – to deliver holistic sand management solutions.

  • Drive technology innovation and adoption, including digital tools and AI/ML applications for predictive sand management.

  • Represent bp in partner discussions, joint ventures, and industry forums to promote technical leadership and collaboration.

  • Document lessons learned, case studies, and best practices to continuously improve sand management delivery.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree or equivalent in Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related disciplines.

  • Experience in sand management, well integrity, and production optimization within oil and gas operations.

  • Strong technical expertise in surveillance integration, predictive modeling, and sand control strategies.

  • Proven ability to influence global standards and collaborate across multi-discipline and multi-region teams.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, including external representation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with advanced sand modeling tools and predictive analytics platforms.

  • Experience in industry forums, technical committees, and joint venture engagements.

  • Demonstrated leadership in capability-building and technical assurance roles.

Skills

  • Technical assurance and standardization

  • Predictive modeling and surveillance integration

  • Stakeholder engagement and external representation

  • Training and capability development

  • Continuous improvement and technology adoption

  • Curiosity, coachability and courage

Travel Requirement

Up to 10% global travel may be required for partner engagements, industry forums, and regional capability-building initiatives.

Success Measures

  • Adoption of global sand management standards and processes across regions.

  • Reduction in sanding-related well failures and unplanned deferrals.

  • Increased technical capability and competency uplift in regional teams.

  • Positive representation of bp in industry forums and partner engagements.

Why join us?

At bp, we support our people to grow in a diverse and exciting environment. We believe that our team is strengthened by diversity.

There are many aspects of our employees’ lives that are meaningful, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life. These benefits can include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, excellent retirement benefits, among others!

title: Associate, Enterprise Strategy & Planning

We are currently seeking a strategic and collaborative Associate, Enterprise Strategy & Planning.

In the highly impactful role, you will help develop the long-range plans for Guardian and partner with key stakeholders to identify, develop, evaluate, prioritize and deliver strategic initiatives across the organization. You will support internal consulting engagements to solve critical strategic questions for the Guardian Leadership Team, working with senior sponsors, business units, and corporate functions, while partnering closely with the rest of the Enterprise Strategy team.

A successful candidate will work across the Enterprise Strategy & Transformation team to provide strategic frameworks and deliver on critical strategy projects. You will structure problem-solving, conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses of operational and financial data, and organize industry/ competitor research to continuously evaluate Guardian’s positioning. You will also synthesize your findings for senior-level audiences through both written and verbal communications. This position offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to Guardian's business while creating pathways for long-term career development and internal mobility.

The role reports to Guardian’s Head of Enterprise Strategy & Planning. You will partner closely with Guardian’s Corporate Development, AI Strategic Transformation, and Finance teams, as well as counterparts in business units and corporate functions.

Your work will span across:

Enterprise-wide strategy development – Work to define the strategic direction, with both near-term and long-term priorities for Guardian. This will be supported by research, analytics, and logical problem solving and strategic frameworks.

Internal strategy consulting – working with a senior sponsor, execute deep-dive strategy projects on high priority topics for the business units and corporate functions

Strategic planning – support with the enterprise-wide processes that drive strategy, including objectives and target setting, portfolio planning, and quarterly progress updates.

Growth initiatives and innovation – assess or develop business cases for new ideas driving innovation, partnerships, and other areas of investment outside of BAU. Identify, frame, and implement specific cross-cutting strategic initiatives that are critical to the success of Guardian’s overall strategy.

Prepare materials for senior leadership –in partnership with the Enterprise Strategy team, develop agenda, content, and analysis for key strategic fora, including the annual Strategy Session of the Board and the annual Guardian Leadership Team Strategic Planning offsite

You are:

  • A strategic problem-solver, with demonstrated experience in using frameworks and analysis to support data-driven recommendations
  • Experienced in conducting analysis on short time frames and with limited data, in a consulting-style approach
  • Highly organized and efficient, with ability to prioritize across multiple projects and competing demands at any given time
  • An effective communicator (both oral and written) with ability to work well on cross-functional teams
  • Results-oriented and pragmatic; looking to make real, tangible impact and ensure that recommendations can be effectively operationalized
  • Proactive and resourceful, a self-starter
  • Intellectually curious and innovation minded; always asking “what’s next?”

You have:

Required:

  • Strong problem-solving skills
  • Demonstrated experience with quantitative and qualitative analysis
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
  • Strong command of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
  • 3+ years’ experience working in roles related to strategy & management consulting within a top consulting firm or internal strategy within a financial services company

  • Work on interesting, complex strategic problems with a chance to make a tangible impact
  • Get exposure to a variety of functions and businesses across Guardian
  • Build a network of peers and collaborators across business units
  • Receive hands-on mentorship and coaching from experienced leaders at Guardian

title: Construction Scheduling Analyst
description:
Summary

The Construction Schedule Analyst is a foundational role within the Clark Planning & Scheduling Department. This position is designed for a detail-oriented individual who excels at data manipulation and logical problem-solving. You will support the Project Schedulers by managing the flow of data into Primavera P6, using Excel to audit schedule health, and creating reports that track project milestones.

This role is part of a structured career path in construction planning and scheduling. No prior construction experience is required; we provide technical training for Primavera P6 for candidates who demonstrate high-level analytical potential and a "quick-study" approach to new software.

Responsibilities

  • Commit to an accelerated learning path to become a power user in Primavera P6.

  • Work closely with Project Schedulers to explore the nuances of the Critical Path Method (CPM) and how it applies to complex construction sequencing.

  • On Site support of project teams to update schedules, expand activity detail, adjust construction sequencing, and produce internal and contractually required reporting.

  • Data Analysis and Advanced Reporting utilizing Primavera P6, Microsoft Excel, PowerBI and other industry specific tools.

  • Calculate and report on Project Metrics Total Float and Schedule Performance metrics to help the department identify potential bottlenecks.

  • Identify patterns in historical data to help Project Teams predict future project outcomes.

  • Quality Control: Ensure all schedule data adheres to standards for naming conventions, activity coding, and organizational breakdown.

Basic Qualifications

  • Undergraduate or Associates degree in construction management, engineering, data analysis, mathematics, computer science, business, finance, accounting, or a related field

  • Excel Proficiency

  • An innate interest in troubleshooting data discrepancies and finding the "why" behind the numbers.

  • Ability to summarize and communicate complex data findings

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Primavera P6

  • Results Oriented - Experience in using data to anticipate and solve problems, manage risk and analyze business needs to deliver high quality outcomes

  • Self Motivated - Takes initiative and personal responsibility to deliver value and excellence in all that you do

  • Team Player - Builds interpersonal relationships and collaborators with internal team members, trade partners, architects and clients.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: Given that a good portion of your day will be spent at a desk, you should be comfortable with prolonged periods of focused work, whether it's collaborating with colleagues, analyzing data, or developing strategies. The role demands effective communication and sharp visual acuity for reviewing complex documents and performing detailed computer work. While there are times for quiet concentration, you'll also be expected to move actively throughout the office and travel occasionally to various locations, including dynamic construction sites, utilizing different modes of transportation. The ability to lift and move objects up to 10 pounds regularly, and up to 25 pounds on occasion (think a box of files or small office equipment), is also required.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines. Beyond regular working hours, there will be occasions where business needs require your attention, particularly for time-sensitive matters or emergencies. You are expected to monitor and respond to communications (phone calls, emails, text messages) as required to address these situations effectively. Your ability to manage these expectations and be responsive when critical issues arise is key to your success in this role and our collective success as a team.

A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment drug “fitness for duty” screening is required, and the company conducts random quarterly drug “fitness for duty” tests.

Clark offers a total compensation package that includes base salary, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision benefits, paid time off, retirement/401k, and Company Contribution plan. Additional benefits include life insurance, commuter benefit, short & long term disability, fitness reimbursement, FSA, tuition reimbursement, back-up daycare, tutoring & family support benefits, EAP/Work-Life assistance, and a holiday contribution program. For this role the base salary range is $80,500 - $95,000. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. Base pay is one part of the Total Compensation Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work. https://www.clarkconstruction.com/careers/clark-experience

title: FT Faculty-Clinical Education Lead
description:
Help shape the future of prelicensure nursing education by combining clinical teaching, faculty development and leadership, simulation and lab education, and healthcare partnership engagement across a growing clinical network.

The Full-Time Faculty and Clinical Education Lead is a non-tenure track faculty position in the College of Nursing and Health Sciences. Reporting to the Assistant Dean, Lab and Clinical Education, this remote role supports prelicensure nursing education through clinical instruction, skills lab and simulation facilitation, student supervision, clinical faculty development, and clinical partner engagement. The faculty member serves as an academic and operational resource supporting implementation of the College's clinical education strategy and consistent, high-quality learning environments across clinical, laboratory, and simulation settings. The role collaborates with academic leadership, lab faculty, clinical operations, course faculty, part-time clinical instructors, and healthcare partners to advance student learning, faculty effectiveness, competency-based evaluation, clinical judgment, NCLEX-RN readiness, and clinical education quality. Preference will be given to candidates located in New York State or the Southeastern United States. Regular travel to clinical partner sites is required, with flexibility for clinical schedules, site visits, lab and simulation activities, and occasional evening or weekend commitments.

This position is based out of the university’s home office in Albany, NY with the option of considering remote candidates. Remote employees will have mandatory occasional travel for meetings, conferences, and professional development opportunities. Remote employees are expected to be available during work hours 8:30 am – 5:00 pm Eastern time. The University will supply necessary equipment to perform the essential functions of this job (e.g., Laptop, docking station). Employees are responsible for having a workspace where they can participate in virtual meetings without multiple interruptions and noise.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Teach, facilitate, and evaluate prelicensure students in clinical, skills lab, and simulation environments.
  • Provide direct clinical instruction based on program needs, faculty coverage, site requirements, and emerging priorities.
  • Supervise and mentor students in safe nursing practice, clinical judgment, psychomotor skills, professionalism, and licensure readiness.
  • Apply course outcomes, competency expectations, evaluation criteria, policies, and grading standards consistently.
  • Identify and escalate student learning, safety, professionalism, and performance concerns; support remediation and student success strategies.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, orientation, development, mentoring, retention, and evaluation of part-time clinical instructors.
  • Conduct clinical faculty observations, site visits, evaluations, and coaching; promote consistent clinical teaching and evaluation practices.
  • Cultivate clinical partnerships through communication, site visits, needs assessment, timely follow-up, and collaboration with clinical operations.
  • Identify prospective clinical sites aligned with curriculum, accreditation, geographic, and placement-capacity needs.
  • Support partnership discussions, agreement development or renewal, partner onboarding, and resolution of placement-related concerns.
  • Collaborate on clinical, lab, and simulation quality improvement, curriculum implementation, program assessment, accreditation, and NCLEX preparation.
  • Represent the School of Nursing professionally with students, faculty, healthcare partners, consortiums, and external stakeholders.

Qualifications: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Hold a Master's degree in Nursing or higher from an accredited institutions.
  • Maintain an active, unencumbered Registered Nurse (RN) license in New York, Florida, and Tennessee, or obtain required licensure by the date of hire.
  • Demonstrate a minimum of five years of registered nursing experience across diverse clinical settings, including care of patients across the lifespan and current acute care hospital experience.
  • Bring recent experience in prelicensure clinical nursing education; three years of experience preferred.
  • Maintain current CPR certification and demonstrate proficiency in nursing skills and clinical technologies.
  • Meet all clinical site onboarding, credentialing, and compliance requirements and travel to partner clinical sites as needed.
  • Provide flexibility to support clinical schedules, laboratory and simulation activities, and occasional evening or weekend commitments.

The hiring salary range for this position is $85,000.00 - $90,000.00. The hiring salary range above represents the University's good faith estimate at the time of posting
