title: Quantum Technology Subject Matter Expert
description:
General Infomatics, Inc. is a trusted partner to U.S. government agencies nationwide, delivering program support, healthcare services, strategic technology solutions, and knowledge management under the highest standards of integrity and excellence. At our core, we believe our greatest strength is our people - talented individuals from all walks of life who share a commitment to service. We are especially proud to champion veterans, transitioning personnel, military spouses, and military families, offering meaningful careers where their sacrifice and skills are recognized and valued.

We are looking for a QUANTUM TECHNOLOGY SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT for a full-time civil contract position in Alexandria, VA, supporting the Test Resource Management Center (Department of Defense)

Position Summary

The Quantum Technology Subject Matter Expert (SME) provides independent, objective technical advice to the DoD TRMC program office on the readiness, relevance, testability, and transition potential of quantum technologies. The SME evaluates emerging capabilities against defense test and evaluation (T&E) needs; translates complex quantum science into decision-quality information; and helps the Government identify practical investments, demonstrations, partnerships, infrastructure, workforce needs, risks, and transition pathways. The position supports quantum computing, quantum sensing, quantum communications/networking, quantum timing, and related enabling technologies, including post-quantum cybersecurity considerations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the program office's principal technical advisor for quantum information science and technology (QIST), with emphasis on DoD T&E applications and mission outcomes.
  • Assess the technical maturity, performance claims, limitations, dependencies, security considerations, and operational relevance of proposed quantum technologies.
  • Develop and maintain a quantum technology roadmap that identifies near-, mid-, and long-term opportunities, decision points, enabling investments, and transition criteria.
  • Translate operational and test-community needs into technical use cases, evaluation questions, performance measures, test objectives, and candidate demonstration concepts.
  • Advise on test methodologies, instrumentation, modeling and simulation, verification and validation, data requirements, environmental constraints, and measures of performance/effectiveness for quantum-enabled systems.
  • Conduct technical reviews, literature and market scans, vendor and laboratory assessments, and comparative analyses of Government, industry, academic, and allied efforts.
  • Identify gaps in T&E infrastructure, ranges, laboratories, reference standards, data environments, cybersecurity, and workforce capabilities required to evaluate quantum technologies.
  • Support planning and technical oversight of studies, prototypes, experiments, demonstrations, and pilot efforts; review technical approaches, schedules, risks, and deliverables.
  • Evaluate proposals, white papers, statements of work, technical reports, test plans, and acquisition documentation; provide clear findings and actionable recommendations.
  • Coordinate technical exchanges with DoD Components, Services, laboratories, test centers, program executive offices, academia, industry, and other Federal stakeholders, as authorized.
  • Prepare and deliver executive briefings, decision memoranda, technical reports, meeting materials, and responses to senior-leader inquiries.
  • Track technical, schedule, cost, supply-chain, classification, export-control, intellectual-property, and transition risks and recommend mitigation actions.
  • Promote technically rigorous, vendor-neutral decisions and clearly distinguish demonstrated performance from projected or marketing claims.
  • Protect controlled unclassified information and classified information and comply with applicable cybersecurity, records-management, and security requirements.

Core Technical Areas

  • Quantum computing and hybrid quantum-classical approaches, including algorithms, benchmarking, error characterization, simulation, and potential defense applications.
  • Quantum sensing, metrology, precision timing, navigation, imaging, and detection technologies.
  • Quantum communications and networking, including entanglement distribution, quantum key distribution, network architectures, and interoperability considerations.
  • Quantum device and system test challenges, including calibration, repeatability, environmental effects, noise, uncertainty, standards, and traceability.
  • Post-quantum cryptography and quantum-related cyber risk as they affect T&E environments and transition planning.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Physics, Quantum Science/Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field, plus at least 8 years of relevant experience; or a Master's degree plus at least 6 years; or a Ph.D. plus at least 3 years; or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in quantum information science and technology, with depth in at least one of the following: quantum computing, quantum sensing/metrology, quantum communications/networking, or quantum-enabled cybersecurity.
  • Experience evaluating emerging technologies, conducting technical research or engineering analysis, and producing defensible findings and recommendations.
  • Ability to connect scientific concepts to defense missions, acquisition decisions, and test and evaluation requirements.
  • Experience working across interdisciplinary scientific, engineering, acquisition, operational, and executive stakeholder groups.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-specialist and senior-leader audiences.
  • U.S. citizenship and eligibility to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Government security clearance.

  • Preferred Qualifications

    • Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in a quantum-related scientific or engineering discipline.
    • Experience supporting DoD, a Military Service, a Federal research organization, a national laboratory, an FFRDC/UARC, or a defense acquisition or T&E organization.
    • Knowledge of DoD acquisition, science and technology, experimentation, developmental test, operational test, and technology-transition processes.
    • Hands-on experience developing or evaluating test plans, benchmarks, demonstrations, prototypes, laboratory systems, or modeling and simulation environments.
    • Familiarity with quantum software and simulation tools such as Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, CUDA-Q/cuQuantum, or comparable platforms; proficiency in Python and/or C++ is desirable.
    • Evidence of technical leadership through publications, patents, conference presentations, standards participation, program leadership, or high-impact research contributions.

    Work Environment and Travel

    The role may require periodic travel to DoD installations, test centers, laboratories, conferences, industry engagements, and technical demonstrations.

Top Secret (SCI) eligible.

title: Specialist, QA Validation & Engineering
description:
Specialist, QA Validation & Engineering

About Site

Our FDA-licensed, state-of-the-art CGMP manufacturing facility for Gene Therapies is located on the Harmans/BWI campus. The campus, featuring two manufacturing facilities is located 5 miles from the Baltimore Washington International (BWI) airport and 13 miles from our Baltimore location. The campus is close to Washington, DC’s I-270 Technology Corridor, top universities, and government agencies.

The Harmans/BWI-1 EMA and FDA approved facility, at approximately 200,000 sq. ft., houses 10 CGMP manufacturing suites, fill/finish, central services, testing labs, and a warehouse.

The Harmans/BWI-2 facility, at approximately 145,000 sq. ft., is under development and will house 8 CGMP manufacturing suites and cold storage warehousing.

Both facilities support Phase 3 through commercial manufacturing of advanced therapeutic products including AAV and other viral vector-based therapies and vaccines.

Position Summary

We have an opportunity for a Specialist, QA Validation & Engineering to join our team. In this role, you will provide Quality oversight of Facilities, Engineering, and Validation groups to ensure compliance with US regulations, industry standards, and internal policies. You will support continuous improvement for processes, equipment, utilities, and computer systems. This position serves as a key Quality resource for Engineering, Facilities, and Validation organizations.

Shift: Monday - Friday 8am-5pm
Location: Harmans, MD - BWI
100% Onsite

The Role

  • Act as Quality Assurance representative for review and approval of process validation lifecycle documents, including Validation Master Plans, Process Performance Qualification protocols and reports, engineering and characterization studies, and Continued Process Verification documentation.
  • Provide QA oversight throughout the process validation lifecycle to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, industry standards, and internal procedures.
  • Support cleaning validation programs through protocol and report review and approval.
  • Collaborate with Manufacturing, Process Development, Validation, Engineering, and Technical Services teams to support process validation programs and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Review and approve deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, and risk assessments related to process validation activities.
  • Review and approve change controls impacting validated manufacturing processes, ensuring proper assessments, implementation plans, and supporting validation documentation.
  • Support client, regulatory, and internal audits by providing subject matter expertise on process validation programs and quality systems.
  • Support QA review of qualification activities for manufacturing equipment, process equipment, cleanrooms, facilities, and GMP utilities.
  • Review and approve calibration and preventive maintenance documentation to ensure continued suitability of validated systems and equipment.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by the manager.

The Candidate

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Microbiology, or a related scientific discipline.
  • Minimum 1-3 years of experience in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or biologics manufacturing environment.
  • Experience reviewing and approving process validation documents, including Process Performance Qualification protocols and reports.
  • Strong knowledge of FDA, EMA, ICH, and current Good Manufacturing Practice requirements applicable to process validation.
  • Experience with deviation management, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, risk assessments, and change control systems.

Preferred Skills & Background

  • Experience supporting equipment qualification (Installation Qualification, Operational Qualification, Performance Qualification).
  • Experience with facility and utility qualification.
  • Experience with cleaning validation and computerized systems validation.
  • Familiarity with biologics, cell therapy, gene therapy, plasmid manufacturing, or sterile manufacturing processes.

title: Flight Instructor, HondaJet Pilot - Abilene, TX
description:
Job Description

XSTAR Aviation is seeking experienced multiengine flight instructors to help build the next generation of Air Force aviators. This role supports a unique and rewarding mission focused on developing airmanship, increasing repetition, and enhancing overall flying proficiency within the bomber aircrew community.

In this role, CFIs will fly multiple times each week, deliver ground-based instruction, and provide focused, high-quality training to military aircrew.

This is an in-person, non-commuter position. Pilots must live, or be willing to relocate, within 30 minutes of Abilene, TX. The schedule is Monday through Friday each week and does not follow a traditional airline or rotational pilot schedule.

This position operates under FAA Part 91 and requires sound aeronautical judgment, strong crew coordination, and the ability to safely execute operations in a fast-paced environment. Pilots will work closely with program leadership, operations support personnel, and maintenance teams to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable daily operations.

In addition to flight operations, pilots will deliver ground-based instruction focused on the differences between FAA and USAF operating procedures, airspace, and regulatory frameworks to support pilot understanding and transition between environments.

Each pilot will also be assigned a ground duty aligned with site operations (e.g., safety, training coordination, or program administration). These responsibilities are integrated into standard duties and support overall program execution. The organizational structure and expectations are similar to a military flying unit.

Essential Functions

  • Act as CFI/PIC and conduct safe and efficient multi-engine flight operations in accordance with FAA Part 91 regulations and company procedures.
  • Plan and execute flight profiles, and instruct aircrew on flight planning, aeronautical decision-making, and mission execution.
  • Mentor and instruct U.S. Air Force aviators on instrument procedures, out-and-back mission profiles, and terminal area operations.
  • Execute proficiency-focused flight profiles designed to enhance airmanship, repetition, and overall pilot performance.
  • Deliver ground-based instruction on FAA and USAF procedural, regulatory, and airspace differences to support pilot understanding and operational integration.
  • Maintain a high standard of aeronautical decision-making, risk management, and crew coordination in all phases of flight.
  • Collaborate with operations support personnel, maintenance teams, and program leadership to ensure effective daily flight execution.
  • Perform assigned ground duty roles (e.g., safety, training coordination, or program administration) in support of site operations.
  • Participate in safety programs, reporting processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate and timely flight, training, and administrative records.
  • Support operational planning, scheduling coordination, and program meetings as required.
  • Represent XSTAR Aviation professionally in interactions with military personnel, government stakeholders, and industry partners.

Minimum Qualifications

(Military pilots may apply a 1.5× conversion factor.)

1,500 hours total flight time.

750 hours of PIC time.

500 hours of instructor time.

500 hours of turbine time.

One of the following:

  • FAA Certified Flight Instructor (CFI/CFII) and Multi-Engine Instructor (MEI), or
  • Airline Transport Pilot (ATP) certificate with multi-engine privileges and prior CFI experience, or
  • Current or Former Military Instructor Pilots

Multi-engine experience required; multi-engine turbine experience preferred

Demonstrated experience providing flight instruction in multi-engine aircraft.

Current FAA Medical Certificate (Class II or higher).

Strong aeronautical decision-making and risk management skills.

Excellent communication and instructional ability.

Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented operational environment.

Minimum of 10 years of aviation experience.

HA-420 experience is highly sought after.

*Prior military pilots who do not meet these minimums may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Multi-engine turbine experience
  • Prior military aviation experience
  • Instructor pilot experience in structured training program
  • Experience operating under FAA Part 91 or Part 135
  • HA-420 Flight experience
  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Experience mentoring developing pilots in a training environment.

Physical Demands

  • Ability to operate aircraft safely and perform duties associated with flight operations.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA medical certificate (Class II or higher).
  • Prolonged periods sitting in aircraft and/or at a computer workstation.

Travel Required

Limited travel may be required for training, aircraft repositioning, or program coordination.

Work Authorization / Security Requirements

  • U.S. Citizen required
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Clearance (Preferred)

Equal Opportunity Statement

XSTAR Aviation is an equal opportunity employer committed to equal opportunity in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristics as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Construction Scheduling Analyst
description:
Summary

The Construction Schedule Analyst is a foundational role within the Clark Planning & Scheduling Department. This position is designed for a detail-oriented individual who excels at data manipulation and logical problem-solving. You will support the Project Schedulers by managing the flow of data into Primavera P6, using Excel to audit schedule health, and creating reports that track project milestones.

This role is part of a structured career path in construction planning and scheduling. No prior construction experience is required; we provide technical training for Primavera P6 for candidates who demonstrate high-level analytical potential and a "quick-study" approach to new software.

Responsibilities

  • Commit to an accelerated learning path to become a power user in Primavera P6.

  • Work closely with Project Schedulers to explore the nuances of the Critical Path Method (CPM) and how it applies to complex construction sequencing.

  • On Site support of project teams to update schedules, expand activity detail, adjust construction sequencing, and produce internal and contractually required reporting.

  • Data Analysis and Advanced Reporting utilizing Primavera P6, Microsoft Excel, PowerBI and other industry specific tools.

  • Calculate and report on Project Metrics Total Float and Schedule Performance metrics to help the department identify potential bottlenecks.

  • Identify patterns in historical data to help Project Teams predict future project outcomes.

  • Quality Control: Ensure all schedule data adheres to standards for naming conventions, activity coding, and organizational breakdown.

Basic Qualifications

  • Undergraduate or Associates degree in construction management, engineering, data analysis, mathematics, computer science, business, finance, accounting, or a related field

  • Excel Proficiency

  • An innate interest in troubleshooting data discrepancies and finding the "why" behind the numbers.

  • Ability to summarize and communicate complex data findings

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Primavera P6

  • Results Oriented - Experience in using data to anticipate and solve problems, manage risk and analyze business needs to deliver high quality outcomes

  • Self Motivated - Takes initiative and personal responsibility to deliver value and excellence in all that you do

  • Team Player - Builds interpersonal relationships and collaborators with internal team members, trade partners, architects and clients.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

title: Consulting Dietitian [Stirling]
description:
This position offers 30 hours per month, flexible start date.

Be part of a collaborative team, passionate about senior nutrition and food service.

Seasons Care is hiring passionate Registered Dietitians to support the nutritional health and well-being of Seniors in Long-Term Care. With decades of experience in Long-Term Care, we work together every day to make meaningful differences in the lives of Residents across Canada. We believe in putting food and people first— for our Residents and our team.

When you join Seasons Care, you become part of a network of professionals who are passionate about leading with heart and evidence. You'll be joining a supportive environment where:

  • Your voice is heard and valued
  • Work-life balance is respected and prioritized
  • Professional development is encouraged
  • Teamwork and interdisciplinary collaboration are part of our everyday approach
  • We care — not just for Residents, but for one another

Your day is varied, structured, and rooted in collaboration. As an RD working in LTC, you will:

  • Manage daily clinical priorities, including referrals, weight monitoring, RAI assessments, and new Resident admissions
  • Collaborate closely with the Nutrition Manager and interdisciplinary Care Teams; participate in morning huddles where applicable
  • Review Resident charts and data (weights, intake, labs, medications, diagnoses, and health changes) to assess nutrition risk

This role provides a balanced blend of independent clinical practice, teamwork, and on‑site engagement across Homes.

You are a dedicated, organized, and empathetic Registered Dietitian who brings clinical confidence and a Resident-first mindset to every Home you support. You thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy working independently, and value collaboration with interdisciplinary teams.

Whether you're counselling a Resident, mentoring dietary staff or reviewing a menu, you bring clarity, care and professionalism to everything you do.

  • Registered and in good standing with the College of Dietitians of Ontario
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities
  • Demonstrated problem-solving and critical thinking skills
  • A people-first approach with strong customer-service skills and a commitment to building respectful, trusting relationships
  • Proficiency with EMR systems and digital documentation
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively
  • Must provide proof of liability insurance, TB testing and vulnerable sector check
  • Travel may be required for certain positions

title: Corporate Impact Intern - MN
description:
Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow? A position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.

At Xcel Energy, our employees are the driving force behind our success. So we make sure that, here, you can be your best. Doing work that makes a difference for neighbors and communities. Working with a team you can count on to push you. Expanding skills, staying ready for change, and capturing opportunities to grow. All with the support, rewards and recognition you need to thrive – during your internship and beyond.

The Xcel Energy Inclusion and Corporate Impact team plays a critical role in advancing business strategy through corporate social responsibility (CSR), fostering a culture of inclusion and belonging, and driving measurable community impact. By aligning social investments with enterprise priorities, the team delivers long-term value for employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

Central to this work is the stewardship of the Xcel Energy Foundation, which serves as a strategic platform for corporate philanthropy, community investment, and stakeholder engagement. Through the Foundation, the team strengthens workforce pipelines, expands nonprofit and community partnerships, and increases employee engagement—positioning Xcel Energy as a purpose-driven organization committed to sustainable, equitable outcomes.

The team leads and evaluates a comprehensive portfolio that includes Business Resource Group (BRG) engagement, workforce development initiatives, employee giving, volunteerism, and community partnerships. Success is measured through defined metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs), such as employee participation rates, grantmaking impact, nonprofit partnership outcomes, and community reach. These insights inform strategy, ensure accountability, and enhance the effectiveness of investments.

To support this work, the Corporate Impact team is seeking a college-level intern to support data-driven projects that advance employee giving, nonprofit partnerships, and community investment strategies. This paid internship is designed for a student with strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and an interest in corporate social responsibility. The intern will work with CSR data systems—including CyberGrants and Power BI—to support data management, reporting, and analysis of key metrics and KPIs related to employee engagement, grantmaking, and volunteerism. This role offers hands-on experience translating data into insights, supporting impact measurement, and helping inform strategic decision-making across the Foundation and Corporate Impact portfolio.


Typical intern responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

  • Support foundation data collection and analysis aligned with strategic goals and performance requirements of the internal programs.

  • Support development of data dashboard and consolidation of current data sources and inputs to manage, track and measure program's key performance indicators.

  • Complete data entry, data management and metric reporting in the Foundation’s online portal, CyberGrants.

  • Support implementation of successful annual workplace giving campaign including donor support, data entry, and input into the key performance.

  • Support accounting and finance teams on audit and financial processes

  • Support employee giving programs which include but are not limited to giving campaigns, Dollars for Doing, matching gifts, volunteer paid time off, sponsorships and in-kind donations; help create process documents and job aids for these.

  • Assist in monitoring and responding to emails and voicemails that come in on shared inboxes and hotlines.


This position is for an immediate start date. This position may have the possibility to extend beyond the internship’s initial term based on the candidate’s successful performance and Xcel Energy’s business needs.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Current student, Sophomore or higher

  • Enrolled in an accredited college or university and pursuing a degree in Data Science, Business Administration, Corporate Social Responsibility, or similar.

  • Able to work full-time during the summer (up to 40 hours a week)/ part time during the school year (up to 20 hours a week) and commuting to the designated work location in-person, per our hybrid work policy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior volunteer or work experience in a professional office setting

  • Management of data projects, identification of inputs with several stakeholders, ability to interpret requirements and define best-in class-solution.

  • Experience in data processing, identification of trends, generation of recommendations, and KPI measurement.

  • Successful candidates will have excellent attention to detail, be organized, and have good communication skills.

  • Experience with Excel Microsoft Office, Data management projects.

title: Workplace Experience Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The Workplace Experience Specialist helps shape an intentional, engaging, and high-performing workplace experience while ensuring day-to-day office operations run smoothly and supporting the broader priorities of the Workplace Experience team. This dynamic, highly visible individual contributor role blends employee experience, office operations, events, communications, vendor management, and special projects.

Success requires strong judgment, creativity, resourcefulness, and follow-through. The Specialist is expected to recognize what needs attention, prioritize competing requests, recommend solutions, and own work through completion. They balance service with accountability, establish appropriate boundaries, and make thoughtful decisions about where time and resources will have the greatest employee and business impact.

What will your job entail?

Workplace Experience & Employee Engagement

  • Own and execute workplace experience initiatives for assigned employee populations and offices, supporting firmwide priorities as needed.
  • Plan and execute intentional experiences including onsite and offsite events, employee programs, celebrations, volunteer and giveback initiatives, recognition moments, and other engagement activities.
  • Identify creative opportunities to improve the employee experience beyond traditional workplace programming.
  • Use employee feedback and available insights to recommend improvements and evolve programming.
  • Ensure initiatives are inclusive, appropriately scaled, and connected to a clear employee or business need.

Office Experience & Operations

  • Maintain a workplace environment that is welcoming, functional, professional, and reflective of the company's culture.
  • Manage relationships with building management, office vendors, service providers, and internal partners to address office needs, repairs, enhancements, and employee-facing concerns.
  • Manage workplace supplies, amenities, food and beverage programs, and shared employee spaces while operating within established budgets, proactively addressing needs before they disrupt the employee experience.
  • Support visitors and new hires with workspace readiness, building and office access, supplies, meetings, lunches, and other workplace logistics.
  • Identify recurring issues or inefficient processes and recommend sustainable solutions rather than repeatedly working around the problem.
  • Escalate risks, service issues, or larger workplace needs early with appropriate context and a recommended path forward whenever possible.

Communications & Culture

  • Develop and execute clear, engaging internal communications, including newsletters, employee announcements, onboarding materials, event communications, recognition, and other Workplace Experience messaging.
  • Identify creative ways to communicate, connect, and share information across offices, business units, and remote populations.
  • Serve as a visible ambassador for company culture, values, performance expectations, and Workplace Experience initiatives.
  • Help employees navigate available resources while reinforcing individual ownership, accountability, and established processes.

Program & Project Ownership

  • Own assigned initiatives from concept through completion, including planning, coordination, execution, follow-up, and measurement of outcomes.
  • Anticipate dependencies, next steps, and potential barriers rather than waiting for each step to be assigned.
  • Effectively manage multiple projects and changing priorities while maintaining strong organization, attention to detail, and timely execution.
  • Close communication loops, follow through on commitments, and confirm intended outcomes are achieved.
  • Create repeatable processes, templates, documentation, calendars, and resources that improve efficiency, consistency, and scalability.
  • Support special projects and evolving priorities identified by the Workplace Experience Leadership Team.

Budget & Resource Stewardship

  • Operate within established budgets and make thoughtful decisions regarding company resources, employee experience, and value delivered.
  • Process and reconcile expenses, invoices, purchasing, vendor payments, and supporting documentation accurately and on time, maintaining required trackers and records.
  • Evaluate programs, purchases, and recurring activities for continued value and business impact.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce unnecessary expenses, and redirect resources toward higher-impact experiences.

How This Role Is Expected to Operate

The Workplace Experience Specialist is expected to demonstrate:

Sound Judgment & Prioritization

Distinguishes urgency from importance, makes thoughtful trade-offs, and focuses time and resources where they create the greatest value.

Ownership & Follow-Through

Takes ownership of outcomes, not just individual tasks. Anticipates needs, brings solutions forward, raises risks early, and follows commitments through completion.

Service & Accountability

Helps others succeed while maintaining appropriate boundaries, clarifying ownership, and reinforcing expectations rather than absorbing responsibilities that belong elsewhere.

Creativity & Continuous Improvement

Brings fresh thinking to experiences, communications, and processes and looks for better, more efficient, and scalable ways of working.

Adaptability & Growth

Comfortably navigates changing priorities, unfamiliar challenges, and evolving expectations while seeking and applying feedback.

Measures of Success

Success in this role is demonstrated when:

  • Employees experience a workplace that is welcoming, connected, functional, and engaging.
  • Initiatives and operational responsibilities are executed reliably, accurately, on time, and within budget.
  • Needs, risks, and dependencies are anticipated and addressed proactively.
  • Leaders and teammates trust the Specialist to independently move objectives from initial direction through completion while keeping stakeholders informed.
  • Workplace programs and processes continuously improve based on employee feedback, business needs, and opportunities for greater efficiency and scalability.
  • The Specialist is viewed as a collaborative, resourceful, and solution-oriented partner who balances service, ownership, accountability, and responsible use of company resources.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 3-5+ years of relevant experience in workplace experience, employee engagement, office operations, events, hospitality, project coordination, or a related field preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple projects, stakeholders, deadlines, and competing priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, organization, attention to detail, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience managing vendors, employee programs, budgets, expenses, and operational logistics.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate needs and recommend solutions.
  • Proficiency with standard business technology and the ability to quickly learn new systems and tools.
  • Ability to handle sensitive or confidential information with sound judgment and discretion.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

The Person Who Will Thrive in This Role

This role is well suited for someone who enjoys variety, notices what others may overlook, and takes pride in making things better. They are comfortable making thoughtful decisions, solving problems, helping others, and taking initiative without needing every step mapped out.

title: Christie's Work Experience Programme 2026
description:
About the Programme

Christie’s London Work Experience Programme offers individuals the opportunity to gain first-hand insight into the world’s leading art business.

The programme is designed for those with a genuine interest in art, business, and careers within the art market. Participants will gain exposure to Christie’s day-to-day operations and develop an understanding of how different teams work together across specialist, operational, and corporate functions.

The experience is primarily observational and shadowing-based, providing meaningful insight rather than independent responsibility.

Programme Format

We offer a limited number of work experience placements in our London offices each year. Placements are dependent on departmental availability and business needs and can last between one and four weeks, with four weeks being the maximum length.

Availability varies throughout the year to ensure participants join at times when teams are able to offer a meaningful and engaging experience.

Work experience at Christie’s is voluntary and unpaid. However, we provide:

  • A £10 daily allowance towards lunch

  • Uncapped reimbursement of standard public transport travel costs for daily travel to and from Christie’s London offices (excluding first class and subject to receipts). This covers normal day‑to‑day commuting costs only.

If you are looking for paid opportunities, please explore our careers page HERE.

Standard working hours are 9:00am–5:00pm, Monday to Friday, and participants are expected to follow a smart business dress code.

Available Clusters

Placements are offered across the following clusters, subject to availability:

  • 20th / 21st Century

  • Old Masters

  • Classic Art

  • Islamic Art

  • Archives

  • Valuations

  • Client Management

  • Operations

  • Marketing

  • Finance

  • Human Resources

  • Legal

Applicants will be asked to indicate their preferred clusters as part of the application process. While we make every effort to place participants in areas aligned with their interests, specific placements cannot be guaranteed.

Application Process

Applications to the Work Experience Programme are reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the year.

Once you apply, your application will be placed into our screening pool. Applications are then shared with the relevant department managers.

Departments review applications as often as possible and select candidates to join them during specific periods, depending on business needs and availability.

Please note that demand for work experience placements far exceeds the availability of places. Unfortunately, we are only able to contact applicants who are successful.

You may apply once per year only. As part of the application, you will be asked to:

  • Select your top two cluster preferences

  • Indicate the months you are most available (if your application is shortlisted, a member of the team will contact you to discuss your availability in more detail)

  • Submit your CV

Each year, a new application link is created for the Work Experience Programme. If you are not successful in securing a placement in one year, you are welcome to apply again in the following year.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for the Christie’s Work Experience Programme, applicants must:

  • 16+ years of age at the time of placement

  • Be able to commit to the full-time work experience hours: 9:00am–5:00pm, Monday to Friday

  • Have the right to work in the UK (we are unable to sponsor or support visa applications)

  • Be willing to sign and comply with Christie’s confidentiality agreement

Please note that eligibility does not guarantee placement, as availability varies by department and demand for work experience placements is extremely high.

Close date for 2026 programme: November 30th 2026

Open date for the 2027 programme: December 1st 2026

title: Graduate - Supply, trading & shipping - China (Jan 2027)
description:
Entity:

Job Family Group:

Job Description:

bp supply, trading & shipping graduate programme – China (Jan 2027)

About bp

As a leading global energy company with a presence in 61 countries, bp’s purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. We are one of only a few companies that can deliver energy – at scale – to countries and millions of customers every day. With more than 100 years of experience, we bring together technology, innovation and deep expertise that keeps communities moving, – and we’re still evolving.

About early careers

Early careers opportunities

Your talent. Your skills. Your big ideas (and even bigger dreams). We know you have a lot to give. So we’ll make sure you get a lot in return. From next-level experiences to global impact. From inspiring teammates to exceptional support, – we offer graduate and internship roles across multiple areas.

Our supply, trading & shipping graduate programme

Fast-moving. High impact. Full of possibility. In supply, trading & shipping (ST&S), every decision matters, – and you’ll be making them sooner than you think.

Why work in ST&S at bp?

  • Play a role in powering economies worldwide.

  • Work in a fast-paced environment where every second counts.

  • Build future-proof skills that open up many different career paths.

  • Learn from experienced teams who’ll help you grow your commercial confidence.

As an ST&S graduate, you’ll complete three rotations designed to give you breadth of experience across your chosen business area while also supporting you to build technical depth. From analysing data to influencing decision making, to building customer relationships and shaping deals, – this programme gives you the exposure and experience to start building a future in commercial business.

Join us and you’ll get the support of a structured technical pathway and our training programme, helping you grow both professionally and personally. In return, you'll bring your ideas, curiosity and ambition to real business challenges. Along the way, you'll be part of a supportive bp early careers community that will help you grow, succeed and make a meaningful impact from day one.

We’re recruiting for graduates to join us on the Commercial track for a January 2027 start.

Commercial development track: Every year, bp invests billions of dollars searching for new sources of energy, supplying our customers with the fuels they need. You’ll help to ensure we make the best use of our investment. We want you to be in the best position to propose new and creative ways to maximize value. The commercial development track will help you to develop strong commercial acumen which is supported by the different rotations you will undertake. You may find yourself placed in a team that sets strategy, tracks the market, or manages foreign exchange, or you may be a trading operator responsible for the logistical success of a trading deal. Other rotations include marketing & origination, structured products and chartering.

No matter where you work, all the roles will offer a challenging experience that gives you first-hand exposure to our supply, trading & shipping activities and will contribute to building your long-term career in the organisation.

About you ​


As a bp graduate, you will have an interest and/or skill in delivering economic value back to a business, identifying solutions and strategies resulting in cost savings and a natural negotiation style. No matter where you work at bp, you’ll be valued, included and respected. We’ll provide you with on-going support and we’ll reward you for the great work you do.

In a global energy market defined by rapid shifts, complexity, and uncertainty, we value people with commercial hunger and sound judgment, not just technical perfection.

Our traders and commercial teams operate across global desks in London, the US, and Asia, engaging customers across Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Malaysia, Vietnam, and beyond. As a result, the ability to connect with people across cultures, build trust, and communicate clearly in global teams is foundational.

Equally important is initiative and intellectual curiosity. Markets do not come with instruction manuals. We look for individuals who actively try to understand what is moving prices, who form hypotheses, and who develop the instinct to sense where opportunity may emerge before it is obvious.

A trading environment also requires the confidence to take risk, paired with accountability and discipline. Decisions are often made under time pressure and imperfect information, and resilience matters. We do not optimise for blemish‑less CVs. Some of our strongest performers are those who have faced setbacks, learned from failure, and demonstrated the grit to push forward with even greater determination.

To be eligible for the ST&S graduate programme you should:

  • be currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in any discipline which could range from Business, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Arts to STEM

  • be in your final year of study, graduating by Dec 2026 or recently graduated

  • on track to achieve a cumulative GPA equivalent to Second Upper Honours or above

Please note the following when applying:

  • You can only apply to 1 bp early careers opportunity globally per academic year. Within this time, we will only process the first application you make, and you’ll be withdrawn from any subsequent applications.

  • Please note that vacancies are filled on an ongoing basis after opening and we may close applications before any stated deadline. Therefore, we highly recommend you submit your application as early as possible to be considered for the opportunity of your choice.

Applications close on 16 October 2026.


Travel Requirement

Some travel may be required with this role, this is negotiable


Relocation Assistance:

This role is not eligible for relocation


Remote Type:

This position is not available for remote working


Skills:

Agility core practices, Analytical Thinking, Computational Thinking, Continuous Learning, Data Analysis, Data cleansing and transformation, Data Management, Data Sourcing, Data visualization and interpretation, Dialogue enablement, Exposure Management, Machine Learning (ML), Macroeconomics, Market analysis methods, Market Risk Management, Sentiment and Trends, Statistics, Trade execution and management, Trading Fundamentals, Trading knowledge

.

title: Execution Analyst, SES Creation/SES Rel/Price Line Verification
description:
Entity:

Finance


Job Family Group:

Procurement & Supply Chain Management Group


Job Description:

Job Description

OVERVIEW:

We are a global energy business involved in every aspect of the energy system. We are working towards delivering light, heat, and mobility to millions of people every day. We are one of the very few companies equipped to address some of the big sophisticated challenges that matter for the future. We have a real contribution to make to the world's ambition of a low-carbon future. Join us and be part of what we can accomplish together. You can participate in our new ambition to become a net zero company by 2050 or sooner and help the world get to net zero.

Would you like to discover how our diverse, hardworking people are owning the way in making energy cleaner and better – and how you can play your part in our special team?

Key Accountabilities and Challenges:
Accountable for accurate and timely transactional input validation and data entry from an invoice or service receiving document, such as a field ticket or timesheet, into an online Service Entry Sheet (SES) document in BP’s SAP ERP Backbone solution. Once accepted by BP, the SES provides confirmation of the services that have been performed by a supplier. The Service Entry Sheet Releaser verifies the acceptability of an SES thoroughly and then forwards it to the responsible business User for acceptance. Under certain process guidelines, the Service Entry Sheet Releaser may accept (release) the SES on the responsible user’s behalf.


Basic activities involved in an SES includes-
o Validate the invoice against supporting documentation, e.g., field tickets, timesheets, etc, and create entry into SAP per defined process.
o Validate BP Purchase Order or Contract line items and record each service as an SES line item.
o Validate and record quantities of each service received for each SES line item.
o Reject invoice in case of clear discrepancy with accurate business reasoning.
o Release the SES in the workflow for acceptance by BP.
o Ensure daily transactional processing targets and KPI are met.
o Timely exception resolution and customer concern as per the process guidelines.
o If exceptions are found, clearly document reasons and refer them to the appropriate responsible party, e.g., PO Buyer and Accounts Payable team for resolution.
o Applies standard agreements and aligns with established purchase-to-pay processes.

title: (Sr) Associate Scientist, Analytical Development
description:
About Aura Biosciences

Aura Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bel-sar, a potentially transformative, first-in-class therapy for patients living with ocular cancers. Bel-sar represents an entirely novel approach to treating ocular cancers via its dual mechanisms of action of acute tumor necrosis and secondary anti-tumor immune activation. The Phase 3 registration study of Bel-sar in early choroidal melanoma, the largest patient segment of uveal melanoma, is fully enrolled, and earlier stage studies in metastases to the choroid and cancers of the ocular surface are ongoing. Aura's mission is to improve outcomes for patients living with ocular cancers by delivering a therapy that not only arrests tumor growth but also preserves vision and quality of life.


For more information, visit aurabiosciences.com. Follow us on X, @AuraBiosciences, and visit us on LinkedIn.



Position Summary

The (Sr) Associate Scientist, Analytical Development will support analytical development and characterization activities for complex biologics, with a focus on virus-like particles (VLPs) and dye-conjugated VLPs. This is a primarily laboratory-based role requiring hands-on experience with molecular biology, electrophoresis, and bioanalytical techniques supporting late-stage clinical drug substance and drug product development.


The successful candidate will work closely with Analytical Development scientists to execute analytical testing, support method development, qualification, and transfer activities, maintain high-quality documentation, and ensure laboratory instruments are ready for use. The role also involves collaboration with internal cross-functional teams and external partners, including contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract research organizations (CROs).



Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Perform laboratory experiments independently following established protocols to support inter-departmental teams, analytical method development, qualification, transfer, and product characterization.
  • Independently culture, maintain, expand, and cryopreserve cell lines in accordance with established protocols and quality standards. Maintain cell banks and accurately document passage history and inventory records.
  • Perform cell-based cytotoxicity, molecular biology, and immunoassays to support product release, characterization, development, stability, and forced degradation studies, including DNA/RNA extraction, qPCR quantification, ELISA, and Gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE, Western blotting).
  • Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to meet project timelines.
  • Identify, investigate, and resolve technical challenges, experimental deviations, and assay performance issues as needed. Communicate findings to appropriate scientific team members.
  • Serve as a subject domain lead for assigned techniques to identify atypical trends and providing technical guidance, as applicable
  • Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot routine laboratory instruments used for molecular biology, bioassay, and analytical testing.
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and compliant records in electronic laboratory notebooks in accordance with good documentation practices and data-integrity requirements.
  • Prepare and review technical documentation, including data packets, standard operating procedures, test methods, and method development reports.
  • Participate in data review and scientific discussions related to analytical development and product characterization studies and present experimental results and scientific findings to internal and external stakeholders, as appropriate.



Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific discipline.
  • 2-4 years of relevant laboratory experience demonstrating hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques, including DNA/RNA extraction, nucleic acid quantification, PCR or qPCR, and agarose gel electrophoresis.
  • Experience in aseptic techniques is required with proven experience in regular cell maintenance techniques. And performance of cell-based cytotoxicity assays.
  • Motivation to learn and grow and ability for problem solving is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently execute, document, analyze, and troubleshoot electrophoresis and qPCR experiments.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with one or more additional analytical techniques, such as SDS-PAGE, Western blotting, capillary electrophoresis, ELISA, UV/Vis spectroscopy, or HPLC/UPLC is preferred.
  • Understanding of analytical method development, qualification, validation, and technology transfer principles.
  • Experience working in a regulated laboratory environment and applying good documentation and data-integrity practices.
  • Experience supporting the analytical development or characterization of biologics, including drug substance and drug product.
  • Familiarity with scientific data analysis, graphing software, and basic statistical concepts.
  • Some travelling maybe required to assist with assay establishment, troubleshooting at CDMOs



Skills and Capabilities

  • Ability to follow detailed protocols, prepare reagents and samples accurately, and independently troubleshoot routine experimental and instrument-related issues.
  • Strong attention to detail, scientific curiosity, and problem-solving ability.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize laboratory activities, and meet established timelines.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within cross-functional teams.


Salary & Benefit Information

(Placement within the listed range depends on many factors including, but not limited to: geographic location, degree, years of experience, and internal company equity)

title: Senior Proposal Lead
description:
About Site

Catalent’s Greenville, North Carolina site is a major oral solid dose development and manufacturing campus, delivering end‑to‑end, turnkey solutions from formulation development through commercial manufacturing and packaging. The site specializes in oral solid dosage forms, supported by integrated formulation expertise, comprehensive analytical services, and scalable manufacturing capabilities designed to support both commercial products and potent or targeted therapies, including orphan drugs. Backed by more than $100 million in recent investments, the Greenville operation features fit‑for‑scale infrastructure, potent handling capabilities, and a strong regulatory track record, making it a critical part of Catalent’s global network for advancing complex oral drug programs from development to market.

Position Summary

We have an opportunity for a Senior Proposal Lead to join our team. This role supports Business Development teams by managing the scoping, writing, and issuing of proposals for new and existing customer opportunities. You will be responsible for commercial pricing proposals and serve as a key liaison between Business Development, Product Development, and other site teams. This position ensures proposals are accurate, timely, and aligned with legal and operational requirements.

Shift: Mon to Fri 8am-5pm
Location: Greenville, NC
100% Onsite

The Role

  • Prepare development, tech transfer, and pipeline proposals related to customer activities within Catalent facilities, including early phase product development or process change proposals.

  • Design and manage proposals for the site.

  • Process requests for company codes and proposal numbers.

  • Collaborate with internal groups such as legal, business development, Science and Technology, Product Development, Analytical, Quality, and project management to complete quotes and QARs.

  • Work with other Catalent sites to ensure project timelines and deliverables are met.

  • Ensure project quotes are within scope and current.

  • Manage proposal development timelines and ensure documents are accurate and delivered on time.

  • Ensure each quote is governed by the correct legal document.

  • Maintain weekly Quotes in Process status and manage other metric tracking as needed.

  • Write Commercial Pricing letters for new opportunities.

  • Generate high-level timelines and provide supporting documents for quotations.

  • Lead complex quotations requiring input from multiple locations or business units and senior leadership.

  • Engage directly with clients regarding quotes in progress and related questions.

  • Lead continuous improvement activities to enhance efficiency and quality of work.

  • Provide support to the site, Business Development, or Commercial Operations Leadership as needed.

  • Manage Strategic Clients.

  • Participate in cross-functional initiatives to reduce cost and improve efficiency and service levels.

  • Work collaboratively and professionally to support or lead global objectives.

  • Serve as lead for mentoring and training new team members.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant science or engineering discipline.

  • 6+ years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical, medical device, or food manufacturing, including quality, technical project management, business management, and/or business development.

  • Knowledge of drug product or consumer product development, analytical research and development, project scale-up, product manufacturing, quality, validations, and regulatory requirements.

  • Strong analytical and financial skills with business acumen.

  • Superior customer service skills and professional demeanor.

  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel).

  • Strong interpersonal skills, both oral and written.

  • Ability to prioritize and multitask effectively.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with attention to detail.

  • Process-oriented and customer-focused mindset.

  • Mathematical and reasoning ability.

  • Self-motivated, collaborative, and action-oriented with ability to work cross-functionally in a matrix organization.

  • Ability to interpret various instructions in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

  • Ability to work effectively under pressure to meet deadlines.

  • Specific vision requirements include reading of written documents and frequent use of a computer monitor screen.

  • Competitive Paid Time Off plus 8 paid holidays.

The Department of Transportation and Public Facilities (DOT&PF), Southcoast Region Design and Engineering Services section is looking for an Engineering Assistant 2 in Juneau to help us Keep Alaska Moving!

The State of Alaska Department of Transportation and Public Facilities’ mission is to Keep Alaska Moving. We are working toward a modern, adaptable, flexible transportation system that will be resilient as we tackle our challenges. We believe collaboration, communication, and coordination increase our ability to succeed. Creating teams that are focused on results, working together, and leveraging resources across our department, with community and private sector partnerships, increases our ability to accomplish our mission and serve Alaskans.

The department values professional development, offering training programs and mentorship opportunities to help individuals expand their expertise and advance in their chosen fields. With the vast and unique challenges of Alaska's geography and climate, employees can work on groundbreaking projects that contribute to the state's growth, making the DOT&PF an ideal choice for those seeking a fulfilling and evolving career in transportation and public facilities.

This position is located in Juneau.
Working at the Alaska Department of Transportation and Public Facilities (DOT&PF) offers a uniquely challenging and rewarding environment. With Alaska's diverse and expansive terrain, coupled with its extreme weather conditions, employees of the DOT&PF can work in various locations, including remote locations and urban centers, addressing a wide range of transportation needs. Their roles demand adaptability and resourcefulness as they maintain and improve roads, bridges, airports, ports, and public facilities in a state known for rugged terrain and extreme seasonal changes. This work not only presents professionals with a range of fascinating challenges but also allows them to contribute to developing and maintaining critical infrastructure against the backdrop of Alaska's breathtaking natural beauty, reflecting a strong commitment to safety and environmental responsibility.

  • Materials Engineering: Knowledge of the concepts, principles, theories, and methods related to the composition, structures, and properties of materials, their use, behavior and performance under environmental influences, and the identification, processing, and manufacture of optimal materials for various applications.

If you are a motivated and detail-oriented individual with a passion for providing exceptional patient care, please apply to this exciting opportunity to join our team as a Staffing Coordinator.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’amateurs de voitures positifs et motivés pour se joindre à notre équipe. Les titulaires de ce poste devront entretenir d’excellentes relations avec nos clients.

CE QUI EST OFFERT PAR L’ENTREPRISE:

L’occasion de travailler pour le plus important fournisseur de pièces automobiles du marché secondaire nord-américain.
Des possibilités d’avancement de carrière dans toute l’organisation Advance Auto Parts.
L’accès à un excellent système de formation en ligne dédié au développement personnel ou à la formation des gestionnaires.
Une culture organisationnelle enrichissante grâce au programme de reconnaissance des coéquipiers et aux repas en équipe.
Un rabais employé sur les pièces automobiles, les outils et l’équipement.
Un régime d’avantages sociaux collectifs après 90 jours à l’emploi, y compris l’assurance maladie complémentaire, l’assurance dentaire, les soins de la vue, l’assurance vie et l’assurance en cas de décès ou de mutilation accidentels.
Des avantages financiers tels qu’un REER collectif avec contribution de contrepartie de l’employeur et un régime d’achat d’actions à rabais pour tous les coéquipiers permanents.

CE QUE VOUS APPORTEREZ À L’ÉQUIPE :

Être passionné par le service à la clientèle. Avoir une disposition naturelle à offrir un service exceptionnel en tout temps et à tisser des liens durables avec les clients, les autres employés, la direction, etc.
Être orienté sur la vente : Posséder des aptitudes avérées pour la vente et toujours s’efforcer d’atteindre les objectifs de vente personnels et en magasin, de même que les objectifs de service.
Faire preuve d’esprit d’équipe. S’engager à travailler en équipe. Démontrer une attitude positive et amicale.
Avoir de l’expérience dans l’industrie automobile. Posséder des connaissances avancées des pièces et systèmes automobiles. Avoir de l’expérience avec le système pour point de vente. Conseiller les clients pour leurs projets ou pour la résolution de problèmes complexes, par exemple l’identification de pièces.
Être débrouillard : Localiser des pièces auprès de différentes sources, y compris les commandes spéciales, secondes sources, etc.
Apprendre rapidement. Avoir une connaissance approfondie des opérations en magasin et une parfaite connaissance des procédures d’entretien et d’inventaire en magasin.
Faire preuve d’autonomie et de fiabilité dans l’exécution des tâches. Effectuer l’ouverture et la fermeture du magasin de manière responsable. Favoriser un environnement de travail sécuritaire.
Scolarité : Détenir un diplôme d’études secondaires ou diplôme d’équivalence d’études secondaires.
Être flexible : Être disponible le jour, le soir, la fin de semaine et lors des jours fériés, au besoin.

Exigences physiques : Les détails de la présente décrivent les exigences physiques nécessaires pour que l’employé puisse effectuer avec succès les tâches essentielles de son poste, avec ou sans accommodement raisonnable. Dans l’exercice de ses fonctions, le coéquipier sera principalement appelé à marcher et à se tenir debout. Le coéquipier doit être en mesure de parler, d’entendre, d’utiliser ses mains et ses doigts pour manipuler ou toucher des objets, de tendre les bras pour atteindre des objets, de grimper, de se tenir en équilibre, de se pencher, de s’agenouiller, de s’accroupir et de ramper. Le coéquipier devra fréquemment soulever et/ou déplacer des objets allant jusqu’à 23 kg (50 lb). Ce poste exige d’avoir une bonne vue de près et de loin, de distinguer les couleurs et d’avoir une bonne perception de la profondeur.
Environnement de travail : Les détails de la présente décrivent l’environnement où le titulaire devra accomplir les tâches essentielles du poste, avec ou sans accommodement raisonnable. Dans l’exercice de ses fonctions, le coéquipier travaillera habituellement à l’intérieur dans un environnement de vente au détail. Le coéquipier sera occasionnellement exposé à des produits chimiques caustiques. Le niveau de bruit dans l’environnement de travail est habituellement modéré.

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives. The role has good knowledge of store systems, basic automotive system knowledge and basic part knowledge. The role has the basic ability to source from stores, hubs, pdq, and external suppliers. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and maintenance processes. Position can be part time or full time. Fleet safety certification preferred.

  • Provide excellent selling experience for DIY customer visits and phone calls
  • Achieve personal sales goal and help store achieve its sales goals
  • Provide DIY services including battery installation, testing, wiper installs, etc.
  • Maintain store product and operational standards
  • Responsible for inventory processes including truck put away, shoot outs, cycle counts, Back stock, etc.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • General stocking including truck stocking and back stock
  • Safely deliver parts to customers as needed

Success Factors

  • Basic driving and navigation ability
  • Ability to use delivery board system
  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Operating inventory systems and store equipment
  • Parts and automotive system knowledge skills
  • Operating POS and Parts lookup systems

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Salesperson

  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and management
  • Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, parts catalogs, and procedure manuals
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

  • 2-3 years of successful sales experience in a diverse retail environment, providing superior customer experiences

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: 3rd Shift Sanitation Coordinator
description:
Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.

Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.

HOW YOU WILL MAKE HISTORY HERE…

As a Sanitation Coordinator, you will play a critical role in maintaining the highest standards of food safety, sanitation, quality, and workplace safety throughout the facility. In this hands-on leadership position, you will coordinate daily sanitation activities, support department operations, drive compliance with food safety programs, and help ensure production equipment and facility areas are cleaned and maintained to company and regulatory standards. You will also serve as a key backup to Sanitation Leadership, providing direction and support across shifts as needed.

WHAT YOU WILL DO…

  • Lead and direct sanitation team members, including Machine Cleaners, Building Cleaners, Helpers, Temporary Associates, and Part-Time Employees.

  • Coordinate daily sanitation activities to meet production schedules, preventive maintenance requirements, and emergency cleaning needs.

  • Conduct shift meetings and communicate priorities, safety expectations, and department updates.

  • Train, coach, and develop employees while supporting performance management activities, including evaluations and disciplinary documentation.

  • Assist with staffing, attendance tracking, overtime management, vacation scheduling, and workforce planning.

  • Develop, update, and maintain Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOPs) and support sanitation program validation efforts.

  • Coordinate completion of the Master Sanitation Schedule and maintain accurate records in manual and computerized systems.

  • Monitor and report sanitation KPIs, prioritize work based on business needs, and ensure timely completion of assigned tasks.

  • Perform sanitation audits and inspections to verify compliance with policies, SSOPs, corrective actions, and food safety standards.

  • Investigate sanitation deficiencies and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

  • Support and ensure compliance with SQF, HACCP, GMP, Environmental Monitoring, Pest Control, Allergen Control, and other prerequisite food safety programs.

  • Partner with Production, Maintenance, Quality, and other departments to achieve plant objectives and support operational needs.

  • Monitor external contractors to ensure compliance with safety, quality, and sanitation requirements.

  • Review and respond to schedules, emails, reports, and operational communications in a timely manner.

  • Conduct job-specific training and verify employee compliance with sanitation procedures and plant programs.

  • Perform visual inspections, environmental swabbing, and chemical titrations as required.

  • Supply team members with appropriate tools, equipment, chemicals, and materials needed to complete assigned work.

  • Perform daily and deep cleaning of equipment, machinery, and facility structures using approved sanitation practices.

  • Complete and maintain accurate sanitation, attendance, and compliance documentation.

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance sanitation effectiveness, efficiency, and food safety performance.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH…

  • Sanitation Supervisor and Department Leadership

  • Sanitation Team Members

  • Production Operations

  • Quality Assurance and Food Safety Teams

  • Maintenance Department

  • External Contractors and Service Providers

  • Cross-functional Plant Leadership Teams

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE… (MUST HAVE)

  • High School Diploma or GED required.

  • 1+ years of experience in sanitation, manufacturing, food production, or a related environment.

  • Demonstrated leadership ability with experience directing, coaching, or training employees.

  • Knowledge of sanitation processes, cleaning chemicals, and food safety requirements.

  • Ability to follow and enforce SSOPs, GMPs, HACCP principles, and safety procedures.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

  • Basic computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.

  • Ability to maintain accurate records, documentation, and reports.

  • Willingness to work overtime, weekends, holidays, and flexible schedules as business needs require.

  • Ability to safely perform physical job requirements, including standing for extended periods, climbing, reaching, lifting, bending, kneeling, and working in industrial environments.

IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAVE… (NICE TO HAVE)

  • Associate degree from an accredited college, technical school, or related educational program.

  • Experience in food manufacturing, food safety, or sanitation leadership roles.

  • Working knowledge of SAP Manufacturing, Kronos TimeKeeper, SharePoint, PowerPoint, and other manufacturing systems.

  • Experience managing sanitation audits, environmental monitoring programs, allergen controls, or pest control programs.

  • Familiarity with SQF, HACCP, GMP, and other regulatory food safety standards.

  • Experience leading continuous improvement initiatives and implementing sanitation process enhancements.

  • Experience coordinating cross-functional teams and supporting plant-wide operational goals.

Physical & Work Environment

  • Frequent standing and walking on concrete floors throughout the shift.

  • Regular climbing, reaching, bending, crouching, and handling equipment and sanitation tools.

  • Ability to work in wet environments with varying temperatures and elevated noise levels.

  • Exposure to cleaning chemicals, sanitizers, machinery, and industrial equipment while utilizing required PPE.

  • Overtime, weekend, and holiday work may be required.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Pay: $31.35 per hour

  • Shift: 3rd Shift 10:00PM-6:00AM

  • Location: 1414 Blue Hills Avenue Bloomfield, CT 06002
