  • Reward and recognition programs, including earned-wage access through our partnership with ZayZoon.
  • Comprehensive Benefit and Retirement packages.
  • Employee discount and perk offerings with various partnerships, including Perkopolis, Telus, Rogers, Goodlife, etc.
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Paid orientation, training and development with opportunities to grow your career.

The Care Access Representative plays a vital role in delivering a seamless and positive experience for clients, families, and care providers by managing the scheduling of direct care staff (Personal Support Workers, Health Care Aides, and Nurses) within a high-volume contact center environment. In this dynamic role, representatives handle chats, inbound and outbound calls, data entry and intake, responding to scheduling requests, resolving issues, and ensuring continuity of care.

As the primary point of contact, the Care Access Representative must excel in problem-solving, communication, and multitasking to effectively coordinate care while balancing client needs and staff availability. By maintaining strong relationships with clients, families, care providers, and referral sources, they contribute to the delivery of high-quality, person-centered care.

What you will do

  • Efficient Scheduling: utilize scheduling software to optimize the assignment of care providers, ensuring client care plans are fulfilled promptly and accurately within a dynamic contact center setting.
  • KPI Achievement: Meet and exceed individual KPIs such as calls/chats per hour, quality assurance, and the successful scheduling of visits.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Maintain open lines of communication with clients, families, and care providers to ensure smooth scheduling processes. Address issues proactively and escalate when necessary.
  • Relationship Building: Cultivate and maintain positive relationships with care providers, clients, funders, and team members, considering individual needs in all decision-making processes.
  • Data Management: Accurately update and manage scheduling databases, client / care provider records, and care plans, ensuring all information is current and accessible for reporting and tracking.
  • Compliance: Adhere to Employment Standards legislation, collective agreements, and organizational policies and procedures.

What you will need to be successful

  • Educational Background: Minimum Grade 12 education.
  • Experience: At least 2 years of experience in Customer Service, Scheduling, and/or Coordination, preferably within a contact center environment.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and experience with scheduling software (e.g., AlayaCare). Keyboarding speed of 35-45 words per minutes required.
  • Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with excellent telephone etiquette.
  • Problem-solving: Results-oriented with strong problem-solving abilities.
  • Multitasking: Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Organizational Skills: Excellent time management and organizational skills, with a keen eye for detail.
  • Computer Literacy: Advanced computer literacy with various applications and programs.
  • Medical Background: Knowledge of medical terminology or experience in medical administration is an asset.
  • Language Skills: Ability to communicate in French is an asset.
  • Healthcare Scheduling: Prior experience in healthcare scheduling is highly desirable.
  • Work Schedule: Availability to work in office.

Hours of Work:

Monday to Friday 8:30am-4:30pm

Work Arrangement

This position is hybrid, combining remote and in-office work, with the potential to transition to full-time in-office in the future.

The current schedule is:

  • Work from Home: Mondays and Fridays (If all work-from-home requirements are met)
  • In Office: Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays

Work from Home Requirements

To be eligible for remote work, employees must meet the following requirements:

  • Access to a private and secure workspace at home to ensure confidentiality during all client and team communications
  • A proper home office setup, including an ergonomic deck and chair, to support comfort and productivity
  • A high-speed wired connection with the minimum speed test of 25 Mbps download and 5 Mbps upload
  • An active wired internet service plan
  • Ability to be on camera for all virtual meetings and calls

title: Adapted Athletics Program Assistant - External
description:
Associated Students of San Diego State University

DEPARTMENT: Aztec Recreation

POSITION TITLE: Adapted Athletics External Program Assistant

GENERAL PURPOSE: Under the direction of the Director of Adapted Athletics, the Adapted Athletics External Program Assistant will assist with the marketing, event planning, recruitment, corporate relations, and stewardship of the Adapted Athletics program. The External Program Assistant is responsible for overseeing program outreach, including creating awareness campaigns, organizing events, providing donor stewardship, and collaborating with external groups on various projects. The Adapted Athletics program provides opportunities for individuals to participate in a diverse offering of inclusive and adaptive athletics and recreation activities within the University at a variety of skill and ability levels.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Primary Functions

  • Assists with the planning, organization, scheduling, administration and facilitation of a comprehensive, inclusive adaptive sports program including competitive sports, drop-in activities, tournaments, and special events
  • Assists with scheduling/calendar management: noting sponsor events that require a member of the program to be present, coordinating on/off campus events and networking opportunities, etc.
  • Uses Virtual EMS to reserve facilities for on campus competitions, meetings and special events
  • Assists Aztec Recreation and Mission Bay Aquatic Center program administrators to develop and enhance adaptive sport and recreation programs in sport clubs, intramural sports, fitness, rock climbing, and water sports
  • Assists with the coordination of team travel arrangements including flight/hotel reservations and travel reimbursements
  • Attends team competitions and assists with team event management
  • Assists with the coordination of recruitment and onboarding for program staff and athletes
  • Assists with any follow up communication with potential student-athlete recruits
  • Utilizes communication tools to interact with current (and prospective) athletes, including email, phone, internet video, face to face meetings
  • Establishes strong working relationships with other campus departments including the School of Exercise and Nutritional Sciences, Student Disability Services, University Development, Financial Aid, Admissions, and Athletics
  • Assists with the organization and leadership of prospective athlete tours
  • Works with the Aztec Recreation and A.S. marketing teams, to develop and implement effective marketing and communication strategies, including social media content, presentations, and promotional photography and videography, and to present and promote programs to various on campus and off campus groups
  • Assists with recruitment, selection, and work assignments for ENS student interns
  • Assists with ENS credit class/internship curriculum development
  • Assists director with annual budget planning and maintaining program expenses
  • Researches and recommends inventory of program supplies and equipment utilized in Adapted Athletics programs
  • Ensures facilities and equipment are safe to use; submits a repair work order if needed
  • Assists with the implementation of safety and risk management procedures for Adapted Athletics
  • Collaborates with the director to assist with documents and presentation materials for meetings
  • Assists with grant material preparation
  • Assists with donor/sponsor prospect research, networking, events and communication
  • Assists director with Student Affairs and College of Health and Human Services Development teams to support fundraising efforts for the Adapted Athletics program
  • Assists director with providing timely reports on all Adapted Athletic program developments to all funders of the organization (government, individual donors, university alumni, corporations, and foundations)
  • Assists in providing inclusion training, disability awareness and other educational programs to part-time and full-time staff as well as the campus and community
  • Assists in the assessment and evaluation of programs and participation through qualitative and quantitative data collection
  • Assists in the formation, review, and enforcement of all policies and procedures including annual revisions of all sport rules, policies and regulations
  • Disseminates necessary information to staff, interns, and athletes
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Customer Service and Collaboration

  • Establishes and maintains working relationships with various A.S. and University departments, as well as vendors
  • Represents the team and Associated Students/SDSU in a professional manner at all times
  • Maintains positive and effective working relationships with all athletes and staff
  • Greets all customers in a timely manner
  • Answers the phone and interacts politely and courteously
  • Assists all customers with questions and/or comments
  • If unable to assist, refers customer to someone who can
  • Maintains positive and effective working relationships with all customers
  • Informs supervisor of any customer issues
  • Serves as liaison to campus committees as needed

Safety

  • Ensures all operations are conducted with safety of staff and customers as first priority, and in accordance with the Injury and Illness Prevention Plan and other safety policies
  • Adheres to Associated Students' Code of Safe Practices
  • Reports accidents to supervisor and reviews changes required to avoid reoccurrence
  • Ensures proper documentation is completed for each accident (employee and/or non-employee) and forwards to supervisor
  • Reports maintenance problems and/or broken and unsafe equipment to the appropriate party immediately

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum & Preferred Requirements

Education:

  • Bachelor's Degree required, in Physical Education, Recreation, Kinesiology/Exercise Science Health, Marketing, Business or a related field preferred

Experience:

  • Must have at least one year of sports administrative or program support experience
  • Must have previous experience with marketing and planning events
  • Must be able to work evening and weekends based on program demands
  • Previous experience with grant writing and management preferred
  • Experience with adaptive sports and recreation and adaptive equipment preferred
  • Demonstrated experience with programs and activities for persons with disabilities preferred
  • Experience within a collegiate recreation or intercollegiate athletics setting preferred
  • Knowledge of student athlete financial aid and scholarship processes preferred

License & Certification:

  • American Red Cross First Aid and CPR/AED certifications are required
  • Valid California driver's license and proof of automobile insurance are required
  • S. Center for Safe Sport required within 30 days of employment

Trainings:

  • Must complete Gender Awareness, Computer Security, Workplace Violence Prevention, and Sexual Harassment Prevention training within 30 days of hire
  • Must complete the California Defensive Driving Course

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

  • Must be punctual and regular in attendance: arrive on time and ready for the workday
  • Must be able to work with confidential items and understand the importance of confidentiality in project work
  • Must meet commitments and complete tasks satisfactorily
  • Must be able to work independently and stay focused under pressure
  • Must help accomplish specific tasks and improve the work process
  • Must be accurate and detail oriented with strong organizational skills required
  • Must be professional and courteous at all times
  • Must be able to work well with different work styles
  • Must be able to work efficiently and show initiative
  • Must be able to coordinate multiple tasks, projects, and assignments within appropriate timelines

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Ability to handle difficult situations involving participants with patience, good judgment, and with diplomacy is expected
  • Ability to work with a diverse group of people effectively and diplomatically
  • Must have strong English language skills and the ability to read, write and verbally communicate at a level appropriate to the duties of the position
  • Must possess excellent customer service skills, including written and oral communication
  • Proficient computer skills are required including Microsoft and Google applications
  • Ability to recruit, train, and supervise personnel
  • Ability to prioritize workload
  • Ability to manage information flow (including internal, external and customer communication and filing/documentation)
  • Ability to develop positive working relationships and work effectively with other employees/departments
  • Ability to demonstrate thoroughness, completeness, follow through on presentation and appearance of work
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare and present program materials in front of an audience

SCHEDULE & WORKING CONDITIONS

This is a part-time position. Typical work schedule to include 15-20 hours per week with a maximum weekly average of 25 hours. Employee schedules vary according to business needs. Must be able to work evenings and weekends based on program demands.

WORK ENVIRONMENT The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

General office environment with some time outdoors. Work is generally sedentary in nature, but may require standing and walking around campus or at sport facilities. The working environment is generally favorable. Lighting and temperature are adequate, and there are no hazardous or unpleasant conditions caused by noise, dust, etc. Work is generally performed within an office environment, with standard office equipment available or at outdoor sport facilities (e.g. tennis courts, track).

PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position may require the individual to spend many hours sitting and using office equipment and computers. This person will also spend time filing and have to do some lifting of supplies and materials from time to time, including banker boxes and files.

Physical requirements include but are not limited to: walking, walking over rough or uneven surfaces, bending, stooping, climbing, and working in confined space, lifting, pushing, pulling and carrying loads up to 50 pounds (unassisted) and 75 pounds (with assistance). Work may require standing and moving for extended periods.

RELATIONSHIPS

Inside the organization:

  • Reports to the Director of Adapted Athletics
  • Closely works with Internal Program Assistant
  • Assists in supervising the program coaches, volunteers, and interns
  • Further interactions may include other full-time and part-time staff within Aztec Recreation

Outside the organization:

  • School of Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
  • Student Disability Services
  • Adaptive Sports Board
  • SDSU Athletics
  • Health and Human Services Development
  • Student Affairs Development
  • Aztec Adaptive Sports and other Student Organization
  • Other adaptive sports organizations

EMPLOYMENT CATEGORY: Starting range $22-$25/hour

A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily before any candidate can be offered a position with Associated Students. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the application status of applicants or continued employment of current Associated Students employees who apply for the position.

Fingerprinting is required for all employee and volunteer positions that have direct contact with minor children and/or supervise other staff.

MVR and DMV record review is required for positions that drive university vehicles and/or passengers for program related trips.

title: Consulting Dietitian [Peterborough]
description:
This position offers 50 hours per month, with a flexible start date.

Be part of a collaborative team, passionate about senior nutrition and food service.

Seasons Care is hiring passionate Registered Dietitians to support the nutritional health and well-being of Seniors in Long-Term Care. With decades of experience in Long-Term Care, we work together every day to make meaningful differences in the lives of Residents across Canada. We believe in putting food and people first— for our Residents and our team.

When you join Seasons Care, you become part of a network of professionals who are passionate about leading with heart and evidence. You'll be joining a supportive environment where:

  • Your voice is heard and valued
  • Work-life balance is respected and prioritized
  • Professional development is encouraged
  • Teamwork and interdisciplinary collaboration are part of our everyday approach
  • We care — not just for Residents, but for one another

Your day is varied, structured, and rooted in collaboration. As an RD working in LTC, you will:

  • Manage daily clinical priorities, including referrals, weight monitoring, RAI assessments, and new Resident admissions
  • Collaborate closely with the Nutrition Manager and interdisciplinary Care Teams; participate in morning huddles where applicable
  • Review Resident charts and data (weights, intake, labs, medications, diagnoses, and health changes) to assess nutrition risk
  • Complete nutrition assessments, document findings, and follow up on care plans
  • Spend time in the dining room observing meals, engaging with Residents, and supporting consistent nutrition care with staff
  • Communicate with families and care teams; document and share nutrition updates and changes
  • Prepare for and participate in care conferences, PAC, CQI, and other Home‑based meetings
  • Occasionally support menu approvals, quality data collection, and organizational initiatives

This role provides a balanced blend of independent clinical practice, teamwork, and on‑site engagement across Homes.



Requirements

You are a dedicated, organized, and empathetic Registered Dietitian who brings clinical confidence and a Resident-first mindset to every Home you support. You thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy working independently, and value collaboration with interdisciplinary teams.

Whether you're counselling a Resident, mentoring dietary staff or reviewing a menu, you bring clarity, care and professionalism to everything you do.

  • Registered and in good standing with the College of Dietitians of Ontario
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities
  • Demonstrated problem-solving and critical thinking skills
  • A people-first approach with strong customer-service skills and a commitment to building respectful, trusting relationships
  • Proficiency with EMR systems and digital documentation
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively
  • Must provide proof of liability insurance, TB testing and vulnerable sector check
  • Travel may be required for certain positions

Seasons Care Dietitian Network is proud to accommodate individual needs in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA), within our recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any time throughout the recruitment process, please let us know.

Seasons Care is a diverse and inclusive network. We encourage applicants from First Nations, Metis and Inuit peoples, racialized persons and those who identify as LGBTQ+.

Join us in our mission to enhance lives through nutrition and quality care.

title: WFRP Claims Specialist
description:
As one of the leading writers of Federal Crop Insurance, AgriSompo North America combines industry experience, resources, capital and talent to deliver both traditional and innovative crop insurance and productivity tools to farmers, ranchers, insurers and agribusinesses in the United States. Our organization operates within a culture rooted in ethics, integrity and a belief that accountability, collaboration and agility are crucial to long-term success.

AgriSompo North America is a part of AgriSompo, Sompo International’s global agriculture platform. This platform is an integrated underwriting, technology and distribution platform delivering innovate insurance and reinsurance solutions to agriculture partners worldwide. Sompo International, AgriSompo’s parent company, is a global organization driven by its core values, a carrier that holds promise, trust and the commitment to protect. Through operating subsidiaries, Sompo International writes agriculture, casualty and other specialty, professional lines, property, marine/energy and aviation lines of insurance and catastrophe, property, casualty, professional lines and specialty lines of reinsurance.

As a leading provider of crop insurance and other agricultural risk management tools, we recognize that our success is derived directly from those whose contributions matter most: our people. AgriSompo North America has major offices in Lenexa, Kansas and Des Moines, Iowa as well as regional offices around the country. A shared commitment to integrity, accountability, collaboration and agility define our culture, and we strive to create exceptional value for our clients and shareholders and maintain AgriSompo North America as a desirable place to work.

Job Description

Are you looking for your next opportunity?

Sompo has a unique opportunity for a WFRP Claims Specialist in our West Region team.

As a Whole Farm Revenue Protection (WFRP) Claims Specialist will provide exceptional customer service to agents and producers by accurately and efficiently auditing and verifying WFRP Claims. You'll serve as an expert in areas of WFRP claims procedure and auditing. The WFRP Claims Specialist will also provide research and verification of claims/policy data, troubleshoot identified problems or issues, and train other staff as needed in the area of WFRP Claims.

Location: This position may be based remotely in Washington, California, Illinois, Texas, Florida, Kentucky, or Oregon, with consideration also given to candidates located in other U.S. state. We strive for collaboration which is why we offer a work environment where our employees thrive and develop long lasting careers.

Our business, your impact, our opportunity:

What you’ll be doing:

  • Audit, review, and process WFRP claims accurately and timely in accordance with policy requirements, standard operating procedures, and regulatory guidelines

  • Research and resolve complex claims, policy, and system issues, including PASS errors, with limited supervision

  • Serve as a resource on WFRP claims procedures, policy interpretation, and related underwriting and claims processes

  • Partner with underwriters, adjusters, compliance staff, agents, and producers to resolve questions and support effective claim handling

  • Apply working knowledge of WFRP, MPCI, FCIC, NCIS, RMA, and related manuals, handbooks, and policy documentation to support claim decisions

  • Support continuous improvement by identifying system issues, assisting with training development, and helping implement process enhancements

  • Maintain knowledge of regional crops, farming practices, and internal procedures to support strong claims performance

  • Adapt to changing priorities, systems, and business needs while maintaining strong research quality and timely execution.

  • Travel as needed, up to 25%

What you’ll bring:

  • Advanced experience in MPCI underwriting, claims auditing, and/or claims processing required

  • 5+ years of MPCI or WFRP crop insurance experience preferred

  • Advanced knowledge of FCIC MPCI and WFRP policies, with the ability to interpret policy provisions and supporting documentation

  • Knowledge of IRS federal tax forms, company policies and procedures, and related claims or underwriting systems preferred

  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe Acrobat

  • Strong analytical, mathematical, organizational, and problem-solving skills

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to work well across all levels inside and outside the organization

  • Strong customer service skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities independently and as part of a team

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality, adapt to change, and work effectively through complex issues

Physical Requirements & Work Conditions

  • Sedentary work. Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time.

  • Ability to stand or sit constantly/continuously.

  • Hearing. Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.

  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; extensive reading; visual inspection involving small defects, small parts, and/or operation of machines (including inspection); using measurement devices; and/or assembly or fabrication parts at distances close to the eyes.

Environmental Conditions

  • The work environment described here are meant to be representative of those an employee would normally encounter while performing the essential functions of this job.

  • The physical environment requires the employee to work inside where there are limited extremes to heat and/or cold; moderate noise; a normal office environment.

  • Travel required for meetings and trainings.

Salary Range: $70,000 - $90,000. Actual compensation for this role will depend on several factors including the cost of living associated with your work location, your qualifications, skills, competencies, and relevant experience.

At Sompo, we recognize that the talent, skills, and commitment of our employees drive our success. This is why we offer competitive, high-quality compensation and benefit programs to eligible employees.

Our compensation program is built on a foundation that promotes a pay-for-performance culture, resulting in higher incentive awards, on average, when the Company does well and lower incentive awards when the Company underperforms. title: Construction Scheduling Analyst
description:
Summary

The Construction Schedule Analyst is a foundational role within the Clark Planning & Scheduling Department. This position is designed for a detail-oriented individual who excels at data manipulation and logical problem-solving. You will support the Project Schedulers by managing the flow of data into Primavera P6, using Excel to audit schedule health, and creating reports that track project milestones.

This role is part of a structured career path in construction planning and scheduling. No prior construction experience is required; we provide technical training for Primavera P6 for candidates who demonstrate high-level analytical potential and a "quick-study" approach to new software.

Responsibilities

  • Commit to an accelerated learning path to become a power user in Primavera P6.

  • Work closely with Project Schedulers to explore the nuances of the Critical Path Method (CPM) and how it applies to complex construction sequencing.

  • On Site support of project teams to update schedules, expand activity detail, adjust construction sequencing, and produce internal and contractually required reporting.

  • Data Analysis and Advanced Reporting utilizing Primavera P6, Microsoft Excel, PowerBI and other industry specific tools.

  • Calculate and report on Project Metrics Total Float and Schedule Performance metrics to help the department identify potential bottlenecks.

  • Identify patterns in historical data to help Project Teams predict future project outcomes.

  • Quality Control: Ensure all schedule data adheres to standards for naming conventions, activity coding, and organizational breakdown.

Basic Qualifications

  • Undergraduate or Associates degree in construction management, engineering, data analysis, mathematics, computer science, business, finance, accounting, or a related field

  • Excel Proficiency

  • An innate interest in troubleshooting data discrepancies and finding the "why" behind the numbers.

  • Ability to summarize and communicate complex data findings

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Primavera P6

  • Results Oriented - Experience in using data to anticipate and solve problems, manage risk and analyze business needs to deliver high quality outcomes

  • Self Motivated - Takes initiative and personal responsibility to deliver value and excellence in all that you do

  • Team Player - Builds interpersonal relationships and collaborators with internal team members, trade partners, architects and clients.

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: Given that a good portion of your day will be spent at a desk, you should be comfortable with prolonged periods of focused work, whether it's collaborating with colleagues, analyzing data, or developing strategies. The role demands effective communication and sharp visual acuity for reviewing complex documents and performing detailed computer work. While there are times for quiet concentration, you'll also be expected to move actively throughout the office and travel occasionally to various locations, including dynamic construction sites, utilizing different modes of transportation. The ability to lift and move objects up to 10 pounds regularly, and up to 25 pounds on occasion (think a box of files or small office equipment), is also required.

Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines. Beyond regular working hours, there will be occasions where business needs require your attention, particularly for time-sensitive matters or emergencies. You are expected to monitor and respond to communications (phone calls, emails, text messages) as required to address these situations effectively. Your ability to manage these expectations and be responsive when critical issues arise is key to your success in this role and our collective success as a team.

A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment drug “fitness for duty” screening is required, and the company conducts random quarterly drug “fitness for duty” tests.

Clark offers a total compensation package that includes base salary, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision benefits, paid time off, retirement/401k, and Company Contribution plan. Additional benefits include life insurance, commuter benefit, short & long term disability, fitness reimbursement, FSA, tuition reimbursement, back-up daycare, tutoring & family support benefits, EAP/Work-Life assistance, and a holiday contribution program. For this role the base salary range is $77,500 - $85,000. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. Base pay is one part of the Total Compensation Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work. https://www.clarkconstruction.com/careers/clark-experience

title: Sr. Solutions Architect
description:
About Us

Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy:

  • Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.

Job Summary

The Sr Solutions Architect at SHI plays a critical leadership role in shaping and delivering enterprise-scale technology solutions focused around Cisco solutions. This role combines deep technical expertise, strategic thinking, and strong project leadership to design, implement, and govern secure, scalable, and high-performing architectures. As a trusted advisor, the Sr Solutions Architect bridges business objectives and technical execution, ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture, security standards, and modern technology frameworks, including cloud, data, AI, and Microsoft ecosystems. This individual partners closely with cross-functional teams, clients, and stakeholders to drive innovation and deliver business value at scale.

Role Description

(Including, but not limited to)

  • Partner with business leaders, product owners, and technical teams to architect end-to-end, enterprise-grade solutions aligned with strategic objectives.
  • Lead the development of Statements of Work (SOWs), architectural standards, reusable frameworks, and best practices to ensure consistent, high-quality delivery.
  • Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies, platforms, and integration patterns to support digital transformation and innovation initiatives.
  • Translate complex business requirements into scalable, secure, and maintainable technical solutions aligned with enterprise architecture principles.
  • Facilitate and lead solution design workshops, defining architecture, integrations, data flows, and system interactions.
  • Review and validate technical designs and implementation plans to ensure architectural integrity, performance, and scalability.
  • Collaborate with engineering, DevOps, and security teams to oversee solution delivery, enforce governance, and ensure adherence to standards.
  • Support pre-sales and client engagements by aligning solutions to customer needs, presenting architectural vision, and contributing to technical strategy.


Behaviors and Competencies

  • Adaptability: Demonstrates agility in dynamic environments, proactively anticipating change and adjusting strategies to address evolving business and technical needs.
  • Executive Communication: Effectively communicates complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, influencing decision-making at all levels.
  • Documentation & Governance: Produces and maintains high-quality architectural documentation, ensuring clarity, consistency, and adherence to standards.
  • Leadership: Leads by influence, mentoring teams, driving technical excellence, and fostering innovation across projects and initiatives.
  • Problem Solving: Anticipates risks, identifies root causes, and architects innovative, forward-thinking solutions to complex challenges.
  • Collaboration: Drives cross-functional alignment, enabling teams to work cohesively toward shared outcomes.
  • Self-Leadership: Demonstrates initiative, continuous learning, and a commitment to advancing both personal expertise and organizational capability.


Skill Level Requirements

  • Deep expertise in cisco architecture.
  • Strong experience designing microservices-based architectures, APIs, and containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Proven ability to architect solutions across enterprise systems, integration layers, and data platforms.
  • Advanced knowledge of cybersecurity principles, data privacy, and regulatory compliance frameworks.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, business-focused insights and recommendations.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automation tools, and infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform, ARM, CloudFormation).
  • Strong understanding of modern software development methodologies, including Agile and DevOps practices.
  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.


Other Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field required.
  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • 7+ years of experience in solutions architecture, system design, or senior-level technical roles within enterprise environments.
  • Industry-recognized certifications, in particular CCIE and any other vendors

title: Applications Analyst - Epic Willow (Salaried, Full time)
location: Washington Regional Med. Ctr. - Fayetteville, AR 72703
description:
Organization Overview, Mission, Vision, and Values

Our mission is to improve the health of people in the communities we serve through compassionate, high-quality care, prevention, and wellness education. Washington Regional Medical System is a community-owned, locally governed, non-profit health care system located in Northwest Arkansas in the heart of Fayetteville, which is consistently ranked among the Best Places to live in the country. Our 425-bed medical center has been named the #1 hospital in Arkansas for five consecutive years by U.S. News & World Report. We employ 3,200+ team members and serve the region with over 40 clinic locations, the region’s only Level II trauma center, and five Centers of Excellence - the Washington Regional J.B. Hunt Transport Services Neuroscience Institute; Washington Regional Walker Heart Institute; Washington Regional Women and Infants Center; Washington Regional Total Joint Center; and Washington Regional Pat Walker Center for Seniors.

Position Summary

The Applications Analyst – Epic Willow reports to the Assistant Manager, Epic Applications. This position is responsible for advanced support, troubleshooting, maintenance, design, build, testing, implementation, and optimization of Epic Willow and related pharmacy applications. The role partners with pharmacy leadership, pharmacists, physicians, nursing, clinical informatics, revenue cycle, supply chain, information services, and Epic/vendor stakeholders to support safe, efficient, compliant, and patient-centered medication management across inpatient and ambulatory settings. Key areas of responsibility include medication records and formularies, ordering and verification, dispensing, inventory, clinical decision support, charging, interfaces, pharmacy automation, medication administration dependencies, application reliability, and cross-application integration.

Essential Position Responsibilities

  • Maintain advanced knowledge of Epic Willow functionality, including medication records, formularies, order and verification workflows, dispensing, inventory, pharmacy queues, clinical decision support, charging, medication administration dependencies, application interfaces, pharmacy automation, and downstream impacts across the enterprise
  • Lead pharmacy, clinical, operational, revenue cycle, supply chain, internal information services, and Epic/vendor partners in developing Epic Willow enhancements, optimization initiatives, and workflow improvement projects
  • Oversee Epic Willow application design, build, configuration, maintenance, and validation to ensure functionality aligns with pharmacy operations, medication safety, clinical care, regulatory, revenue cycle, inventory, and end-user requirements
  • Perform complex analysis, build, implementation, and optimization of medication workflows supporting prescribing, verification, preparation, dispensing, administration, monitoring, charging, inventory management, and medication reconciliation
  • Configure and maintain medication records, formularies, NDC mappings, order questions, dispense logic, pharmacy queues, labels, clinical decision support, shortage substitutions, charging rules, and related pharmacy master files in accordance with approved governance and change-control processes
  • Meet regularly with pharmacy leaders, pharmacists, physicians, nursing, medication safety, clinical informatics, revenue cycle, supply chain, and operational teams to evaluate workflow concerns and identify opportunities to improve safety, efficiency, compliance, documentation integrity, and user experience
  • Lead coordinated testing for Epic Willow, including unit, regression, system, integrated, interface, pharmacy automation, medication ordering, verification, dispensing, administration, charging, inventory, reporting, and user acceptance testing
  • Serve as an application and workflow resource by translating medication management, pharmacy operational, clinical, regulatory, and business requirements into reliable system solutions
  • Coordinate Epic Willow interfaces and integrations with automated dispensing cabinets, dispensing and packaging systems, wholesaler and drug knowledge databases, barcode workflows, medication administration functionality, revenue cycle applications, and other connected systems
  • Provide mentorship for team members and assist with team member training, workflow education, and knowledge transfer, as needed
  • Ensure programs and services support applicable Joint Commission, CMS, controlled-substance, medication management, quality, Promoting Interoperability, and organizational governance requirements
  • Ensure the safeguarding of protected health information and appropriate access to medication and pharmacy data
  • Maintain accurate application documentation, build records, test scripts, workflow diagrams, issue resolutions, and support materials
  • Monitor help desk software for new tickets; troubleshoot complex pharmacy application issues; perform root-cause analysis; and document timely, sustainable resolutions
  • Lead Epic Willow projects, upgrades, enhancements, optimization efforts, go-live activities, testing, stabilization, and ongoing maintenance initiatives
  • Identify and lead opportunities to standardize and improve medication ordering, verification, dispensing, administration, inventory, charging, reporting, and pharmacy operational workflows through application optimization and process improvement
  • Adhere to all information services policies, procedures, application governance, change-management, and documentation standards
  • Participate in on-call support and lead incident response, medication-related issue resolution, and downtime procedures, as assigned

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or clinical license, preferred.
  • Licensure and Certifications: Epic Willow Inpatient and/or Epic Willow Ambulatory certification required. Additional Epic certification or proficiency in Willow Inventory, Beacon, Orders, Bridges, or related integrated applications preferred. Pharmacy licensure or certification is preferred when applicable to the candidate’s background.
  • Experience: Four to six years of clinical, pharmacy, operational, or healthcare applications experience as an applications analyst supporting multiple modules or applications, with direct experience in Epic build, testing, implementation, troubleshooting, and optimization strongly preferred. Experience supporting Epic Willow workflows is preferred, including medication records and formularies, order verification, dispensing, inventory, charging, clinical decision support, pharmacy automation, medication administration dependencies, interfaces, and reporting. Strong knowledge of medication-use processes, pharmacy operations, application dependencies, testing methodologies, integration workflows, change control, and coordination with pharmacy, clinical, revenue cycle, supply chain, technology, interface, data, reporting, and operational teams is required.

Work Environment: This position will spend 90% of time sitting while performing work in a standard office environment and 10% of time standing and/or walking while pushing, pulling, lifting, and/or carrying up to 50 lbs. This role is considered a remote position with onsite presence as needed.

The job description is not designed or intended to cover or set forth a comprehensive listing of all activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Washington Regional reserves the right in its absolute discretion to change duties, responsibilities or activities or assign new duties, responsibilities, or activities at any time with or without notice. Employees may be directed to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description.

Job Description:

The Parts Coordinator’s primary responsibility and accountability is to provide an exceptional and successful customer experience while proactively managing the process of ordering, receiving, storing, dispatching and returning parts for each repair order.   • Ensure consistent execution of WOW (Wow Operating Way) plan.

  • Order and receive supplemental Parts in the MIS, monitor performance of parts, materials and sublet vendors. Ensure daily reconciliation of the parts vendor invoice history report (e.g. 043 Report).

  • Ensure vendor invoices have the correct negotiated discount to maintain proper profit margins.

  • Frequently required to bend, crouch, reach, handle tools

Adhering to and enforcing all safety procedures.

Physical fitness, ability to walk, dance, stand, lift, or meet other physical demands.

Adaptability and strong organization and time management skills.

Excellent resource management, computer, record keeping, interpersonal, decision making, and verbal and written communication skills.

title: Table Mountain Facility (TMF) Maintenance & Operations Lead
description:
Job Details

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

The Facilities and Logistics Operations Division oversees the physical development, maintenance, and safe operation of the Laboratory’s infrastructure to enable advanced workplaces, resilient systems, and uninterrupted mission support. Within this division, the Facilities Operations Section, which assumes end-to-end ownership of the physical work environment and responsibility for the overall physical maintenance and safe operation of the Laboratory, is seeking a facilities Maintenance and Operations Engineer V to serve as the lead technical authority for the Table Mountain Facility (TMF).

Located near Wrightwood, California, in the Angeles National Forest, TMF is a premier, remote site facility operating under a permanent, non-expiring permit with the U.S. Forest Service (USFS). The site also maintains key multi-agency partnerships, including a specialized facility permit with the U.S. Air Force (USAF).

Based on-site at the Table Mountain Facility, the selected candidate will report to the Facilities Management Group Supervisor and step into a lead-level role responsible for the overall reliability, maintainability, compliance, and strategic oversight of TMF's complex infrastructure, ranging from remote power grids and industrial cooling arrays to standalone, self-sustained water loop operations. In this critical capacity, the selected candidate will not only ensure day-to-day operational excellence but will also direct the engineering strategy to support future site developments and the integration of new hosted facilities.

Tasks include but are not limited to:

  • Manage and oversee various facility and capital improvement projects from initial planning and cost estimation through design, procurement, construction, and closeout (including concrete pads, asphalt repair, facility roof replacements, and telescope pier/ray dome modifications).

  • Provide senior technical leadership and oversight for the facilities maintenance, operations, and subcontractors. Conduct quality inspections, identify work deficiencies, and ensure strict compliance with contractual performance standards.

  • Serve as the Contract Technical Manager (CTM) for the security/custodial subcontract. Partner closely with the Subcontracts Manager (SCM) to jointly direct contract execution, oversee vendor performance, and maintain productive relationships with subcontractor personnel to meet all operational objectives.

  • Serve as the primary on-site coordinator and facilities engineering point of contact for external subcontractors and collaborators, utility providers, USFS/forest service rangers, USAF/military point-of-contacts, and internal technical stakeholders. Interface with various organizations internally including Acquisition, Contracts Management, Engineering & Science Directorate technical staff as well as JPL’s Real Property Administrator and the NASA Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO) for permits/permit mandates and lease agreements to ensure alignment with operational requirements.

  • Develop, prioritize, and manage preventive and corrective maintenance schedules that seamlessly accommodate active scientific operations, minimizing disruptions to telescopes, lasers, and optical communication ground stations (such as the O2O optical terminal).

  • Oversee the procurement and technical tracking of facility materials, maintenance supplies, replacement parts, and specialized equipment.

  • Ensure all site operations, civil alterations, and maintenance adhere to NASA, JPL, OSHA, fire/life safety, and environmental regulations, including hazardous waste handling, environmental stewardship, and sustainability initiatives.

  • Act as the technical authority for the end-to-end reliability and safe operation of complex, remote-site infrastructure, including high-voltage/3-phase electrical distribution, critical surge mitigation systems, industrial glycol chillers, and standalone water/pump utilities.

  • Ensure the proper routine operation and maintenance of site roads, parking areas, drainage systems, and perimeter civil infrastructure.

  • Drive emergency preparedness planning, continuity of operations, wildfire mitigation, severe weather (heavy mountain snow/wind) response, and rapid disaster recovery activities. Provide after-hours support and coordinate immediate responses to critical system failures.

  • Coordinate and track employee and subcontractor safety training, industrial equipment certifications, and operational qualifications required for remote-site work.

  • Manage site fleet operations, fuel storage and distribution systems, regular equipment inspections, and preventive maintenance for all facility vehicles and heavy equipment.

  • Ensure the integrity of the facility's perimeter fencing, automated main gates, badge reader infrastructure, and facility security camera networks.

  • Conduct routine facility condition assessments to identify infrastructure renewal and deferred maintenance priorities, driving long-term capital planning, budgeting, and cost control. Utilize CMMS platforms to maintain precise asset inventories, operating procedures, permits, and maintenance records.

  • Lead continuous process-improvement initiatives focused on operational reliability, efficiency, customer service, cost reduction, and the elimination of redundant or low-value operational tasks.

Required Qualifications:

  • Typically requires a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a similar related discipline with a minimum of 12 years of related experience; OR Master’s degree with a minimum of 10 years of related experience; OR PhD with a minimum of 8 years of related experience.

  • Proven experience managing facilities or engineering operations in remote, high-altitude, mountain, or environmentally challenging locations subject to severe winter weather and wildfire risks.

  • Demonstrated project management experience leading complex infrastructure upgrades, facility renovations, or technical engineering projects from inception through completion.

  • Demonstrated success supporting 24/7 operational environments where facility downtime directly impacts scientific, aerospace, optical, or astronomical research operations.

  • Strong technical familiarity with heavy infrastructure systems, specifically industrial cooling (glycol chillers), complex electrical distribution, automated transfer switches, and standalone water infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a federal government, aerospace facility, or high-security laboratory setting.

  • Expertise in electrical arc flash hazard analysis and mitigation.

  • Working knowledge of CMMS platforms such as MAXIMO or Meridian.

  • Experience using Bluebeam Software as a review and documentation tool.

Work location: Table Mountain Facility (TMF). Wrightwood, CA.

Note: The nature of this work may require occasional non-standard hours to meet critical project deadlines and support operational requirements.

title: Graduate - Supply, trading & shipping - China (Aug 2027)
description:
Entity:

Job Family Group:

Job Description:

bp supply, trading & shipping graduate programme – China (Aug 2027)

About bp

As a leading global energy company with a presence in 61 countries, bp’s purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. We are one of only a few companies that can deliver energy – at scale – to countries and millions of customers every day. With more than 100 years of experience, we bring together technology, innovation and deep expertise that keeps communities moving, – and we’re still evolving.

About early careers

Early careers opportunities

Your talent. Your skills. Your big ideas (and even bigger dreams). We know you have a lot to give. So we’ll make sure you get a lot in return. From next-level experiences to global impact. From inspiring teammates to exceptional support, – we offer graduate and internship roles across multiple areas.

Our supply, trading & shipping graduate programme

Fast-moving. High impact. Full of possibility. In supply, trading & shipping (ST&S), every decision matters, – and you’ll be making them sooner than you think.

Why work in ST&S at bp?

  • Play a role in powering economies worldwide.

  • Work in a fast-paced environment where every second counts.

  • Build future-proof skills that open up many different career paths.

  • Learn from experienced teams who’ll help you grow your commercial confidence.

As an ST&S graduate, you’ll complete three rotations designed to give you breadth of experience across your chosen business area while also supporting you to build technical depth. From analysing data to influencing decision making, to building customer relationships and shaping deals, – this programme gives you the exposure and experience to start building a future in commercial business.

Join us and you’ll get the support of a structured technical pathway and our training programme, helping you grow both professionally and personally. In return, you'll bring your ideas, curiosity and ambition to real business challenges. Along the way, you'll be part of a supportive bp early careers community that will help you grow, succeed and make a meaningful impact from day one.

We’re recruiting for graduates to join us on the Commercial track for an August 2027 start.

Commercial development track: Every year, bp invests billions of dollars searching for new sources of energy, supplying our customers with the fuels they need. You’ll help to ensure we make the best use of our investment. We want you to be in the best position to propose new and creative ways to maximize value. The commercial development track will help you to develop strong commercial acumen which is supported by the different rotations you will undertake. You may find yourself placed in a team that sets strategy, tracks the market, or manages foreign exchange, or you may be a trading operator responsible for the logistical success of a trading deal. Other rotations include marketing & origination, structured products and chartering.

No matter where you work, all the roles will offer a challenging experience that gives you first-hand exposure to our supply, trading & shipping activities and will contribute to building your long-term career in the organisation.

About you ​


As a bp graduate, you will have an interest and/or skill in delivering economic value back to a business, identifying solutions and strategies resulting in cost savings and a natural negotiation style. No matter where you work at bp, you’ll be valued, included and respected. We’ll provide you with on-going support and we’ll reward you for the great work you do.

In a global energy market defined by rapid shifts, complexity, and uncertainty, we value people with commercial hunger and sound judgment, not just technical perfection.

Our traders and commercial teams operate across global desks in London, the US, and Asia, engaging customers across Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Malaysia, Vietnam, and beyond. As a result, the ability to connect with people across cultures, build trust, and communicate clearly in global teams is foundational.

Equally important is initiative and intellectual curiosity. Markets do not come with instruction manuals. We look for individuals who actively try to understand what is moving prices, who form hypotheses, and who develop the instinct to sense where opportunity may emerge before it is obvious.

A trading environment also requires the confidence to take risk, paired with accountability and discipline. Decisions are often made under time pressure and imperfect information, and resilience matters. We do not optimise for blemish‑less CVs. Some of our strongest performers are those who have faced setbacks, learned from failure, and demonstrated the grit to push forward with even greater determination.

To be eligible for the ST&S graduate programme you should:

  • be currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in any discipline which could range from Business, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Arts to STEM

  • be in your final year of study, graduating by July 2027 or recently graduated

  • on track to achieve a cumulative GPA equivalent to Second Upper Honours or above

Please note the following when applying:

  • You can only apply to 1 bp early careers opportunity globally per academic year. Within this time, we will only process the first application you make, and you’ll be withdrawn from any subsequent applications.

  • Please note that vacancies are filled on an ongoing basis after opening and we may close applications before any stated deadline. Therefore, we highly recommend you submit your application as early as possible to be considered for the opportunity of your choice.

Applications close on 16 October 2026.


Travel Requirement

Some travel may be required with this role, this is negotiable

This role is not eligible for relocation

This position is not available for remote working

Agility core practices, Analytical Thinking, Computational Thinking, Continuous Learning, Data Analysis, Data cleansing and transformation, Data Management, Data Sourcing, Data visualization and interpretation, Dialogue enablement, Exposure Management, Machine Learning (ML), Macroeconomics, Market analysis methods, Market Risk Management, Sentiment and Trends, Statistics, Trade execution and management, Trading Fundamentals, Trading knowledge

.

description:

Support bringing the right people in the right place.

By creating desirable solutions and great experiences that enrich people’s daily lives and the health of our planet, we want to be a driving force in delivering enjoyable and sustainable living. Responsibilities for this role include collaborating with all departments within the facility, the Electrolux RDC Advocate Team, Electrolux Sourced Deployment Team, International Transportation Team and Ryder Load Planners. This individual will also be responsible for the effective use of WMS for the generating of pick-lists, put away lists, load sheets and outbound BOLs.

Your main tasks:

  • Work in tandem with various departments and maintain flexible attitude supporting all the work that helps achieving organizational goals.

  • Coordinates unloading and loading of inbound/outbound shipments, orderly stacking of product and picking/staging of outbound shipments in accordance with EMS expectations (safety, quality and delivery).

  • ·Direct efficient operation of the department and ensure procedures are documented and followed.

  • Identify damaged and defective products and partner with the Warehouse Supervisor to ensure that it is accounted for and has proper resolution.
  • Make recommendations to the Warehouse Supervisor on programs to improve warehouse operations focusing on Continuous Improvement and Quality initiatives.
  • Assist with monitoring daily KPI’s, Quality Metrics and Productivity administration is completed accurately and on time.
  • Observe and identify performance behaviors and coach operators based on Electrolux expectations.

Education & Experience:

  • High school graduate or equivalent
  • 5-7 years’ experience of Shipping / Receiving Office Clerk responsibilities
  • Operational experience is preferred
  • Understanding of SAP
  • Experience working with variety of WMS Excellent written and verbal communication skills required
  • Ability to multi-task under pressure independently and as part of the team
  • Strong work ethic with a focus on results
  • Strong attention to detail, with excellent follow-up skills
  • Creative problem solver, ready to take ownership of assigned duties in a timely manner
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft Excel
  • Knowledge of ERP/MRP, Warehouse management systems, SAP, etc.
  • Flexibility to work standard shifts as well as extended business hours depending on customer needs

Physical Demands:

  • Regularly sitting on a powered industrial truck.
  • Lift up to 50 + pounds and adjust body position to bend, stoop, stand, walk, turn, pivot, and stand for long periods of time.
  • Having a good sense of balance and good eye-hand-foot coordination.
  • Ability to assess weights and judge distances and heights.
  • Ability to work in varying temperatures, depending upon season.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, and ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

description:
Job Description

Veracruz

Nivel de Estudios

Licenciatura en Finanzas, Contabilidad, Administración, Ingeniería Industrial o afín.

5+ años de experiencia en costos de manufactura, análisis financiero de cervecería, FP&A industrial o control presupuestal operativo.

Mínimo 3 años en costos de manufactura, servicios de manufactura, mantenimiento, FP&A industrial o análisis operativo-financiero.

Experiencia Requerida

Experiencia en análisis de costo de conversión, mantenimiento, servicios de manufactura, producción, eficiencia operativa o
entornos industriales complejos.
Capacidad para construir modelos predictivos, escenarios presupuestales y análisis de sensibilidad.
Conocimiento deseable de OEE, energía, agua, vapor, CO2, mantenimiento, SAP/ERP y estructuras de centros de costo.

Inglés intermedio-avanzado deseable: lectura, escritura y comunicación de resultados.

Habilidades

Excel avanzado; Power BI deseable; PowerPoint ejecutivo; SAP/ERP deseable; manejo de bases de datos y análisis de drivers.

Resumen

Pensamiento analítico profundo; curiosidad financiera; capacidad de anticipación; comunicación clara; disciplina de seguimiento; colaboración con operación.

Responsabilidades

1. Gestionar el desempeño financiero de los costos de conversión de la cervecería, incluyendo Elaboración y Envasado como asignaciones primarias, así como EHS, Capacitación y demás funciones de soporte asociadas, identificando desviaciones, explicando sus principales drivers y cuantificando impactos contra AOP, LE y resultados reales.

2. Monitorear incidencias operativas que puedan afectar el presupuesto, incluyendo consumos de servicios de manufactura, eventos de mantenimiento, backlog, paros, capacitación operativa, iniciativas EHS y cambios en condiciones de operación.

3. Construir proyecciones financieras y escenarios base/riesgo/oportunidad con enfoque predictivo, anticipando impactos futuros antes de que se materialicen en el resultado mensual.

4. Supervisar y evaluar el desempeño financiero de los procesos de Elaboración y Envasado, monitoreando los principales indicadores operativos y productivos —incluyendo productividad, OEE, rendimiento, mermas, sobrellenado, consumo de materiales y utilización de recursos— identificando riesgos y oportunidades con impacto en el costo de conversión de la cervecería.

5. Traducir KPIs operativos como OEE, paros, eficiencia energética, mantenimiento correctivo/preventivo y utilización de recursos en impacto monetario, costo unitario y riesgo presupuestal.

6. Desarrollar análisis cuantificables que permitan separar variaciones por volumen, eficiencia, precio, consumo, mix, temporalidad, eventos no recurrentes y causas estructurales.

7. Preparar inputs ejecutivos para el Coordinador de Finanzas Operativas, asegurando que cada análisis incluya mensaje, causa raíz, impacto, riesgo/oportunidad y acción recomendada.

8. Participar y desarrollar los procesos de AOP, LE1 y LE2 generando bases, supuestos, validaciones y escenarios para los rubros asignados.

9. Identificar oportunidades de eficiencia en servicios de manufactura, mantenimiento y procesos de soporte operativo, validando su factibilidad con áreas responsables y cuantificando el beneficio esperado.

10. Mantener rutinas de seguimiento con áreas operativas para revisar variaciones, actualizar supuestos, validar riesgos y asegurar acciones correctivas. 11. Asegurar calidad, integridad y trazabilidad de la información financiera utilizada en los análisis de conversión.

12. Asegurar, dentro de su ámbito de responsabilidad, el cumplimiento de los objetivos de costo por caja definidos por la organización, mediante la identificación temprana de riesgos, la captura de oportunidades de mejora y la generación de análisis que soporten una agenda de ahorros alcanzable, sostenible y alineada a las prioridades estratégicas de la cervecería.

Job Description

Location:
Enid Community Corrections Center

This is an on-site position and is not eligible for remote work.

Basic Purpose:

Positions in this job family are assigned responsibilities involving offender records management and auditing operations at a department facility, probation and parole district office, or Sentence Administration unit to ensure that all offenders remanded to the custody of the Department of Corrections are confined in accordance with the order of the sentencing court and Oklahoma State Statutes.

Typical Functions:

  • Maintains a consolidated record card, legal file and computer record system for offenders which includes time served, sequence of sentences, all credits earned, granted or lost, jail time, warrants outstanding, detainers, misconduct reports, offender movement histories, job assignments and other related information; calculates time served and credits earned and distributes a monthly report of such to offenders; monitors discharges and rebills of sentences to be consecutively served, through projected release dates; audits offender files to ensure proper file contents and accuracy of time calculation records.

  • Reviews and handles all legal mail dealing with certified judgment and sentences, jail time statements, detainers, and court sentence modifications; processes all offender transfers, receptions, discharges, paroles and sentence rebills which occur at the facility or district; monitors and reports the daily inmate count.

  • Contacts law enforcement agencies, court officials, private attorneys, state and federal agencies, offenders and their families, all levels of department staff, and the inquiring general public concerning information such as offender locations, judgment and sentences, jail time, credits, current release dates, misconduct reports, count issues, paroles and other related information.

  • Prepares extradition paperwork; processes and monitors Interstate Agreement of Detainers paperwork; and testifies in court regarding records related matters.

  • Provides supervision to clerical support staff in the physical maintenance of offender field files, the filing of escape charges, the chairing of offender misconduct hearings, the monitoring of the parole process and/or the closing and transferring of files to another location or to closed offender records.

  • Within the Sentence Administration Unit, performs audits of offender time credits to ensure proper release dates with authority to correct discrepancies. Reviews the offender file to ensure that documentation is filed in the proper sequence and section, and that the offender photo is up to date and of good quality. Provides records management training to various departmental and private prison personnel.

Level Descriptor:

The Correctional Records Officer job family consists of only one level and incumbents are responsible for performing all functions related to the position.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Competencies:

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities required include knowledge of policies, procedures and laws which govern the administration of court-ordered sentences and the records which must be maintained to document the enforcement of those sentences; of mathematical computations; and of the general operations of the criminal justice system including corrections.

Ability is required to gather and organize information and data from other documented sources; to conduct several tasks simultaneously; to read and comprehend policies and procedures, manuals, statutes, rules and regulations; to communicate decisions; and to establish and maintain effective working relationships with others.

Education and Experience:

Education and Experience requirements consist of a bachelor’s degree and one year of professional or technical administrative* experience in business or public administration

or in correctional records management or social casework which involved the classification and assignment or field supervision of offenders;

or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

*Technical administrative experience would include highly complex clerical work, which was gained under the direct supervision of a professional supervisor or manager.

title: Analista Senior, Operación
description:
Job Description

Veracruz

Nivel de Estudios

Licenciatura en Finanzas, Contabilidad, Administración, Ingeniería Industrial, Supply Chain o afín.

5+ años de experiencia en análisis financiero, costos de manufactura, gastos operativos, inventarios, logística o FP&A industrial.

Experiencia Requerida

Experiencia deseable en costos indirectos, materiales, Logística Inversa/METS, inventarios, servicios administrativos, IT o procurement.

Capacidad para traducir variables operativas en impacto financiero cuantificable. Conocimiento deseable de SAP/ERP, estructuras de centros de costo, cuentas contables, inventarios, contratos y modelos de costo unitario.

Mínimo 3 años en costos indirectos, gastos operativos, inventarios, logística, supply chain finance o FP&A industrial.

Habilidades

Pensamiento crítico; sensibilidad financiera; enfoque a detalle; orientación a negocio; colaboración transversal; capacidad para encontrar costos ocultos y estructurar oportunidades.

Excel avanzado; Power BI deseable; PowerPoint ejecutivo; SAP/ERP deseable; análisis de bases de datos, inventarios y costos unitarios.

Resumen

Administrar, proyectar y anticipar el comportamiento financiero de los costos operativos indirectos de manufactura, integrando las categorías de Administración, IT, Logística Inversa/METS y Materiales Indirectos, mediante escenarios financieros, estrategias de optimización e identificación de costos ocultos, riesgos y oportunidades que impacten el costo total de la cervecería, así como riesgos asociados a eventos de No Calidad y obsolescencia de Producto Terminado Asignaciones primarias: Administración, IT, Logística Inversa/METS, Materiales Indirectos y costos de No Calidad. Asignaciones complementarias: inventarios, contratos de servicios, logística de soporte y categorías operativas indirectas.

Responsabilidades

1. Gestionar el desempeño financiero de las áreas administrativas y de soporte de la cervecería, incluyendo Administración, IT, Materiales Indirectos, Logística Inversa/METS y demás costos asociados, identificando desviaciones, explicando sus principales drivers y cuantificando impactos contra AOP, LE y resultados actuales.

2. Actuar como socio financiero de las áreas administrativas y funcionales bajo su responsabilidad, proporcionando visibilidad oportuna sobre riesgos, oportunidades y requerimientos presupuestales, así como recomendaciones para optimizar la utilización de recursos.

3. Supervisar la gestión financiera de los programas asociados a Logística Inversa/METS (marcos, entrepaños y tarimas), incluyendo análisis de rotación, utilización de activos, pérdidas, daños, costos logísticos, eficiencia operativa e impactos en capital de trabajo, identificando oportunidades de optimización y captura de valor para la cervecería.

4. Analizar el comportamiento de los materiales indirectos y consumibles operativos, evaluando tendencias de consumo, precio, eficiencia y utilización, identificando riesgos de sobreconsumo, oportunidades de ahorro y mejoras en la gestión de inventarios.

5. Evaluar los principales indicadores financieros y operativos relacionados con los rubros bajo su responsabilidad, asegurando la correcta interpretación de tendencias, identificando desviaciones relevantes y proponiendo acciones para mejorar el desempeño económico de la cervecería.

6. Desarrollar modelos financieros, escenarios estratégicos y análisis predictivos que permitan anticipar impactos económicos derivados de cambios en niveles de actividad, utilización de activos, consumo de recursos, contratos de servicios o variaciones en costos operativos.

7. Administrar el seguimiento financiero de eventos de No Calidad y riesgos de obsolescencia de Producto Terminado, asegurando la construcción y mantenimiento de bases de información confiables que permitan cuantificar impactos económicos, identificar tendencias, anticipar riesgos y soportar acciones preventivas orientadas a la protección del resultado financiero de la cervecería.

8. Identificar, cuantificar y dar seguimiento a iniciativas de productividad, eficiencia y optimización de costos en las áreas bajo su responsabilidad, asegurando la adecuada documentación y validación financiera de los beneficios generados.

9. Participar activamente y desarrollar los procesos de AOP, LE1 y LE2, estableciendo las bases financieras, escenarios y supuestos requeridos para las categorías operativas asignadas, garantizando consistencia metodológica y trazabilidad de la información.

10. Preparar análisis ejecutivos y recomendaciones que faciliten la toma de decisiones, transformando datos financieros y operativos en información clara, accionable y orientada a la generación de valor para la cervecería.

11. Asegurar, dentro de su ámbito de responsabilidad, el cumplimiento de los objetivos de costo por caja definidos por la organización, mediante la identificación temprana de riesgos, la captura de oportunidades de mejora y la generación de análisis que soporten una agenda de ahorros alcanzable, sostenible y alineada a las prioridades estratégicas de la cervecería.
